  - **The contract** (shared with the challenge characters' block, which
    adds its own entries): the element holding a live drawing gets
    `char-special` for `CHAR_SPECIAL_MS[id] || CHAR_SPECIAL_MS[kind] ||
    CHAR_SPECIAL_DEFAULT_MS` (2800), then loses it. Parts that exist only
    for the special are `cx-sp` + their own class, drawn with
    `opacity="0"` - a still drawing, a board row, a silhouette and a
    flip-book recording never show them. They move only under
    `.char-special`; every animation is finite (check-loops ignores
    them). The table is a `const` before `drawAvatarCharSVG`, keyed by id
    first because the three ultimates share the `zenith` kind.
  - **How this block draws them:** `CHAR_SPECIAL_DRAW[id](T)` runs from
    `done()` (via `charSpecialParts`) once the figure is closed; `T.back`
    sits behind the figure, `T.front` over everything. Each moving piece
    carries its own animation in an inline `--a` (plus its numbers as
    custom properties: `--dx`, `--rs` ...), and ONE rule,
    `.char-special .avatarchar-svg .cx-spa{ animation:var(--a) }`, runs
    them - so nothing moves without the class. The keyframes are the
    shared `sp-*` set beside it. An orbit is two nested pendulums with a
    front copy and a behind copy that hand over (`spOrbit`). Fills,
    transforms and opacity only; no filter.
  - **The scheduler** (`playCharSpecial(el)`, `charSpecialTick`): only a
    PROMINENT character - `.profile-hero-avatar`, `.person-card-art`,
    `.cz-pick-character`, `.results-level-avatar`
    (`CHAR_SPECIAL_PROMINENT`), never a board row, the race line or the
    tab bar. First one no sooner than 8-16s after it is on screen, then
    every 12-30s (`charSpecialTiming`, which a gate may shorten), one at a
    time app-wide, nothing while the page is hidden (the clocks move on by
    the time away), nothing under Reduce motion. A flip-book steps aside
    for it: `.char-special` hides `.char-flip-play`, shows the drawing
    under it and adds `char-live` for the length of the special so the
    idle runs too (`data-sp-live` says it was added, and it comes off
    again). `setCharState` clears all of it. It also plays 0.5s after a
    rank-up scene hands back to Profile (`rankUpSceneEnd(scene, true)`)
    and 2.6s after a 100 lands on the results character.
  - **The thirteen, escalating within each group:**
    - Lunar (Silver): silver motes gather in its hands into a crescent
      cradling a star, which lifts away.
    - Solar (Gold): gold gathers into a small sun with a turning corona,
      which lets go a ring of light and a burst of sparks.
    - Tempest (Platinum): its teal flare circles it twice like a storm
      front, comes to its hands and cracks out as lightning.
    - Frost (Sapphire): a comet streaks past behind it, a second comes in
      low and lands in its hands, blooms into a snowflake and shatters.
    - Oracle (Amethyst): a ring of runes turns round it while light
      spirals into its hands as a turning galaxy that flings out.
    - Inferno (Supernova): embers rush in, a star forms, burns white,
      shudders as it collapses and goes off - frame-wide flash,
      shockwaves, rays, sparks.
    - Umbra: the light goes out and only its Penumbra flare is left,
      flickering like a failing lamp until it catches and pulses twice.
    - Horizon: its flare slips the brow, leaving a black hole there,
      circles it with a tail and is pulled back in through a closing
      event horizon.
    - Genesis: the Worldheart rises out of its chest, laps the planet
      twice like a moon (in front and behind) and dives in - the planet
      flashes rose.
    - Void (the coolest secret): the lights go out, its three flares tear
      loose into an accretion disc, spiral back into its face and go off
      in white.
    - Astral: the plasma core overloads - rings thrown off it, arcs
      cracking over the body, a cyan discharge.
    - Celestial: meteors behind it, the crown's seven stars rise into a
      ring round its head and draw their constellation, then fold back
      in starlight.
    - Zenith (the most): a corona opens and turns behind it, the comet
      laps its shoulders, rings ring out, stardust falls and the whole
      frame goes to light.

    nothing while hidden; nothing under Reduce motion. It fails on
    57212ce. **Cost, measured:** the parts are in every copy of those
    thirteen drawings (30-60% more nodes for each, e.g. Zenith 224 ->
    336), all at opacity 0 and none animated outside a special.
  - **Videos are recorded by seeking, not in real time:** every animation
    paused and its `currentTime` set per frame (a special's animations
    offset from when its class went on), so a loaded machine gives the
    same frames as a quiet one. The 100% hundo trigger is not covered by
    the gate.
- **HOME'S RINGS HAVE TWO TIERS: ORANGE, THEN THE SIX FLARES, AND THEY DRAW ON (build 317).** *"I
  noticed that the orange glowing rings light up when you hit max rank.
  Let's do it so that that happens once every one of flares and secret
  flares are lit up. OR make it where the rank one is all orange but if
  you get all the secret flares AND the rank ones, then it's like black?
  Could be sick but idk."* The second option, as two tiers, decided in
  `homeRingTier()` and nowhere else:
  - `""` - plain rings.
  - `"supernova"` - `store.supernovaAchieved` (every rank flare lit; set
    when the Supernova cutscene finishes). The orange
    `.cosmic-orbit-ring-supernova`, unchanged.
  - `"eclipse"` - that AND `secretFlaresAllFound()`, which is every key
    of `MYSTERY_ORDER` in `store.mysteryColorsFound` (all SIX). Not
    `mysteryAllFound()`: that one means the three Void flares and has
    since build 302. `.cosmic-orbit-ring-eclipse` and NOT the orange
    class. Every secret flare without Supernova is plain - tier two
    needs both. The key is still `"eclipse"` whatever it looks like.
  - **THE TOP TIER IS BUILT EXACTLY LIKE THE ORANGE, AND ONLY ITS COLOUR
    IS ITS OWN.** Round three, after *"I don't like the black rings on the
    main menu, they don't look like the other orange, they are thicker,
    they just look different.. maybe black isn't the move but I figured
    black would be sick."* What was wrong, measured: the orange is ONE
    circle a ring, stroke-width 1.4, paint at .55 alpha, opacity 1,
    `filter:drop-shadow(0 0 3px)` at .5. The black was SEVEN circles a
    ring - a 5.2-wide near-black body, a 13-wide shadow, three corona
    strokes (6, 3.4, 3) and two rims (.85, 1.15) - a band about 13 units
    across, with no glow at all. Two rounds of making a dark ring
    readable on a dark sky had each added light and width round it, so
    it stopped being the same object as the orange. Now both styles are
    one circle with those exact numbers; the gate compares them property
    by property.
  - **`RING_ECLIPSE_STYLE` picks the colour** (a `let` beside
    `homeRingTier()`, only so the gate can draw every one). **Since
    planet2 the default is `"black"`** - see "PLANET2" below; `"flares"`
    and `"white"` are one line away.
    - `"flares"` (the default until planet2) - the six secret flares' own colours
      (`MYSTERY_COLOR`) round the ring. SVG has no conic gradient, so
      `ringFlaresURL()` draws one once onto a canvas (in hue order -
      red, orange, yellow, ice blue, violet, pink - blended in OKLab so
      no join goes muddy, the .55 baked into every pixel's alpha) and the
      stroke is a `<pattern>` carrying it. The whole ring layer turns
      once every 96s (`cosmic-orbit-spin`, a full turn, so the loop is
      seamless; on the shared loop clock; off under Reduce motion).
      Turning a circle about its own centre moves the colours and not
      the stroke.
    - **Round four: "the flares ring reads paler and weaker than the
      orange ... lavender/white with faint colour."** Three causes, all
      fixed without touching the stroke or the .55: the swatches are
      bubble colours, and the ice blue and violet in particular wash out
      as a 1.4-wide line at .55 on a dark sky, so each colour's chroma is
      raised (`RING_FLARE_CHROMA`, 1.6 for those two, 1.3 for the warm
      four, which would clip into red any higher) and its lightness held
      at `RING_FLARE_LIGHT` (.7, about the orange's own); each colour
      HOLDS for half its sixth of the ring before blending, so it reads
      as six colours rather than one long blend; and the glow was a
      single pearl drop-shadow, which whitened everything. **A
      drop-shadow is one colour however many the ring has**, so the
      flares ring's glow is the orange's drop-shadow written out
      longhand: the same two rings again in `.cosmic-ring-glowsvg`,
      blurred by exactly the drop-shadow's 3px (a standard deviation of
      1.5 user units, i.e. `calc(1.5 * 100cqw / 360)` on the hero's
      container) at its .5. The blur sits on an HTML-level svg rather
      than on SVG elements, so iOS draws it. Measured: every flare's
      centre has a chroma (max - min channel) of 189-255 against the
      orange's 168.
    - `"black"` - **the default since planet2, rebuilt**: true black
      (`RING_BLACK`, opaque), the orange's one 1.4-wide circle, edged by
      a thin cool rim (`.cosmic-ring-glowsvg.is-rim`); no drop-shadow, no
      ember corona. It was a near-black at .55 with an ember drop-shadow,
      which is a darker patch of sky with a brown halo. See "PLANET2".
    - `"white"` - the same circle in white at .8 (`RING_WHITE`), its rim
      the orange's own glow (1.4 wide, blurred 1.5 units, at .5) in white.
  - **The top tier's rings sit in a layer of their own**
    (`.cosmic-hero-ringlayer`), placed UNDER the main svg - where the
    orange paints, first in that svg - so the sweep is a compositor
    transform and never repaints the sphere's turbulence filters. No SVG
    filter anywhere (those break on real iOS); the drop-shadow is the
    same CSS filter the orange has always used.
  - **THE RING DRAW (round four).** *"I do like how there's a small
    cutscene within the main menu when the rings get colored."* There was
    none - the rings simply changed when Home was next built - so
    `playRingDraw()` is it. The first time THIS DEVICE shows a ring tier
    above the last one it showed (none -> orange, orange -> flares,
    none -> flares), Home opens with the rings as they were and the new
    colour draws on round each ring from the top, the outer first and
    the inner 200ms behind (1.4s each), with a soft glint at the head;
    the old rings fade under it and the real new rings (with their glow)
    fade up as it hands over.
    - `showHome()` asks `ringDrawPlan()` before building the hero and
      hands the old tier over in `ringDrawFrom`, which only that one
      build reads. That build puts the new rings in a hidden ring layer
      (`.is-drawing`, even for the orange, which otherwise lives in the
      main svg) and adds `.cosmic-hero-ringold` and
      `.cosmic-hero-ringdraw`. Their classes are deliberately NOT
      `.cosmic-orbit-ring`, so everything that counts rings still counts
      two.
    - The last tier shown is `class26e.ringtier.seen`, viewing history
      like `class26e.daily.seen`: not on `store`, so it does not sync and
      a second device gets its own moment. Missing counts as no tier, so
      a device already at a tier when this shipped plays it once. It is
      written when the draw STARTS, so leaving Home before then means the
      next Home plays it. A drop (a reset) or Reduce motion records the
      new tier and draws nothing.
    - It holds nothing up and nothing waits for it. It waits: no tour,
      loading screen, cutscene, reward card, scene bridge or What's New
      may be up (`ringDrawHeld`, the badge cutscenes' rule), reward
      cards still owed on this Home go first for up to
      `RING_DRAW_CARD_WAIT_MS`, and the page has to be visible.
    - Compositor-friendly: the old rings and the new rings (glow and
      all) are still layers that only fade; what moves is one
      filter-free svg - two dashed strokes and two glints - for 1.6s.
      The handover and the tidy-up are read off the animations, not the
      clock, so a slow or seeked page cannot pull the layers out early.
      The flares rings keep turning while hidden, so the drawn copy is
      set to the angle they will be at when it hands over.
    - **Recording it frame-stepped needs one correction**: the draw's
      animations are created 600ms (real time) after Home mounts, which
      is many frames late on a recorder that takes a second a frame, so
      the recorder puts them on the virtual clock as starting 0.6s after
      the swap.
  - **Gate: `check_b317_rings`** - all four states on both reference
    devices, read off the rings Home really builds: the top tier matches
    the orange's stroke-width, opacity, stroke-opacity, glow shape and
    alpha and paint alpha, with no extra circles; by default its paint
    is light and carries all six flare hues round the ring (sampled off
    the pattern's picture at 24 angles), each flare's centre at least as
    vivid as the orange and the glow the same rings blurred by the
    drop-shadow's own amount; the sweep turns and stops under Reduce
    motion; `"black"` is built the same way, near-black with an ember
    glow; and the ring draw opens in the old look, draws both rings
    filter-free with glints, records the key, hands over, does not play
    on the second Home, waits for a tour, plays from no tier when the
    key is missing, and does nothing under Reduce motion. Fails 1888b11
    (5.2 wide, six extra circles, black, no draw); the vividness check
    fails 3644f1b (round three).
- **HOME'S TAPS: A RANK BUBBLE ANSWERS LIKE A SECRET FLARE, AND THE PLANET
  ANSWERS THE TOUCH (build 317).** *"I like what happens when you click the
  secret flares. Can the large flares do the same? I also think the same
  could go for the large planet, improve what happens when you click."*
  **REPLACED BY ROUND THREE (below): there is no box, no pointer line, no
  ring and no follow any more** - `showContextualInfo`,
  `contextualFollowPath`, `ringFit`, `aimEdge`, `refind` and
  `check_b317_followglide` are gone. What follows in this bullet is the
  history of rounds one and two; the planet's touch (`planetTapFx`) and the
  bubble's light (`flareBubbleTold`, reworked) are the parts that survive.
  - **What a secret flare did** (REPLACED - round three):
    `showContextualInfo(dot, flareSays(...), { follow, ring, refind })` - a
    box that follows the turning dot, a ring round it in place of the grey
    dot, found again if Home is rebuilt, open 4.2s; pressing it moves
    nothing.

    ring is the bubble's own width + 10px, not the 16-28px a tiny flare
    gets), and answers in the glass with `flareBubbleTold()`: a light of
    its own colour (`--rank-color`) swelling from the middle and fading,

    bubble opened a box that stayed where it was put, with "Bronze rank -
    reached. Its flare is lit." **It never opened the Rank screen and
    still opens nothing.** The bubbles do not orbit on Home (only in the
    rank-up scene); `follow` costs nothing and keeps the box on the
    bubble through any re-layout.
  - **The flare and its rank share a name now** (`ACCENT_DISPLAY_NAME` was
    renamed to the rank names), so the words are "Gold flare. Lit since
    you reached Gold rank." held, and "Platinum flare. Reach Platinum rank
    to light it: 10 more levels, 2 more badges." locked - the old flare
    names (Ember, Comet) do not exist any more.
  - **The planet keeps its "....." and gains a touch** (`planetTapFx`): the
    surface presses in (its edge darkens), a ripple of light runs out from
    where the finger landed, a halo leaves the rim, the inner ring then the
    outer one brighten (outline overlays, not the rings themselves, which
    live in the filtered svg), and the two rings of secret flares surge a
    few degrees and give them back over nine seconds - the individual
    `rotate` property on the orbit layers, which adds to their `transform`
    spin, so they end on the shared loop clock again. All in one
    `.cosmic-tapfx` box made on the first tap and placed just before the
    rank bubbles: over the sphere and anything later drawn on it (the
    Supernova scar), under the bubbles, `pointer-events:none`. The
    planet's own DOM is not touched. Transform and opacity only.
  - **Reduce motion**: no ripple, no surge, no swell; the press, the halo,
    the rings and the bubble's light show still for a moment. No layout
    moves (measured: the greeting, Start Studying and the hero box are
    identical before, during and after). A tap is the only thing that
    starts any of it, so it cannot collide with the unlock queue, a tour
    (which takes the tap itself) or the daily alert.
  - The bubble's light is removed when its animation finishes, not on a
    timer, so a slowed or seeked page keeps it until it has played.
  - **Gate (round one, rewritten in round three): `check_b317_hometaps`** - real clicks at the live positions on
    both reference devices: a held and a locked bubble (words, ring sized
    to the bubble, following, the light), a secret flare unchanged, the
    planet ("....." kept, five overlay animations, both flare rings
    surging, no filter, no layout shift, one box after four taps, at most
    one surge per ring), and Reduce motion (still and visible, nothing
    moving). Fails 1888b11.
  - **The box rode with the flare, on the compositor (round two - REPLACED:
    there is no box to ride).**
    *"The things pop up when clicking the flares they slightly shake."*
    The follow was a requestAnimationFrame loop that MEASURED the target
    each frame and wrote the line's left/top and a rounded translate. The
    flare moves on the compositor (the orbit's spin, a bubble's float), so
    on any frame the main thread missed the box stood still while the
    flare went on, then jumped to catch up. Now the box, its line and its
    ring are one group (`#contextual-info-follow`, fixed, the size of the
    screen, so the children's fixed positions mean what they always did),
    and `contextualFollowPath()` reads the target's path over the box's
    life ONCE, by stepping the target's own animations (every ancestor
    animation that moves it, the surge included) through 4.65s in 150ms
    steps and measuring, then puts every one back (running ones by their
    start time, so they stay on the timeline). The group plays that path
    as translate3d keyframes from the same moment, so box and flare move
    together on the compositor frame for frame. No layout property is
    written after placement, nothing is rounded, and the box is placed
    once already clear of the screen edges for the whole path, so it
    never flips side. `refind` re-reads the path from the new target if
    Home is rebuilt underneath. Nothing moving (Reduce motion) means no
    path and a still box. **Measured** (`check_b317_followglide`,
    frame-stepped, the page's frame callbacks run on two frames in four):
    worst frame-to-frame change of the box's offset from an inner-ring
    flare 1.02px on e877af7 (17 Pro Max), 0.012/0.033px after (17 Pro Max
    / iPad Pro 11); from a floating bubble 0.36/0.35px before (a slow
    bob, under the bar, so only the flare case fails before) and
    0.023/0.068px after.
  - **The planet's pointer ended on its rim** (REPLACED - no pointer) (`aimEdge`): *"clicking the
    planet, the line pointing at goes to the center, do it from the
    bottom or top edge."* The line runs to the sphere's bottom edge when
    the box is below it and its top edge when above. The tap effect
    itself is unchanged (*"The effect when clicking it is cool."*).
  - Recorded frame-stepped: the popups' 3.2/4.2s timers run in real time,
    so the recorder clears `showContextualInfo._t` and closes them on the
    virtual clock, and `element.animate()` is patched to freeze each new
    animation at the virtual moment it is made.
- **THE END OF A RUN, WALKED END TO END (build 317 flow).** Madison: *"Absolutely
  make sure the flow of the unlock stuff is good and the flow of everything
  else in the result screen is good to go."* Every stage was driven for real
  (answers clicked, pop-ups read for 3s and tapped, Main menu, Home, the
  Profile tab's call) and timed on both reference devices - a 100% that tips
  Gold, a badge, a hundo effect, level 80, the daily, two badges at once,
  Reduce motion, Mute banners, a Virtual Room. Five things were out of
  order; all five are orchestration, none is inside a cutscene or an effect:
  - **A one-level climb popped half-way through its second fill.** The
    pop step asked `levelBlock.matches(".is-levelup")` while the sequence
    was being BUILT - a class the climb adds 1.1s into its own fill - so it
    always got 1.25s, the multi-level path's own `fillMs` aside. The block
    says `levelsUp` now and the pop waits 2.05s. **Never decide a step's
    delay from a class the animation adds later.**
  - **The 100%'s effect was faded out 2.3s in by the first scene.** Grade
    +180ms the effect, +1300 the Unlocked card, +1200 the badge case or
    rank cutscene, whose dim fades the effect (`clearCelebrationsForScene`):
    a World Tree is 5.6s, a UFO 8.6s. The first held step after the grade
    now waits until `HUNDO_FX_TAIL_AT[id]` (`firstHeld()` in
    `showRunRewards`) - a plain delay, so a tap still brings it on. Confetti
    has no tail entry and is over by 2.5s anyway.
  - **Re-run and Main menu landed under a scene's bridge.** A scene leaves
    `openSceneBridge` up (72% black) for the pop-up it expects; a badge case
    that is the LAST unlock has nothing to claim it, so the buttons sat
    under it for ~1.4s. The actions step and `finish()` drop it.
  - **The character's special played under scenes** - "no character
    special while any cutscene, overlay or reward card is up". The idle
    scheduler counted the results card as on screen under the badge case,
    the rank cutscene and a reward card (it is: under their dim), and the
    hundo's own special (2.6s after the reaction) was cut by the badge case
    a second in. `charSpecialCovered(el)`: anything in `CHAR_SPECIAL_COVERS`
    (the case, every cutscene, a pop-up, the flare scenes, the scene bridge,
    LOADING, a tour, What's New, the generating overlay, a sheet) that the
    character is NOT itself inside - the person card is an `.invite-overlay`
    and its character is one of the prominent ones - or, for the results
    character, the reveal still running (`.rs-rewards:not(.rs-done)`: a
    special begun in the gap between two pop-ups is under the next one a
    second later). The scheduler passes over a covered character and
    `charSpecialFire` waits for it to clear. On a run with unlocks the
    hundo special is the reveal's last beat, fired from `finish()` 0.7s
    after the buttons are in.
  - **Home sat unlocked ~2.7s after Main menu before the rank-up lock.**
    `showHome()` always arms the card queue's 2.2s timer and
    `rankUpLockWaits()` waited on the timer whether or not a card was due -
    with Start Studying live the whole time. It waits only when a card is
    really owed (`rankUpLockCardDue()`); otherwise it locks at its own 1.2s.
  - **Left as they are, on purpose**: a muted or Reduce-motion run still
    plays its rank cutscene on Home (the builds 217-218 rule) - under
    Reduce motion it is the ~4.4s still scene now (see the rank-up
    cutscene's flow round) - and the rank-up
    Profile scene's ~20s is its own design.
  - **Gate: `check_b317_flow`** - the one-level pop >= 1.9s on both
    devices, the World Tree to its tail before the case, the hundo special
    never under the case and after it, no live bridge when the buttons land,
    the lock within 1.9s with nothing owed, the idle special never under a
    cutscene and played once it goes. All seven fail on e877af7; the eighth
    (a person card's own character still plays its special) guards the
    inside-the-overlay exception and passes on both. `FX_RUN` (the gates'
    real 100%) now waits 12s for the effect, not 6: a run that climbs a
    level lands its grade 0.8s later than it did, and check_b314_unlocks'
    Fireworks and Bubbles sections ran out of budget on a loaded box.
  - **How it was measured, for next time**: a 40ms poll in the page
    records every stage turning on and off (each card landing, the pop,
    the effect's layer, the case, the cutscene, each pop-up and its kind,
    the bridge, the buttons, the lock, the call, LOADING, the map, the
    arrival, each special), while a scripted person reads each pop-up for
    3s and taps it, taps Main menu 1.5s after the buttons and Profile 2.2s
    after the call. The MP4 is `tools/record-hundo.py`'s clock (every
    timer, rAF and animation on a clock advanced 1/30s a frame) run over
    the whole walk, with the person acting on that clock. A screenshot
    harness on a loaded box takes 0.5-1s a shot, so stills lag their
    stage; the poll's times are the measurement.
- **THE SECRET FLARE SCENES, REBUILT (build 317).** Madison: *"The secret
  flare cutscenes, these are a huge one ... they could be longer, and I think
  the way the character pops out is kind of lame, it's just a still character
  with the body, could it be animated? Maybe you make it so it's super dark
  and you can barely see the character but still can tell it's a character
  ... Change that part for them all ... they should all be different but
  similar ... This rank up cutscene is nearly perfect, I need these ones to
  be on par"*, and *"If the cutscene needs to be longer to make it cooler
  then do it. THAT GOES FOR ANY CUTSCENE IN THE APP, longer is better."*
  Every scene a find plays is new: `playFlareFoundScene` picks
  `playFirstFlaresScene` (red, orange), `playVoidFlareScene` (the third),
  `playUmbraFlareScene`, `playHorizonFlareScene`, `playGenesisFlareScene`.
  `playFinalFlareScene` is kept as an alias for old callers.
  - **One engine, one arc** (`sfScene`, `sfFigure`; CSS "THE SECRET FLARE
    SCENES"), in the rank-up's language: an opaque dark (#030209), the
    subject rising out of it .32s later, the FIND (the flare streaks in and
    ignites - the rank-up's `.rank-litpop`, `sfIgnite`), the BUILD-UP (the
    flare's own story, speeding up to a climax), the DARK, the SILHOUETTE,
    ITS MOVE, THE LIGHT RISES, the TITLE (the rank-up's type: kicker, the
    name big in the serif with a glow of its colour, one line), ONE ending
    (`sf-end`: stage, sky, wash and words fade together, then `sf-out` and
    the bridge in the character's colour). Lengths, start to hand-over
    (b6cd249 -> now): first two 5.1 -> 10.3s, Void 18.7 -> 28.7, Umbra
    18.9 -> 27.7, Horizon 19.1 -> 28.3, Genesis 19.3 -> 28.6.
  - **The four stories.** *Void* - absence: the three spots round the
    planet, Afterglow lands, the three whirl faster and faster, light
    streams in off the sky, the planet's core goes black from inside, the
    flares spiral in and are swallowed, it implodes to a point that goes
    out, and a wave of black runs out and takes every star with it; then
    three small lights in a triangle (its face) and the hood round them.
    *Umbra* - the eclipse: Penumbra lights the moon's limb, the shadow
    slides across, Baily's beads, the diamond ring, the corona round a
    black disc; two violet eyes open IN the disc and the hood grows out
    of it, the corona its rim light; its move turns the corona down
    (`sf-lamp`) and its second pulse is third contact (the diamond on the
    far limb), the light back, the moon's phases round it. *Horizon* - the
    edge: a black hole pulls every flare found in, stretched, and they
    freeze at its edge; the hole sinks and its disc lies down flat - a
    horizon line; light breaks over it like a dawn (glow and rays) and
    Horizon rises out of it in three stages (wholly under, head over the
    edge in the dark, shoulders in the light). *Genesis* - creation: your
    own Home planet (`buildCosmicHero(true)`), Worldheart dives in, the
    ranks clear and the camera closes in, cracks, a growing quake, the
    split on a blazing core with a column of light, the matter flung off
    becomes a disc round the core, and the silhouette stands in the core's
    glare. Overlay states are `sf-*` (`sf-pull`, `sf-total` ...): the Home
    hero inside Genesis styles `.is-found` and friends, so a bare `is-*`
    on the overlay could one day match its descendants.
  - **THE CHARACTER IS NEVER A STILL PUT ON SCREEN.** `sfFigure` holds the
    live drawing twice, built in the same moment: `sfSilhouetteSVG` (ONE
    svg: a copy of the figure painted in a rim-light gradient of its
    flare's colour, a hair larger about the chest and lifted, under a copy
    painted near-black - so only the edge catches the light; `SF_SIL[ch]`
    says what stays lit in its own paint (`keep`: eyes, the worn flare,
    the special's parts; `first`: what lights before the rest) and what
    is light rather than shape (`drop`)) and `sfLitSVG` (the drawing as
    everywhere else, without its little scenery - the scene is its
    scenery). Both take `.char-live` in ONE frame (`F.live()`, at the
    first beat the figure shows), so every idle loop and later the special
    run in step across the wipe's edge, and nothing invisible repaints
    through the build-up. In the dark it BREATHES (`.sf-breath`, the
    `scale` property, alternate) and TURNS towards you (`.sf-figmove`, a
    flat turn: the body narrowed as if turned 13deg away, opening out
    through 6 to facing you, with a drift, a lean, a rise and a settle -
    `scale` x/y, `translate`, `rotate`, three transitions). **Never
    `rotate:y`**: it was, under a perspective, and a 3D transform on any
    ancestor makes Chromium raster the drawing's CLIPPED parts coarse -
    Umbra's brow moon was a blurred block for the whole silhouette while
    everything round it stayed sharp (found frame by frame on the
    recording; real time showed the same). At 13deg the keystone a real
    turn adds is a few per cent.
  - **Its own special turns the light on.** `F.special()` puts
    `char-special` on both copies for `CHAR_SPECIAL_MS[ch]`; the reveal is
    timed to the special's own flash (Void's white at 3.12s, Umbra's
    second pulse, Horizon's flare pulled back in at 2.35s, Genesis's rose
    at 2.82s). One gesture, the same in all four: the family resemblance.
  - **The light rises as a wipe of the lit copy over the dark one, on two
    transforms**: `.sf-wipe` (overflow hidden, its top edge feathered by a
    STILL mask) slides up while `.sf-wipe-in` slides down by exactly as
    much, so the drawing holds still and the edge passes over it - the
    compositor's job, never a clip-path or a moving mask. A line of light
    riding the edge was tried and dropped: it travelled over the empty air
    above the head and read as an ellipse floating there.
  - **A CSS MASK ON THE <svg> BREAKS ITS INNER CLIP-PATHS IN CHROMIUM.**
    The bust-dissolving mask was first on the svgs (as the app-wide
    `.avatarchar-svg` edge mask is): Umbra's brow moon drew as a full disc,
    and under the 3D turn as a blurred square; on the wrapper
    (`.sf-figbody`) every clip draws. The scene's drawings carry
    `mask-image:none` and `filter:none` (avatarDepth is an svg filter).
    Not checked: whether the app-wide mask does the same to Umbra's moon
    at board size in Chromium - at 12px nobody would see it, and iOS is

  - **`focusQuietly(el)` is the only way a screen focuses a control now.**
    The focus stays - Enter and a screen reader start from it - but unless
    the last input was a key (`lastInputKeyboard`, set by any non-modifier
    keydown and cleared by any pointerdown/touchstart/mousedown, all in
    capture), the element carries `.is-quietfocus`, and
    `.is-quietfocus:focus-visible{ outline:none !important }` takes any
    ring off it, the UA's included. The first key press takes the class
    off every element, so a keyboard user sees exactly where they are; a
    blur takes it off too. Text fields are still focused plainly - a caret
    and the keyboard are the point there.

### Build 314 - the gate: levels, ranks and badges tied together

**The rule, Madison's words:** *"you can't get past that next ranks level
until you hit the badges needed."* Each rank's LEVEL is a gate its BADGES
open. With b badges the highest level you can hold is the level of the
first rank asking for more than b badges: 0 badges -> 21, 1-2 -> 29,
3-4 -> 36, 5-6 -> 45, 7-8 -> 52, 9-11 -> 65, 12-13 -> 71, 14+ -> the cap.
You can REACH a gate's level; you cannot pass it until you hold its
badges. `badgeWallLevel()` reads this off `TIER_UNLOCKS`, never a typed
table, so moving a rank moves its gate.

- **XP IS NEVER CAPPED.** The total keeps counting at a gate; only the
  level is held. When the badge lands the level jumps straight to what
  the XP has earned. *"When hitting max, the numbers would start
  collecting ... 700/100 or whatever it'd be."* At a gate the bar for
  that level fills as normal, then STAYS full in a brighter "banked"
  blue with a ring round the track (`.is-banked`), and the numbers above
  it run past what the level asks: `into / span XP`, e.g.
  "44,475 / 5,085 XP". `levelStateOf()` deliberately does NOT cap `into`
  at `span` when `stopped`.
- **One function owns the level.** `levelStateFor(st)` (and `levelOf`,
  now `effectiveLevelOf`) = `min(curve level, max(badge wall,
  levelFloor))`, never above `LEVEL_CAP`. Everything that shows or
  publishes a level goes through it: the rankings row
  (`buildLeaderboardRow`), chat and Virtual Room presence, the ranks
  (`rankOf`, `tierColorUnlocked`), the level-80 banner, the flare level
  gates, the Profile card, the results card, the road map.
  `rankOfStats()` also holds a published level to the badge wall, which
  cannot change an answer (a rank needs its badges, and with them the
  wall is already past its level) but means a row from an older build is
  asked the same question.
- **THE GRANDFATHER FLOOR - nobody loses a level, and nobody is lifted
  past their badges.** `store.levelFloor`, defaulted ONCE in
  `applyLoadedData()` for an account that has none, is the level it holds
  NOW, on the OLD curve (`legacyLevelOfPoints`, build 313's curve kept for
  this one job). It was first built as the HIGHER of the old and new
  curves, which would have handed every player at the top 5-7 free levels
  on the day it shipped, and Madison stopped it: *"Here's the part you
  aren't considering at all, by giving us at the top more levels, we are
  already under the badge count needed to rank up, by leveling us up even
  more, the discrepancy of badges to levels WILL get even more."*
  So: effective level = min(new curve, max(gate, floor)). An account
  inside its gate gets the new curve's boost; one already past its gate
  stays exactly where it is, and the XP the new curve would have turned
  into levels shows as overflow on a full bar ("banked") until its badges
  open the gate, when the results card climbs through every banked level.
  **NOTHING may write a floor from the new curve.** Floors merge by max
  (`mergeSameAccount`, `mergeLeavingAccount`), so one new-curve floor
  anywhere would leak the lift in for good. That includes the roll-out
  case: a copy from an older build arrives with no floor and is defaulted
  again - from the OLD curve, so it is the same number. `check-curve`
  section 8 asserts the floor is the old curve's level, a held account is
  not boosted, an unheld one is, and fails on the max-floor commit
  (44ffd88). 0 for a new account and after a reset
  (`wipeLocalProgressAndSettings`).
  **Lowering progress on purpose must lower `levelFloor` too**, like the
  `__floor` document, or the floor hands the level straight back.
  A merge's `bonusLevels` gift raises the floor to the gifted level: it is
  an explicit gift, and at a gate more XP would show nothing.
- **THE NEXT GATE is the one idea every surface shows** (*"we really
  need the levels, ranks, badges to all be tied together perfectly"*).
  `nextGateOf()`: when your level is held, the rank whose badges open it
  (a grandfathered level 52 with 3 badges is at the SAPPHIRE gate, 9
  badges, not Gold's); otherwise simply the next rank. Copy, plain and
  the same everywhere: "Next gate", "Level", "Badges", and
  **"Earn N more badge(s) to pass level L"** ("more" only when you hold
  at least one).
  - Profile: directly under the XP bar, a Next gate box
    (`buildNextGateSection`): the rank's emblem and name, two chips
    (`buildGateChips`: "Level 25 / 29" or "Level 29 ✓", "Badges 1 / 3"),
    the line above when it is holding you, and "Closest: <unit>, X of Y
    hundos". At a gate the old "Level N → N+1  43%" line is replaced by
    it.
  - Results card (every mode, the Virtual Room too): the overflow numbers
    under the bar and one compact line, "Next gate: Silver · Badges 1 / 3
    · Earn 2 more badges to pass level 29", then the closest badge.
    `summarize()` hands the badge count either side of the run
    (`lastRunBadgesBefore/After`) so a run that opens a gate climbs
    through EVERY banked level, one fill after another (quicker per level
    the more there are; timers, not transitionend, so Reduce motion
    cannot stall it), and the tag reads "Up N levels".
    `levelBlock.fillMs` tells the reveal sequence how long that takes.
  - Rank tab: every stop's requirement line is the two chips against
    you (ticked once met); the current gate is outlined, its circle
    carries "X / Y badges" and its card the same "Earn N more ..." line;
    the hero adds one summary - "Bronze · Level 25 · 1 badge" and "Next
    gate: Silver" with what it takes. The climb's note says it once
    ("... unlocks rewards along the way. Its level is a gate: you can
    reach it, but you only climb past it once you hold its badges" - the
    "unlocks" stays, check-behaviour asserts it), and a rank's own card
    says "Level 29 is a gate: you climb past it once you hold 3 badges".
    User-facing copy says GATE, never wall. Gate content only - the road's own
    animation, end circle and colours are another builder's.
- **RE-MEASURE: a rank's level and the gate are now the SAME number
  doing two jobs.** Move a rank's level and you move a wall people are
  standing at. Check the board (`firestore-admin.py audit`) first.

*"Level 71 needs about 140,000 total XP and level 80 about 200,000"*,
against the class's measured pace (median active player ~160,000 XP by
January 1st; 25th percentile ~85k, 75th ~325k, a little allowed for the
holidays). Levels 1-25 untouched (21 is still 9,912); x1.18 into 26 (1,087
against 25's 921), then every level +3.65% (`LEVEL_LATE_GROWTH`), one rate
with no bands: 29 17,933 · 36 27,739 · 45 44,567 · 52 61,965 · 65 108,478 ·
71 138,431 · 80 197,370. **Raising LEVEL_CAP (100-120 is planned) just
carries the same growth on; nothing below it is re-fitted.** The steep
tail past 45 is retired (`LEVEL_STEEP_*` kept for `legacyLevelOfPoints`).
**Every level 2-80 is CHEAPER than build 313, so no XP total reads a lower
level** - `check-curve` section 2 walks 0-600,000 in steps of 37 against
313's curve rebuilt from its own constants. What anybody actually SEES is
the curve held by the gate and the old-curve floor (above): nobody's level
goes down, and the boost only reaches whoever is inside their gate.

cheapest first, reaches 1 -> 12, 3 -> 25, 5 -> 33, 7 -> 40, 9 -> 46,

`tools/firestore-admin.py audit` now checks a row's level against the

### Build 315 - the results screens at the grade number's standard

*"The result screen numbers nice, let's ensure all other things on the
result screen is up to par with that cleanliness."* The grade (build 314:
the system sans, heavy, lining figures, a small raised %) set the standard,
and every end-of-run screen is one type system now: the rewards screen, the
review, a retake, a no-XP (Starred) run, the daily question's verdict, the
Virtual Room's results and its leaderboard. Pop-ups and cutscenes over the
results (`.rs-spot`, the badge case, the flare scenes) keep their own
display face and were not touched.

- **ONE FACE, ONE KIND OF FIGURE.** Every number is `--sans` with lining,
  tabular figures, set ONCE on `.rs-screen`, `.vrc` and `.dailyq-outro`
  and inherited, so nothing added later can come up old-style or
  proportional. What was not, measured: the units title ("1 unit", Georgia
  - an old-style "1" on a phone), the XP total (the mono, where a comma is
  a whole figure wide: "+2,085" read "+2 ,085"), the Unlocked rows' names
  (`.unlockbanner`'s Georgia), the room's "4/4" (mono), the leaderboard's
  step ("Final standings", Georgia) and its scores (mono), and the daily
  verdict ("Correct", Georgia). A `<button>` does not inherit the figures -
  the UA's `font` shorthand resets them - so the results' buttons say
  `font-variant-numeric:inherit`. (The review's question text drew in the
  sans all along - `[data-layout="modern"] .rq` outranks `.rs-q-text` -
  and now says so itself.)
- **FIVE ROLES, ONE SIZE EACH**, as variables on `.rs-screen`: kicker
  (.68 / .72rem tablet - card headings, the stamps, the rank under the
  level, an unlock row's heading, the review's tags), label (.92 / 1rem - an
  XP line and its value, "Total", a unit's name and score, a badge's name,
  an unlock's name, the room's status line), caption (.78 / .84rem - the
  line under a label or a bar). The hero (the grade) and the display sizes
  (the XP total, the units title) are unchanged. Before, measured: as many
  as four kicker sizes, six label sizes and four caption sizes on one
  screen (a three-unit run; a Virtual Room race).
- **A PAIR IS "N / M"**, never "N of M" or "N/M": the grade's "10 / 12",
  each unit's "10 / 12", the room's "3 / 4" - the level bar's
  "216 / 2,156 XP" (Profile's own `buildXpNumbers`, unchanged) set the
  pattern. The "out of" half is quieter (`.rs-frac-of`): an opacity of the
  number's own colour, not a grey, so a hundo effect's tint still reaches
  the whole figure. `rsNum()` / `rsPair()` format every count on these
  screens, thousands separated - "1500 of 1500" was the one bare count.
  **Not done, and flagged:** the hundo-effect miniature
  (`buildHundoFxMock`, another builder's) still prints "12 of 12" and
  "12/12" - two strings to bring in line after the merge.
- **THE LEVEL IS A NUMBER, SET LIKE THE GRADE**: "Level 33" in the heavy
  sans, not "LEVEL 33" in spaced capitals (which pulled the 3s apart); the
  rank under it is a kicker; "Level up" is a pill like the stamps, centred
  on the number by the flex row rather than nudged up .12em.
- **ONE TEXT EDGE.** Every card takes `.rs-card`'s padding. The grade card
  had its own - 1.6px further in on a phone and, because its rule
  outranked the tablet one, 2.4px on an iPad - and so did the retake note
  and the room's waiting card, so their headings, names and right-hand
  numbers sat off the line the others share. The header ("Test results",
  the chip, the units title, the unit list) is one column: the title used
  to sit 20px in from the chip above it.
- **THE XP LINES FLOATED 12px HIGH, FOREVER.** `.rs-xpline.rs-land{
  transform:translateY(-12px) }` comes later than `.rs-land.rs-in-now{
  transform:none }` at the same weight, so a landed line kept its -12px:
  each jumped up as its drop ended, the first sat 10px under "XP earned"
  (every other card's heading ~20px over its first line) and the rule over
  Total had 30px above it and 17 below. `.rs-xpline.rs-land.rs-in-now{
  transform:none }`; now every heading is 18-21px over its first line and
  the rule is 20 / 20 - measured off the ink (font metrics on each text
  node's rect), never off the element boxes.
- **NO LABEL BREAKS INSIDE ITS PILL.** Two buttons share a row only when
  both fit in equal halves (`flex-basis:calc(50% - gap)` +
  `min-width:max-content`), else each takes a row: "Re-run the full test"
  stood on three lines beside a one-line Main menu at 320px, and Main menu
  itself broke in two there. The leaderboard's Return to lobby / Main menu
  the same. The wide button ("Continue to review (N missed)") can still
  need two lines at 320px and then breaks evenly (`text-wrap:balance`, as
  do the retake line, the room's status and the daily verdict's last line).
- An XP row is a two-column grid with its caption across both columns: as
  a column beside the value it was ~150px on a 320-375px phone and broke
  "1:24 total · 11s a / question". The unit rows follow the header's order
  (they came in whichever unit's question fell first). Badge names wrap
  evenly instead of ending "Identity Crimes ba..." at 320px, and the badge
  line breaks only at its dot. The room's review tabs say "Missed" on a
  phone ("Missed questions" broke in two on every phone; the full words on
  a tablet). On the leaderboard "(you)" never gives way to a long name.
- **Measuring here, a caveat:** Chromium in the sandbox draws the system
  sans as DejaVu Sans, 15-20% wider than SF Pro (and Liberation Sans a
  little narrower), so a wrap seen here may not happen on an iPhone. The
  layouts above are wrap-SAFE - they stack or break evenly when they must -
  rather than tuned to fit one font.
- **Gate: check-results section 9** - `TYPE_AUDIT` (no serif, no
  old-style figures, every number the --sans with tabular figures,
  pseudo-element text included) on a drill, its review, a three-unit 100%
  that earns a badge, an exam, a retake, a Starred run, the daily verdict,
  a Virtual Room race and its leaderboard; `SHAPE_AUDIT` (one size per
  role, one text edge, numbers on the content edge, equal heading gaps,
  even card gaps, no lifted XP line, the header on one edge, every pair
  "N / M"); `ONE_LINE` at 320 and 375px. It fails in every scenario on
  f543e95 and, on 94a3108^, catches the serif grade itself ("83%", "92%",
  "100%" in Georgia). It also runs one scenario at 834px, so the tablet
  sizes are held to one per role as well. check-vroom compares the room's
  count by its digits, not its spacing.
- **The sweep looks at the results screen now.** It was never in `SCREENS`
  because it needs a run behind it; `RESULTS_STAGE` (an init script) gives
  the sweep `__sweepResults('drill')` - three whole units with two missed -
  and `__sweepResults('retake')`, both put through the real `summarize()`
  with reduce motion, last in the list because a run changes the account.
  Every combination in the matrix (74 today) now audits the results
  screen for overflow, insets and collisions like every other screen.
- **Run these gates one at a time.** With a sweep running beside it,
  check-behaviour's check_b232 (a banner drawn into its chip after the
  first paint) and check_penal_versions (a tap on the unit card) failed on
  this build and passed alone; check_b282's ring arc fails on f543e95 under
  load and passes alone. They measure timing, and a loaded box moves it.

### Build 315 - every account write is a transaction

**Two accounts went down overnight on Oct 6-7, on current builds.** The
read-only audit against the 21:05 backup (`firestore-admin.py audit
--backup`) caught both:
- **Rogelio.salcedo, -2,590 XP.** The account AND its high-water mark
  were replaced by a copy last saved at 22:33 on Oct 5 - one the server
  had never seen (every backup through Oct 6 13:43 still had the 21:55
  copy). His other phone's tally went back from 4,210 to 1,620. That phone
  had played the 2,590 on Oct 6.
- **Alfred Lake, -1 full test, -1,640 XP, -3 hundos.** A phone with a
  new tally id wrote at 05:57 on Oct 7 from a copy that predated his Oct 6
  17:55 test: the test, its hundos in TCOLE Rules, Racial Profiling and
  Multiculturalism, and the other phone's tally (6,180 back to 4,540) were
  gone, its own 2,345 XP and Constitution hundo kept - which is why the
  hundo count only went down by two.

**Why the gates were green.** Build 296's gate (`cloudConfirmedFor`)
waits for one server read per launch and then trusts it. But a merge only
runs when a snapshot ARRIVES, and a phone that is offline, asleep, or
whose listener has gone quiet gets none - only its own write shown back
to it. Two ways in, both seen here: a write made as the app was hidden
(`publishNow`) that Firestore could not send before iOS suspended the
page, which Firestore keeps and sends when the app wakes, a day later,
over whatever was played since (Rogelio - and it wrote the floor too,
because the floor goes out on the way out); and a phone that played on a
copy the server had moved past (Alfred). The per-device tallies (298)
cannot help with either: they only work when the writer has merged.

**The fix: `writeAccount()`, a transaction.**
- It reads the account (and `__floor` when that goes too) in the same
  round trip as the write. Where the server's copy holds progress this
  copy lacks, the two are merged exactly as a snapshot would merge them
  (`mergeSameAccount`; the newer side's preferences, as
  `syncSameAccount` does) and the merge is what goes up; the device then
  takes the merge itself.
- **"Holds progress this copy lacks" is `accountAhead()`, and it is
  deliberately narrow**: lifetime counts, hundos per unit, the per-device
  tallies (not the week's), study time per day, test history. Only
  things that grow by play and that no load or merge ever lowers. Where
  the server holds nothing new, this device's copy goes up exactly as
  before - which is what still lets a voided weekly win, a cleared list
  or a reset flag reach the account. Merging on every write instead
  would bring a voided win straight back each time and two devices would
  trade the same write forever.
- **The high-water mark is read and merged only when the account
  exists.** A missing account is brand new or reset, and a floor left
  behind must never bring a reset one back - the same rule
  `markCloudConfirmed` follows at launch - so there the floor is written
  over unread. The first version of this read it regardless, and
  `check-sync` 8f's reset case caught it.
- Firestore never queues a transaction offline and never replays one
  late; it commits only if what it read is unchanged and otherwise runs
  it again against the new copy. A write that fails leaves nothing behind:
  it drops `cloudConfirmedFor`, so the next one waits for a fresh server
  read (`ensureCloudConfirmed`, which retries on `online` and on becoming
  visible), and the row waits with it. The first failure retries as soon
  as the server answers; a run of them keeps the minute between pushes.
- One at a time per device (`accountWriteAt`); what is asked for in the
  meantime goes when the first lands.
- **The row goes once the account write has landed** (`afterAccountWrite`),
  so the board never runs ahead of the account - `check-sync` 8h failed
  the first version of this, which still sent the row in the same tick as
  the push. On the way out of the app it goes at once (`flushLeaderboardRow`)
  rather than waiting out its 90s deferral. A failed account write drops
  the confirmation, and `writeLeaderboardRow` holds every row until the
  account is confirmed again.
- Cost: one extra read per push, two when the floor goes with it. With
  pushes at most once a minute while answering, that is a few thousand
  reads a day across the class against the 50,000 free.
- `writeAccount` has two paths that exist only for the gates' stand-ins:
  read-merge-write for one with no `runTransaction`, and the old plain
  write (row straight after) for one that cannot read at all - the
  friends and chat gates, which measure the row, not the account. The
  real SDK always takes the transaction.

**Gates.**
- `check-sync` 8k replays both incidents against a stand-in server that
  keeps versions, holds writes made offline and sends them when the
  network returns, and commits a transaction only if what it read is
  unchanged: (A) a quiet listener and the other phone's test, (B) a save
  made offline and sent a day late, (C) the other phone's write landing
  between this phone's read and its commit, (D) the server holding
  nothing new. A, B and C fail on 313 and on 315 before this
  (32,345 / 20,000 / 10,500), D passes everywhere.
- `check-sync` 8e's server answered a direct read with "no such
  document" while its listener said otherwise, so build 313's own server
  read (`ensureCloudConfirmed`) confirmed an account that did not exist.
  It passed on 313 only because the push happened to land just after the
  snapshot, and failed on 315 when boot got a little slower. Its server is
  now unreachable until its snapshot arrives. It still fails on 295.

**The two accounts heal themselves when the right phone opens** - on any
build from 298 on: Rogelio's phone that played on Oct 6, and Alfred's
phone that played his Oct 6 test, both still hold that progress in their
own tallies, and merging the server's copy into them pushes it back.
Never hand-credit them: that counts it twice the moment those phones
merge. A server-side restore from the 21:05 backup (merging, never
replacing) is the alternative if either phone is gone, and it needs
Madison's go.

### Build 315 - one flip-book recording at a time, for the screen that is up

Three gates went red on the merged 315 build that were green on the home
stream's own (d9a116f): every flare on Home moving within 40s, the
tab-switch timing, and the Bubbles tail. Each had a different cause, and
only one of them was the gate.

- **The rank emblems had no queue.** Home was the only screen that
  recorded them until 315 put flare bubbles on Profile and on the road
  map's chips, each at its own size (Home's are 46px on an iPad, Profile's
  50 and 70, the chips smaller). Every `startOrbitEmblemAnims` call ran its
  own loop, so three screens' recordings shared the same idle time, and a
  recording asked for by a screen that had gone went on to the end.
  Measured in the gate's own order of screens: Home's seven sheets took
  39s against 33s on d9a116f. `orbitRecPump` is the character recorder's
  queue for them: a saved sheet is read at once, one recording at a time,
  oldest first, only for a screen still up; what a gone screen asked for
  is dropped and asked for again when it comes back. 39s became 30s.
- **An unwanted recording stops for a wanted one.** `recordingWantedNow()`
  looks at both queues; a rank sheet or a character sheet that nobody can
  see any more stops at its next batch when the screen that is up is
  waiting on one. In the gate that started Home's first sheet at 20.7s
  instead of 24.0s (a Profile bubble and a Customize picker tile had been
  finishing first). A stopped character recording returns `false`, which
  the tile reads as "dropped, ask again" - never `null`, which is "cannot
  be made" and sends the tile live.
- **A hidden tab bar made your own character a live drawing for the rest
  of the session.** Picking a character in Customize redraws the tab's
  avatar while the bar is hidden; `charFlipAttach` read the width of an
  element with no box, which is its declared `100%`, as 100px - over
  `CHAR_FLIP_MAX_CSS` - and the tile went live for good: nine animations
  repainting inside an svg on every screen afterwards, the thing the
  flip-books exist to stop. No box now means later: the attach returns
  `null`, the retry loop leaves it to the watcher, and the watcher
  attaches it when the bar is shown. Look for this whenever a tile is
  drawn while something hides it.
- **Tried and measured, not shipped: serialising the emblem once.** The
  character recorder's template (one serialisation, a marker per moving
  part) makes an emblem snapshot 2-4x cheaper and every sheet came out
  pixel-identical - but the whole recording got SLOWER, 20s to 27s for
  the six, with three times as many idle callbacks timing out: six images
  made in one slice load in one burst and leave no idle time behind them.
  The per-frame clone stays. The work per frame was never the cost; the
  waits between slices are.
- **Where the time goes in this sandbox.** At 834x1194, Home renders at
  about 11 frames a second in software compositing after the gate's
  earlier screens, and every idle callback times out, so the recorder runs
  in its 8ms timeout slices and seven sheets take 30-45s. The home
  stream's own build fails the 40s flare check one run in two here. It
  is a gate sitting on the edge of its budget on this machine, not a
  phone that waits 40s: on a device with a GPU, Home leaves real idle
  time and the slices are 4-12ms. The budget is 60s now. What the check
  guards is "the locked ones move too", and on 298 they never do at any
  budget.
- **The tab-switch gate takes three rounds.** A median of its twelve
  switches swung between 280 and 350ms on one build here; a median of
  thirty-six holds within a few ms. 313 (~390) still fails it. Over
  thirty-six the merged build is 230ms against the home stream's 203; the
  difference is Profile's new card, whose first frame lays out, paints and
  layers about 45ms more each at 4x CPU - the design itself, not a fault.
- **Half the tab-switch regression was 800 CSS rules nobody could file.**
  The characters' results reactions (`tools/gen-reactions.py`) wrote each
  rule as `.rx-<id>.rx-<band> :is(#rx,.part)` - the `#rx` matches
  nothing and is only there to lift the rule to id weight over the idle
  loops. A rule whose last compound is an `:is()` of several things has
  no class or id for Chromium to file it under, so all ~800 were tried
  against every element of every screen drawn, on every screen, though
  they only ever apply on a results screen. The merge took the rules
  ending in `:is()` from 52 to 856. Rewritten as
  `.rx-<id>:where(.rx-<band>) .part:not(#rx)`: the same elements, the
  same weight (1,2,0) - `:where()` costs nothing, `:not(#rx)` is the id -
  and it ends in a class. Tab switches at 4x CPU, median of 36: 262ms
  before, 230ms after (the home stream's own build: 203; the rest of that
  gap is painting the richer Profile card). Proven equal, not assumed:
  every character, every grade, motion on and off, every part's computed
  animation, transform and opacity - 42,320 rows, 0 different, 745 of
  them animating. **Never end a selector in a multi-argument `:is()` in
  anything generated by the hundred**; put the weight on the right of a
  class with `:not(#id)` instead.
- **The Bubbles tail check measured the wrong moment.** It read the
  effect once, at 45% of its tail, and wanted two part-faded pieces.
  That passed d9a116f, where four bubbles sat fully shown until the layer
  was cut away at 7s - the hard cut the unlocks stream's pop fix (7b32502)
  removed - and failed the fixed build, whose bubbles have all faded out
  by 6s. It now watches the tail from its start to the moment the layer
  goes: fading at the start, and nothing (a leaf, with a box) fully shown
  at the last look. Fails d9a116f (four shown at 6.97s), passes every
  effect here.

### Build 317, badge round - badges built in bands, a briefcase that stays open, a token with an edge, one case everywhere

Madison: *"The badge cutscene is great, the only technical flaw right now
is when you open the briefcase, the lid disappears, I think the lid should
still be there so it gets that briefcase feel ... Ensure the badges when
spinning and being placed and everything really give off that 3d look ...
Ensure the edges of the badge look clean and not ridged or rough ... They
need to look a tad bit more real ... rough around the edges and the
surface ... I want that shine on them, that 3d feel, yeah still feel like a
token/badge. If the cutscene needs to be longer to make it cooler then do
it. THAT GOES FOR ANY CUTSCENE IN THE APP, longer is better ... keeping that
briefcase feel app wide now so it's for sure seen as a briefcase ... in the
badge tab, it's a different shape than what you get in the cutscene, in the
profile thing under the challenges it's different, how do we make it all
the same and make it look good without ruining the cohesiveness."*

> **Superseded for the TOKEN by "Build 317, badge2" below.** The bands
> still draw the slot and stay as the token's fallback with no canvas;
> the token itself is now rendered from a height field.

**BADGES ARE BUILT IN BANDS (`buildUnitBadgeSVG`, supersedes "the plate is
the silhouette scaled about ITS OWN centre" and the token's `.86` about the
frame's centre in the Badges section).** Measured on the old drawing, the
roughness was construction, not resolution. Every edge that was not the
outline itself was a COPY of the outline nudged sideways (the slot's lip,
the plate's bevel, the band's catch-light), and a nudged copy of a concave
shape crosses its own inside: the star, the bolt and the burst grew ghost
lines. The token was scaled about the FRAME's centre and the plate about
the shape's, so the bolt and the ring sat lopsided in their holes, and the
silver was thick at one tip and a hairline at the next. One rule replaces
all of it: **a stroke is symmetric about its path, so a stroke of width 2r
painted with the fill covers exactly "within r outside the outline", and
the same stroke clipped to the outline covers exactly "within r inside
it".** Painted outermost first, those give every band as a ring of even
width round ANY shape, concave corners included (joins round). The order
is: the slot's lip, then its wall (for an empty slot, its floor in three
soft steps), then the token's shadow in the gap, then the keyline, the
enamel, the enamel's shade and light, the plate's dark edge, the channels,
the silver inside then outside the outline (one ramp in one space, so the
halves are one piece), then the rim's form. `BADGE_GEOM` holds every
proportion. The recipe is untouched (a dominant dark keyline, a broad
silver band, plates with their own dark edge, silver channels, a slot cut
to the outline). What is new is that each part is a surface lit from the
top-left:
- the rim is a rounded piece of polished metal: its outer slope catches
  the light at the top-left and turns away at the bottom-right, its inner
  slope the other way, with a crest between and one soft specular where
  the light is. It needed a ramp darker than instinct. The first one read
  as a white sticker outline;
- the enamel sits BELOW the rim, with the rim's shade along its top-left
  edge, a little light along its far edge, and one broad soft bloom at its
  top (a lacquer, never a streak);
- each channel is a bar of the same metal, lit on its top or left face,
  shading the enamel beside it. Every cut is a straight H or V line, so
  its ramp runs ACROSS it in user space (a ramp resolved against a line's
  own box is the zero-width trap);
- the token's dark edge carries on past the keyline along the
  bottom-right, which is what says it is raised. A LIGHT sliver there was
  tried and read as a second outline, the very ghost line being removed;
- the token and its slot both scale about the shape's own centre, so a
  seated badge has the same narrow gap all the way round.
- **A ring's shade cannot fade ACROSS its width**, only along the light, so
  the enamel's soft shade is NINE thin faint rings (each under a device
  pixel at 3x, a few levels deep). Three wide ones showed as three printed
  lines.
- **The uniform inset has a cost on thin shapes**: the bolt's lower plate
  and the star's arms lose enamel to the rim. `inner` is 4.4 for that
  reason, not the old ~5.8.
- Kept on purpose, and gated: no `<pattern>` (check_b242, "no printed
  grain"), the cast shadow's fill is still `rgba(0,0,0,.42)` (check_b242
  reads that literal), a grey badge has more than 12 paths and no unit
  colour anywhere in its markup, and an earned one has its colour
  literally (check_b314_chars). No filter, no gloss streak, no sparkle,
  no glass, no motif.
- **The frame holds what is drawn.** `badgeViewBoxFor` measures the
  outline (`badgeMeasure`, one layout for many) and grows the frame round
  the token and slot as scaled about the shape's centre, out to the lip.
  The trefoil and the quatrefoil still grow theirs; check_b270 holds it.
- `buildUnitBadgeSVG(u, true, { slot: false })` is the token alone, in the
  same frame: the cutscene's coin. Laid over a slot, it lands on it to the
  pixel.
- **The rim's spun finish exists only where a badge is drawn big
  (`opts.fine`)**: the cutscene's token and a badge's own card. It is
  fine rings round the shape's own centre (a repeating radial gradient,
  0.8 units, about 4% each way), reading as turned metal.
  - At the case's sizes, rings that fine would beat against the pixels,
    and straight grain across the colour was "printed stripes" in build
    242.
  - A coarser, stronger version (1.15-unit rings at 7%) was tried first
    and read as hatching.

**THE BRIEFCASE IS ONE OBJECT, IN THREE SIZES.** Its materials are defined
once, as tokens on `:root`, and every part of every case is drawn from
them:
- `--case-grain`: a 96px seamless PNG of pebbled leather (an emboss of
  blurred noise, generated once, about 7KB). It is an IMAGE, not an SVG
  filter;
- `--case-shell-bg` / `--case-shell-size`: the grain, the light falling
  across it, and the leather in the Next rank card's 160-degree light;
- `--case-trim`: aluminium for an edge or an opening, darker than the
  hardware (the polished ramp on a two-pixel edge read as a white
  outline) and NEUTRAL. It is a layer of the tray's own background, and
  check_b232 reads every colour in that background for blue: a
  steel-blue trim failed it;
- `--case-metal`: the hardware;
- `--case-lining-bg`: the neutral graphite lining (check_b232 still holds:
  no blue in it);
- `--case-lid-bg`: the lid's quilting.

The classes: `.nova-case` (the root), `.nova-case-shell`,
`.nova-case-trimmed` (a shell panel inside an aluminium edge),
`.nova-case-lining` (the lining inside its aluminium bead),
`.nova-case-lid`, `.nova-case-plate` (engraved: dark letters with a lit
lower lip), `.nova-case-latch` (with its catch), `.nova-case-hasp`,
`.nova-case-hinge` (a barrel with its knuckle joints) and
`.nova-case-handle` (leather on two mounts; it takes its `position` from
its context, because a shared `position:relative` threw the cutscene's
handle off the case). Each context sets only its geometry:
- **the cutscene**: the whole case in 3D, below;
- **the Badges tab**: the same case standing open. The lid sits behind the
  tray (its quilted lining, the plate, leaning towards you a little on
  `perspective(42rem) rotateX(-14deg)`), the hinges where it meets the
  tray, the tray of badges in its bead, the front with its two latches,
  and the handle folded down in front. Still exactly two spans in
  `.badge-case-front` (check_b242). Tapping a badge still opens its card
  (check_b317_badgecase);
- **the Profile card**: the same case, small and shut round its tray. Its
  shell has the trim and stitching, the strip of badges sits in the
  lining, two latches are on its front edge and the handle hangs under
  it. It keeps a gradient and a tinted border (check_b316_tiles) and its
  head row is untouched (check_b317_pfcard).

**THE CUTSCENE'S CASE IS A REAL BOX (`buildBadgeCase3D`) AND ITS LID STAYS.**
- **The structure.** `.bc-stage` holds the camera and the fade. Under it,
  `.bc-case` (preserve-3d) holds: a shadow on the table; the base's top
  (`.bc-tray`, trimmed shell) with the lining and the slots, and the
  hinges on its far edge; the front wall (`.bc-front`, hung from the
  tray's near edge by `rotateX(-90deg)`) with the latches; the handle,
  folded down in front at a third of the base's height; the light inside
  (`.bc-spill`); and the lid. The lid is hinged on the far edge with
  `transform-origin` at its top. Its outer shell is backface-hidden, with
  the plate. Its inside is a leather frame round a quilted pad with the
  "Badge case" plate, flipped by `rotateX(180deg)` so it faces you once
  the lid passes upright. It also has a front wall. Sizes are in the
  case's own width (`--cw`, `--ch`, `--d`, `--dl` on `.bc-scene`), so one
  set of numbers frames a phone and an iPad.
- **The open case is about 1.75 of its own width tall**, so the case and
  the token are sized by HEIGHT as well (`44vh`, `34vh`). It was checked
  open at 320x568, 375x667, 440x956, 834x1194, 844x390 and 1194x834. A
  phone held sideways has no room under the case, so `placeWords` puts
  the words beside it.
- **The camera.** Shut, it looks from the front and above at 52deg (the
  latches and the handle). As the lid swings back to 112deg it rises to
  21deg and pulls the case back (`--open-s`). The open lid STANDS behind
  the tray with its lining towards you, which is the briefcase feel. The
  latches' hasps flip out and down (`rotateX(-158deg)`), the lid cracks
  with the light spilling out of the gap, and the case gives a small thud
  when the badge seats.
- **NEVER FADE A preserve-3d ELEMENT.** An opacity below 1 (and a filter,
  `overflow:hidden`, a mask, `isolation`) flattens it, so the front wall
  and the lid fold flat into the case's plane for the length of the fade.
  The case fades on its STAGE and the token on its FLYER, both of which
  are flat parents of the 3D. check_b308_unlocks reads the case's
  EFFECTIVE opacity now, the product up its ancestors.
- Under 3D a slot's `getBoundingClientRect()` is its projected box, which
  is what the landing aims at.

**THE TOKEN (`buildBadgeCoin`) HAS AN EDGE.** Two faces with the edge
between them: `BC_EDGE_LAYERS` (20) copies of the silhouette in edge
metal, stacked through a thickness of 7% of the coin. Turned, it shows the
side of the metal the way a turning coin does. Edge-on it is a 35px band
on a Pro Max where a flat drawing was a hairline.
- **The faces and the slices are IMAGES of one drawing each** (a
  `data:` SVG), so twenty-two layers cost two decodes.
- **The edge is one colour, every slice.** Alternate slices a step apart (a
  milled coin's edge) were tried and read as a LADDER up the side of the
  token as it turned through 45-80deg, the "ridged" look this round was
  asked to remove. Twelve slices were tried too, and the gaps between
  them showed.
- **One angle curve drives everything that follows from the turn.** The
  angle eases out to rest facing you, and it is sampled into Web
  Animations for the spin, the floor shadow's width (`|cos|`, so the
  shadow narrows edge-on) and the light on each face (it crosses the face
  as the face turns through the light and is gone either side). The
  samples are linear between, so the four stay in step on the compositor
  (`bcSpinCoin`).
- **The light on a face is HTML, not the drawing.** It is a band behind a
  CSS mask of the token's silhouette (`badgeSilhouetteURL`), moved by a
  transform, so a turn never repaints a drawing.
- Its moments are: a spin up out of the dark (four turns over 3.4s), the
  glint once at rest, a sway (plus or minus 15deg) that shows its edge
  while it waits, a lift, waiting in front of the open lid, then the
  drop. The drop is a short rise, then down into the slot with one more
  flip and a tilt to lie in the tray (`rotateX(21deg)`, the camera's).
  It lands on the slot's own drawing (`flyInto` aims at the slot's svg,
  which shares the coin's frame). The seat follows: the slot takes the
  badge, a ring of light opens out, its glisten crosses it, the case
  thuds and the words come up under the case's handle (`placeWords`).
- **Longer, as asked: about 16.9s for one badge** (it was about 13.4).
  Each further badge in a run adds about 3.75s: a shorter spin at the
  lid, then its own drop.
- **A Web Animation filled forwards outlives the step that made it.**
  A run with two badges showed the second token sitting on the first
  one's slot, because the first flight held the flyer there over its
  inline position. `showCoin` cancels the flyer's animations first.
  Gated by a two-badge run on the fake clock.

**REDUCE MOTION GETS THE CASE, STILL.** The scene used to be skipped
outright. Now `playBadgeCaseScene` builds the case already open, with the
latches undone and the new badges seated and softly lit, names them,
holds `BC_STILL_MS` (4.6s) and ends; a tap ends it sooner. The results
screen's quiet path plays it once over the landed screen, but never on
the way back from the review (`opts.instant`), and Mute banners still
mutes it. **A `*` selector never reaches a `::before`**: the still scene
names the pseudo-elements, because the seated slot's glow is one.
- **The still scene does NOT hide the screen under it** (`bc-covering`).
  That class saves the painting under a moving scene, and nothing in the
  still scene moves. With it, check-results' type audit, which reads only
  visible text, found no numbers on the three screens it opened during
  those 4.6s.
- **A still scene played over the results ends with them**
  (`opts.alive`). Otherwise it would sit over whatever screen replaced
  the results.

**Gates.** `check_b317_badgecase` runs on a fake clock (the recorders'
method: every timer, frame and animation stepped and seeked), so load
cannot move a frame. On both reference devices it checks:
- the token keeps a band of edge at its most edge-on frame, more than the
  face's own width at that angle (`w/h >= aspect * |cos| + 0.045`);
- the lid is still there once the case has opened: opacity 1, at least
  30% of the tray's area, standing above it, and in pixels against the
  plain backdrop beside the case;
- the scene runs over 15s;
- the cutscene, the Badges tab and the Profile card are built from the
  same parts (a lining, two latches, a handle), with identical computed
  lining, latch, handle and leather;
- tapping a badge in the case still opens its card.

Then, for all sixteen badges: no LIGHT copy of the outline is drawn
shifted off it, and in pixels nothing light sits in the band just outside
a token's top-left edge (+61 levels on every badge of b6cd249; the worst
here is +12, the slot's own lip in a concave shape, so the bar is 20).
After that come a two-badge run and the Reduce motion still scene.
Against b6cd249, 14 of the 16 fail, the two-badge run included (its
second token sat on the first one's slot). The two that pass ("tapping
a badge still opens its card", on both devices) guard what was kept. check_b308_unlocks polls for the open case
instead of reading it at a fixed 8.4s, because the scene grew longer on
request. `tools/record-cutscenes.py` waits 17.8s for it now.

### Build 317, badge2 - badges struck, not drawn; the case's name on its side

Madison, after the briefcase round: *"not sure why when you open the case
the word badge case would be under the top, it should be on the side and
still be on the side as it opens and fully opens. I already told you the
badges need to look better, they also need to look better in the
cutscenes ... I feel like all the silver parts of the badges look
different/don't connect either, they also seem fake and have rough
edges!!! I've already said this though."*

**THE TOKEN IS RENDERED FROM A HEIGHT FIELD (`renderBadgeStrike`), and
no vector recipe could have fixed what he named.** Every silver part of
the band drawing was a gradient laid out by POSITION across that shape's
own box, so the light fell differently on every badge (a wide shape and a
tall one cannot match), and the channels were a second ramp that met the
rim at a step. Real metal is lit by which way its surface FACES. So:
- **One casting.** The rim's inner half and every channel rise by the
  same profile (flat polished top, chamfer, steep wall) from the same
  field - the distance to the enamel - so they are one piece by
  construction, with a cast fillet wherever they meet. The rim's outer
  half falls by the same profile to the outline.
- **Enamel below the metal**, at 38% of the rim's height, a slight
  meniscus up the walls, occluded at their foot and shaded where a wall
  stands between it and the light (a short ray-march).
- **One light.** Every surface is lit by its normal from one studio
  (`badgeLightTables`): a lit ceiling with a softbox edge across it, a dark
  horizon, a big softbox top-left, all in LINEAR light (values tuned as
  if they were sRGB came out white - 0.78 linear is 229 on screen). The
  face is very gently domed (`dome`), which is what makes a flat face
  show light giving way to shade - the cue that reads as polished metal.
- **Clean edges.** Every edge is antialiased from a distance field at the
  size it is SHOWN at (the signed-distance-font trick). The fields are
  computed once per shape at 288px (`badgeStrikeGeometry`: an exact
  feature transform to sub-pixel edge points from the canvas's own
  coverage, then lightly smoothed - unsmoothed, a diagonal edge left a
  ripple a sharp reflection drew as a dashed line), and a render at any
  size samples them, with normals by the chain rule.
- **No slivers.** The enamel is OPENED by 1.5 units (eroded, grown back):
  no cell thinner than 3 units survives - it becomes cast metal, walls and
  all - which also fillets every enamel corner. Doing that by colouring
  the sliver metal but keeping its walls left a trench with a ridge in it;
  the walls have to come from the distance to the OPENED enamel.
- **Two shapes changed for it.** The cross's arms are 36 wide, not 28 (28
  left 1-unit slivers either side of its channel), and the bolt has no
  channel (its middle band is 12 units tall, all rim anyway, and the cut
  only shrank the lower cell to a fleck).

**Rendered at the size it is shown, to 4 device pixels
(`badgeStrikeSize`).** A render scaled down by the browser (576 to 450)
turned a polished edge's one-pixel highlight into a dotted line. Each
`image.badge-raster` is measured after mount and re-rendered at its own
size (`badgeStrikeUpgrade`, a 12ms budget a frame); geometry for all
sixteen and the case-size renders are warmed in idle time 5s after
launch. Costs here: geometry ~30-40ms a shape once; a render ~12ms at
case size, ~40ms for a 700px coin face. The slot, the token's shadow
(check_b242's fill string) and the glisten stay vector. `data-enamel` on
an earned token's image is the colour it was rendered in; a grey one has
none - no unit colour reaches a badge not yet earned.

**The coin's face is the render at the coin's own device pixels
(`badgeCoinFaceURL`)**, and its twenty edge slices are each `scale(.988)`
of the face: exactly behind it, their half-covered edge pixels stacked
into one hard, stepped outline round the face at rest. The softness a 3D
layer adds (measured: the same face flattened is sharper) is the
compositor resampling a transformed layer; the old SVG face had it too.

**THE CASE'S NAME IS ON ITS SIDE, one plate in all three
(`buildCaseSidePlate`, `.nova-case-sideplate`).** The front wall between
the latches: on the cutscene's base (never in the lid, never under it),
on the Badges tab's front strip (the lid is plain quilting now), and on
the Profile card's front edge - whose "Badge case" heading over the tray
is gone for the same reason. In the cutscene the plate hangs from the
wall's top edge leaning 42deg: once the case is open the camera is 21deg
over it and the wall is nearly edge-on, and a plate flat on it shrank to
an unreadable sliver. It is a `<b>`, so the clasps stay the only spans in
a front (check_b242 counts two).

**Gates.** `check_b317_badge2` (16 checks, all 16 fail on 9e62633): the
plate's centre hit-tests to the plate at five moments from shut to fully
open, unsquashed, nothing in the lid saying it; the tab's and Profile's
plates are the same plate and nothing over their trays says it; every tab
badge and the coin face are rendered at their device pixels; along every
