channel from the badge's middle into its rim the metal has no step over
1.5 units (worst 6 levels; the old ramps stepped 90-220); no enamel cell
fails a 1.25-unit opening (worst 5%, the old cross 10%); and the coin at
rest gains no outline from its slices (47 changed pixels against 1299).
`check_b242` and the Profile squeeze check now read the name off the
case's side.

### Build 318 (builder f) - What's New, the challenge rows, the curve question, two touch bugs

- **What's New lost two rows**: *"remove the rank ups reimagined, the new
  badges and case thing"*. Gone from `showIntroPopup()` ("Rank-ups,
  reimagined", "New badges and case") and from `RELEASE_NOTES[0]`
  ("Rank-Ups, Reimagined", "New Badges, One Case"). Eight rows now: fits a
  17 Pro Max (card 83-901 of 956) and an iPad Pro 11; with the "Your level
  was adjusted" note the phone overlay scrolls (1161 of 956) and Got it is
  reachable.
- **A challenge row's two numbers are both its colour** (`.pf-now` and
  `.pf-need`, `--tc` at 85%), met or not: *"the number on the left can
  match actually, don't make it grey"*. Only the slash is quiet. This
  reverses 317's "grey on left"; check-curve asserts it.
- **No tests-left pill on the class card**: *"Remove the amount of tests
  left as well."* `testsRemaining()` stays (the calendar marks the days it
  counted). Section 104 now asserts the pill is absent.
- **"It took 50k XP to get level 80" is the curve, not a bug.** The figure
  is the Profile bar at the cap, "41,551 / 48,022 XP": XP since 80 against
  what an 81st level would cost (`topInto/topSpan`, build 317). The curve
  was build 313's when this was written (superseded the same round by
  b318g: 79->80 is 13,492 and 80 is 348,388 now): 79->80 cost 44,321, level 80 598,449 in all (21:
  9,912 · 30: 22,924 · 45: 58,046 · 50: 75,181 · 60: 138,980 · 70:
  281,237). The screenshot fixture carried 640,000 XP.
- **A swipe may start on a flashcard's words.** `.fc-text` is
  `overflow-y:auto`, so it is a scroll container, and touch-action only
  carries down to the nearest one: `.fc-mover`'s `pan-y` stopped at its
  edge and a horizontal drag on the text was a browser pan (pointercancel;
  in Chromium a swipe right even went Back in history). `.fc-text` carries
  `touch-action:pan-y` itself. Any new scrolling box inside the card needs
  the same, or swipes starting on it die.
- **A tap on the rising Next / See results always counts.** A click lands
  where the finger LIFTS; the button rises .62s, fast at first, so a finger
  down on its lower half for an ordinary 150ms tap lifted below it and the
  tap was lost (reproduced: lower-edge taps 1.02-1.10s after answering, held
  180ms, all missed). `render()` now takes a press on `#nextbtn` that lifts
  as a tap (under 12px, not cancelled) off the button's current box;
  `tapTook` swallows the native click if one also arrives. Taps that start
  BEFORE the button is on screen (the first .78s it is below the fold at
  opacity 0) still do nothing, by design.
- **Gates.** check-behaviour `318f-a` (swipe on the text both ways, both
  reference devices; an overflowing question still scrolls - fail on
  219bfea) and `318f-b` (the rise paused part-way with its own Web
  Animation, finger down near the bottom edge, rise finished under it,
  finger up: results must open - fails on 219bfea; a settled tap still
  moves exactly one question).
### Build 318 (b318d) - planet taps that keep going, the scar with the planet, the daily button's colour, one chat button

**A planet tap speeds the rings' OWN spin up; nothing is laid on top of
it** (`orbitBoostKick` / `orbitBoostStep`, beside `planetTapFx`). *"If I
spam the big planet make it so that it just does it over and over again
seamlessly with that tiny speed up thing."* Build 317's surge was a Web
Animation of each ring's `rotate`, forward a few degrees and given back
to 0 over nine seconds; spammed, ten restarts piled up ~50/100 degrees
that were then given back, so the rings ran BACKWARDS (-0.86x) for
seconds, and every restart jumped the speed ~4x in one frame. Now:
- one velocity `w` (in multiples of each ring's own pace, so the inner
  ring stays quicker) eases towards a drive `u` (`tauW` .12s); a tap moves
  `u` 62% of the way to the cap (6) - every tap counts, none can run away;
  `u` decays (`tauU` .42s). One tap is ~3.3x at its peak and gains ~1.5
  lap-seconds (~5 degrees outer, ~11 inner - what 317's tap gave);
- `w` is applied as the `playbackRate` of the rings' `cosmic-orbit-spin`
  AND of the scar veils timed to them (`cof-scarpass`) -
  `ORBIT_PHASE_ANIMS`. Setting playbackRate keeps currentTime, so the
  position is continuous by construction. The loop runs only while a
  boost is above zero (~2s after the last tap);
- **nothing is given back.** What the rings gained is `orbitAdvanceMs`,
  and `syncLoopClock` adds it to those two animations only, so a Home
  built again puts the rings where they were left. It is READ OFF the
  spin when a boost ends (its currentTime against syncLoopClock's own
  clock), not only summed per frame: the sum ran 0.2-1.3s of lap short
  under a busy main thread, which re-entry showed as the rings stepping
  back 4-9 degrees. (A give-back is what
  makes a sustained spin run backwards; there is no give-back fast enough
  to be invisible and slow enough not to.)
- Reduce motion: no spin, nothing to speed up. Taps on flares, bubbles
  and secret flares under the glass are untouched (paint order).
Measured, 10 taps in 2s, every frame, five themes (default, Gold,
Supernova, the orange rings, the black rings): never below 1.0x, peak
~4.9x, per-frame speed change <=0.83x (66ms frames), max per-frame angle
step 0.25 degrees outer / 0.57 inner at 60fps, back to 1.0x after.
Gate: `check_b318_planet` (fails on 219bfea); `check_b317_hometaps` now
reads the spin's playbackRate rather than a rotate animation.

**The scar, the soot and the plasma settle with the planet** (B2).
`.cosmic-hero-svg` fades in over its first ~100ms (`cosmic-hero-settle`)
on every arrival; the HTML laid over it (`.cosmic-scar`, `.csc-ringsoot`,
`.cosmic-plasma`) had no settle, so a Supernova account saw the crack
float on nothing for ~100ms every time Home came up. They take
`cosmic-hero-settle-in` - same length and curve, NO 100% keyframe (each
ends on its own opacity: the plasma's .55) and `backwards` fill (nothing
held afterwards, so the rank cutscene's own opacity on the scar is
untouched). The flares, bubbles and debris on the orbit layers still do
NOT fade on a return (build 314, "the rings do not blink") - the debris
rides with the flares. Gate: `check_b318_scar`, frame-stepped.

**The daily button is the rank's own colour, `--dq-c`.** Every ring,
glow and flare on it (and the orb that leaves it) used `--theme-c1`,
which in a rank's triad is the warm HIGHLIGHT next to the rank colour -
Supernova's is yellow. `--dq-c: var(--rank-accent, var(--theme-c1))`:
the rank colour where a rank theme is set, the default's gold where not.
The seal (`dq-sealed`) lost its `brightness(1.7)`, which clipped every
colour towards white (Bronze went yellow, Sapphire cyan). Gate:
`check_b318_daily`. `.daily-question-fab.is-fresh` is styled but nothing
adds the class any more (the recharge replaced it).

**One chat button on the race leaderboard.** *"Leaderboard has two chat
buttons."* The main Leaderboard tab always had one; it was the Virtual
Room's leaderboard cutscene, where the Room chat button becomes a circle
(phone CSS, so it clears "RACE RESULTS") with the dock's own glyph, right
beside the dock's circle. While `#vroom-race-cut` is up and a
`#roomchat-fab` exists, the dock's button is hidden and the room's takes
its corner (CSS only, by `:has`). The room's results screen keeps both -
there the room's is a labelled "Room chat" pill, a different control,
which build 194 allows. Gate: `check_b318_one_chat` counts visible
buttons carrying the chat glyph on Home, four Profile tabs, Settings,
every Leaderboard board and re-entry, the race leaderboard and Home after
it (fails on 219bfea: two on the race leaderboard).

### Build 318 (b318g) - the XP curve fitted to the class

*"Most people don't have 50000 xp yet.. we need to find the average user
and make the xp curve based on them ... maybe the xp total should only be
changed after level 60 so people aren't affected? ... do the math"*

- **SUPERSEDED the same day (Oct 10) - the curve now eases from 50.**
  Madison: *"I want top 25 percent to reach level 100 by May. I'd want most
  people at or very close to 100 by July 8th."* Measured on the class
  (33 people with 2,000+ XP and 2+ study days; pace = mean of pace since
  Sep 22 and pace over the last 12 days), the top quarter hold ~410k XP on
  May 1 and the middle person ~327k on Jul 8. With 1-60 frozen that cannot
  be met: 40 levels at no less than level 60's 8,914 is already ~495k. So
  **1-50 are build 313's to the point and past 50 each level costs
  `LEVEL_EASE_STEP` (0.1%) x (level - `LEVEL_EASE_FROM` = 50) more than the
  one before.** 60: 116,042 · 70: 161,659 · **80: 217,910** · 90: 294,417 ·
  **100: 409,117** (100 alone 14,006). `LEVEL_TOP_*` is gone.
  Nobody SHOWS above 49 (badge wall), so no shown level moved - checked on
  all 57 live accounts; two just bank more saved levels.
  Projected (central pace): top quarter at 100 Apr 4 (Apr 20 on the slower
  12-day pace); on Jul 8 the middle person ~93, 14 of 33 at 100, 16 within
  5. The bottom ~40% study far less (p25 ~430 XP/day) and land ~61-73 - no
  curve reaches them without the top finishing by Christmas. **Re-fit
  81-100 in January** with real pace data; nobody can hold them until
  `LEVEL_CAP` is 100, so it moves nobody. Scripts: scratchpad `curve319/`.
- **Why 60, measured (one read-only pass, Oct 9, 57 onboarded accounts):**
  the highest level anyone held was 56 (108,670 XP), so nobody moved, and
  every level past 60 is cheaper than before, so somebody crossing 60 on
  the old build before updating can only gain. The 32 active accounts
  (>= 2,000 XP, >= 2 days of 5+ minutes, studied since Oct 2, duplicate
  sign-ups out): median 22,843 XP, ~1,000-1,400 XP a calendar day (last
  12 days ~630), 0 badges; p90 ~75,000 at ~4,500 a day. Badge work runs
  at ~25,000 XP per badge-equivalent across the class.
- **What it was fitted to**: at ~25k XP a badge the 14th badge lands on
  level 80, so Supernova's two halves arrive together for an average
  player (313 had them at level 73, 250k short). Projected at the class's
  pace: the median ~55 by Dec 17, ~61 by Jan 25, ~80 at the course end
  (Jul 8); the top 10% reach 80 in early December and 100 in spring.
  "Supernova's level by the end of the current content" for the AVERAGE
  player is not reachable without lowering levels below 60, which would
  lift most of the class - said to Madison rather than built.
- **JANUARY IS ONE CONSTANT: `LEVEL_CAP = 100`.** 81-100 are already on
  the curve; nothing below 81 moves (check-curve 4b serves a copy with
  only that line changed). The two new ranks are a separate edit to
  `TIER_UNLOCKS`/`TIER_ORDER_FULL`. Until the cap moves nobody can HOLD
  81-100, so `LEVEL_EASE_STEP` can still be re-tuned before January
  without moving anyone - re-measure the class first. After January,
  treat every level up to the cap as frozen like 1-60 are now.
- **Re-fitting later**, the method: read each onboarded account
  once (`studyLog` = minutes per day, `weekPoints`/`prevWeekPoints` = XP
  per week), take the highest level held, freeze through it, and make
  every level above it cheaper - that is the only direction that cannot
  take a level off anybody.

### Build 318, badges round - sampled, not stepped; enamel that is metal; one square case

Madison: *"where the color meets the silver part is rough and not smooth,
the edges of the badge aren't smooth ... the corners of the case don't
look good, you can see where it disconnects on the top and bottom ... the
badge case placard is glitched ... all the badges need a smidge of glow
... The cutscene has a square brief case which is great. All the other
ones are different shapes ... the colored part doesn't look like a nice
metal."*

**THE ROUGHNESS WAS SAMPLING, NOT GEOMETRY.** The distance fields were
clean. The enamel's wall is ~1.3 units wide (under 3 device pixels on a
case-sized badge) and its light turns over across it, so ONE sample per
pixel landed on the lit or the dark side at random along the seam: a
dashed, stepped dark line. The rim's crest highlight did the same, and on
the coin the outer wall stepped along every diagonal. `renderBadgeStrike`
now averages SS x SS samples per pixel in linear light (`ssMin` 2, up to
`ssMax` 3, enough for `ssK` ~3.4 samples per token unit: 3 on the Profile
strip, 2 elsewhere). Two more causes, each visible only once the first
was gone:
- the light tables were read NEAREST-neighbour; on a reflective face the
  256-step grid printed as mottling. They are read bilinearly;
- the heights and edges came from the RAW fields (only the normals were
  smoothed), and on the coin - rendered ~4.6x finer than the 288px fields
  - the field's own sub-pixel ripple drew a wavy seam round every plate.
  The smoothed fields carry everything now.
Cost, measured here: ~20ms a case-sized badge, ~10ms a Profile one,
~110ms the coin (was ~40). Nine buffers are reused across renders
(`badgeStrikeBuffers`) - allocating them per render was most of the first
version's ~1s coin. The coin's face and the open case's badges are
rendered in idle time while the results screen reveals
(`warmBadgeCoinFaces`), not as the scene starts.
- **A draft first, the finish in idle time.** Anything built
  synchronously (`badgeStrikeImage`: a tab, a case, a cutscene) gets a
  one-sample-a-pixel draft at once - what every badge was before - and
  the supersampled finish swaps in a moment later, one badge per idle
  slice (`badgeStrikeEntry(.., draft)`, `badgeStrikeFinish`,
  `BADGE_STRIKE_DRAFTS`). The first render of a session runs before the
  engine has compiled the loop: ~0.5s here for one badge as the Home
  badge cutscene began. `badgeStrikeURL` (the coin, the warm-ups) still
  renders the finish there and then. **A check that reads badge pixels
  waits for `BADGE_STRIKE_DRAFTS.size === 0`** (b317_badgecase and
  b317_badge2 do now).
- **The default and warm-up size is the tab's tile** (`badgeDefaultPx`:
  5.4rem, 6.6rem from 40rem), so the warm-up renders what the tab asks
  for; the iPad's 212px tiles missed the old 92px warm-up by more than the
  cache's 8%. The Home badge cutscene's art is given its stage's size
  (`min(13rem, 46vw)`, 16rem wide): measured on screen it was caught
  mid-entrance at scale(1.5).
- `check_cutscene`'s "the second follows it" is a ~0.5s budget on real
  time and fails on 219bfea too when the machine is loaded (load average
  ~15 here: failed 1 of 3 runs against 219bfea).

**A SEATED BADGE IS RENDERED FOR THE OPEN CASE (`badgeCaseSlotPx`).** The
case's slots took the default size and were re-measured under 3D while
the case was shut and tilted, so the open case drew a ~276px render into
a ~194px hole. A browser shrinking an image by a quarter SAMPLES it, and
the keyline came out a dotted ring. The size is now the CSS's own --cw
sum times `--open-s`. (Headless Chromium still stipples the open case a
little: that is its compositor resampling the 3D layer, and it shows
the same with the badge drawn flat. Flattened, the badges are clean.)

**THE ENAMEL IS COLOURED METAL** (`enDome`, `enTilt`, `enRamp`, `enMetal`,
`enDiff`, `coatK` in `BADGE_STRIKE`). It was the unit colour times a
diffuse shade, flat as paint. Its face is domed a little more than the
rim and its tilt towards the light is read through a polished ramp
(bright top-left, a dark band, picking up off the floor) - smooth,
because the dome is - with a little of the flat colour kept so the dark
band stays the unit's colour. No streak, no motif: the light is the
dome's. Same colour family per unit, same shapes.

**ONE SQUARE CASE (`--case-r` .2rem, `--case-r-in` .32rem).** The 3D case's
tray and lid were rounded 1.05rem in plan and its walls hung straight
down from them, so each wall's square end stuck out past the tray's
curve: a notch at all four corners. A box's walls can only meet a top
that is square where they meet it. Every wall (`.nova-case-wall`: the
cutscene's front and lid front, the tab's front, the Profile's front)
carries an aluminium corner guard on each end (`--case-guard`, two
pseudo-elements, so the clasps stay the only spans in a front).
- **The Badges tab** is the cutscene's open case drawn flat, part for
  part: the lid (a trimmed shell framing its quilted `.badge-case-pad`),
  the hinges, the tray (`.badge-case-tray`, a trimmed shell round the
  lining), the front wall, the handle. The root `.badge-case` holds no
  paint; it is the footprint.
- **The Profile case** is the same case from above, small: the tray (the
  button: square, gradient, tinted edge, black shadow) with the count on
  its rim, and the front wall hung OUTSIDE its border with the guards,
  latches and plate, the handle under the wall with its mounts behind
  it. The placard was "glitched" because the latches, plate and handle
  were all pinned ACROSS the tray's bottom border, the handle's two
  mounts poking up round the plate. `check_b289`'s "the case keeps the
  Next rank card's corner" is revised: it keeps the briefcase's.

**A SMIDGE OF GLOW.** An earned badge on the tab and on the Profile strip
has two CSS drop-shadows in its own colour (`--badge-glow`), a close one
and a wider breath. Still elements, so rasterised once; never an SVG
filter.

**Gates.** `check_b318_badges` (fails on 219bfea): renders sampled
against a 4x reference, enamel that changes across its face, the case's
corners and parts, the Profile wall and plate, the glow, and the seated
badges' render size.

### Build 319, badges round - one open case, found not unlocked, a soft seam, seated, nothing shown until found

Madison: *"when the case opened, the inside of the case was shining purpose,
seems like the timing was wrong on the glow ... Within the badge case it has
the word mastered under it, that shouldn't be right there, that should say
that when you click the badge for details and you did master it. The title of
the badge should say badge at the end though ... where the color meets the
silver looks rough ... it's still missing that look like it's sitting inside
of the missing spot, AND the ones you don't have should not be there ... the
top of the case looks weird. I see the hinges but then yeah it cuts off ...
the badge cutscene shows a great case, and then the profile makes it
elongated and the badge tab makes it different too ... it should be 'found'
badge instead of unlocked badge."*

> **Supersedes** build 314's grey badge (a badge not yet earned "seen, not
> shown") and build 318's tab and Profile case geometry.

- **ONE OPEN CASE (`buildOpenBadgeCase(kind, cellFor)`, `.ncase`).** The
  Badges tab and the Profile draw the cutscene's case as it stands at the end
  of the scene, flat, part for part and in its measured proportions: the lid
  standing behind (`aspect-ratio 1/.8`, leaning a little towards you so its
  top is wider, as the cutscene's is), hinges on the seam, the tray
  (`1/.88`) with sixteen slots four by four, the front wall (guards, two
  latches, the plate), the handle. Every size is in `cqw`: the root is its own
  container, so the two places are one drawing at two widths (`--ncase-w`:
  25rem/31rem on the tab, 13rem/17rem on the Profile). **Only the lid may
  carry a 3D transform**: a badge under one is resampled by the compositor
  (build 318). The parts keep their old class names (`badge-case-*` on the
  tab, `pf-case-front`/`pf-strip`/`badge-strip-cell` on the Profile), so the
  older gates still find them; the old 242/244/318 rules for those names are
  overridden by `.nova-case.ncase ...`, not edited.
- **Nothing is written in the case.** The tab's slots carry no name and no
  "Mastered"/"5/15"; the name is an `.sr-only` span and the slot's
  `aria-label`. A tap opens the badge's card: "Mastered" there (the shared
  card says "Unlocked" for everything else), or "5 of 15".
- **A BADGE NOT FOUND IS ITS EMPTY SLOT, everywhere** - the tab, the
  Profile, its card (`buildUnitBadgeSVG(u, false)`), the results' progress
  box (3rem there so the outline reads). Build 314's `"grey"` token is no
  longer drawn anywhere; the option still exists in the builder.
- **Titles end in "Badge"** (`badgeTitle(unit)`): the card, the cutscene,
  the results' rows, the reduced-motion banner. **Badges are found**: BADGE
  FOUND in both cutscenes, "Badge found" on the results (and the results'
  card is headed "Found" when it holds only badges), "7 badges found" on the
  tab. What earns a badge is unchanged.
- **THE SEAM (`wallMax`, `eOff` in `BADGE_STRIKE`).** The rough edge was a
  black hairline with a white one beside it round every plate: the wall's foot
  was near vertical (`pow(.., .55)` has infinite slope at the foot), so its
  normal reflected the studio's dark horizon, and a ring of bare metal floor
  sat between the wall and the colour. The inner wall now leans at most
  `wallMax` (.22) and the colour runs up to where the wall meets its level
  (`eOff` .5 units). The outer rim is untouched.
- **SEATED.** `BADGE_GEOM.gap` 1.7 -> 2.6 and `lip` 1.2 -> 1.5, so the hole
  shows round a badge; the far wall is lit (`-wall` ramp up to `#46525F`);
  and the hole's edge throws a shade on the badge's top-left edge in three
  masked steps (`BADGE_SEAT_SHADE`, `.badge-seat-shade` rects - masks, not
  filters). The glow in the case is lower (`.ncase-cell.is-earned svg`): a
  strong halo round the slot lifted the badge out of it.
- **THE CASE'S LIGHT (`.bc-spill`) IS THE LIGHT THROUGH THE CRACK.** It sat
  at the tray's far edge (under the lid, never seen through the crack) and
  held at .95 for .5s after the lid began to swing, then took 1.2s to go: the
  opening lid uncovered a tray washed in the badge's colour. It is centred at
  the near edge now and fades in .3s as the lid starts to open.

**Gates.** `check_b319_badges` (fails on 8aded7f): the seam metric (every
metal-to-colour step on every badge, rows and columns, at 264px: 8aded7f's
worst 10th percentile .27, now >= .88), gap and seat shade, no token for a
badge not found on the tab / Profile / card / results, nothing written in
the case, Mastered and "... Badge" on the cards, found not earned, the tab's
and the Profile's case the same open case in the same proportions (lid >= .6
of the tray; four by four), and the spill >= .5 through the crack and <= .05
.5s after the lid opens.

### Build 318 - the secret flares: their moment on the results, owed until seen, the next one's rumour, Umbra's eclipse

Madison: *"the cutscene is happening from the main menu and so are the
popups. Those need to happen from the result screen ... cutscene first,
then the pop up that you found it ... cutscene, flare, and then
character"*; *"The popup for the next flare should not mention what level
it appears at"*; *"for the character you are closest to only ... 'they say
these are seen in tests when level blah blah' ... if you haven't unlocked
void then the others wouldn't give the hint"*; *"Umbra cutscene ... at the
very beginning the flare goes to the moon but that's kinda confusing ...
when all the secret flares float around umbra, when they get to the front
they are cutoff"*.

- **Where a find plays.** In the code the results screen already played
  the scenes - the pack recordings had played them over Home, which is
  what he saw. What was really wrong: the 3rd-6th went card, scene,
  character (build 241), and a find was LOST whenever its results never
  ran (Exit test, the app closed, a resumed run - `mysteryFoundThisSession`
  was reset on resume) apart from the character's card on Home.
- **Order on a results screen**: the hundo effect, the badge case, the
  rank-up and its reward card, the other cards, then the find LAST: its
  scene, the "Secret flare found" card, the character it completes, that
  character's banner. One builder for the find's cards
  (`flareFoundItem`, `flareFindCharacter`, `flareCharacterItem`) serves
  the results and Home.
- **Owed until seen** (`oweFlareFind` / `markFlareFind` /
  `flareFindsOwed`, localStorage `class26e.flarefinds.owed`, entries
  `{c, all, s}`): written the moment the flare is tapped; `s` 1 once its
  scene has played, 2 once its card has been up `SPOT_SEEN_MS` (in
  `playUnlockSpotlight`'s markSeen, like every other card) while the
  character it completes is still to be announced; the entry goes when
  that character's card is seen (`flareFindCharacterSeen`), or at once
  muted / after Reduce motion's still scene (stage 3). A flare character
  is never in Home's ordinary list (`HOME_UNLOCK_SKIP`), so without this a
  results screen cut between the two cards lost the character's card. Device-local on
  purpose, like the run session: on `store` it would sync and a second
  device would play the scene too. Entries for a flare the account does
  not hold are ignored (a reset, another account linked). Whatever is
  owed plays on the next Home through `playHomeUnlocks`, after the other
  cards and before the "out there" hint: a `flare-scene` pseudo-item,
  then the flare's card, then its character and banner (held back from
  the ordinary list so they follow it). A resumed run carries
  `flareFound` in its session and announces the find on its own results.
- **B4 / `pendingVoidCutscene`**: `playVoidCutscene` is deleted. showHome
  turns the stored flag into an owed Void find; the queue plays it one
  card at a time and announces Void's banner. **One Home queue at a
  time**: `playHomeUnlocks` waits while another is running
  (`homeUnlockActiveAt`, taken as over after 35s quiet) - a second
  showHome() used to start a second queue in the 320ms gap after a
  scene, which stacked the card.
- **The Virtual Room** goes through the same results sequence;
  `VROOM_SCENE_SELECTOR` now names `.sf-scene` so the leaderboard never
  rolls over a find.
- **The "is out there" cards name no level** (Genesis's said "from level
  78"). **The next flare's caption on Home is the one hint**
  (`homeTapCopyFlare`, flareHuntState "next"/"hunting"): "They say this
  one is seen in tests from level N." at the account's own drawn level
  (`mysteryLevelGate`), or "...has been seen in tests at your level." once
  reached. Every other unfound flare still says only "Secret flare has
  not been found."; no name, no colour for any unfound one.
- **Umbra's opening**: no flare flying from a corner to touch a lit moon.
  Penumbra lights in the middle of the dark (`.sfu-flare`, `sf-flarein`),
  ignites, and swells into a violet SUN (`.sfu-moon.sfu-sun`, no craters;
  `sf-touch`); a dark moon (`.sfu-occult`, a body outside the sun's disc,
  seen against its glow) slides across it from 3.7s and the sun dims as
  it is swallowed ("The moon swallows its light"). Beads, the diamond,
  totality and everything after are unchanged and keep their times.
- **The ring flares were cut in two ways** (all four ring scenes):
  `.sf-orbit`'s clip was `inset(50% 0 0 0)` in the plane's unsquashed box,
  and a flare sits ON the box's edge at the front, back and ends -
  counter-squashed to ~5x its height in plane units - so the near flare
  was cut in half at the plane's bottom edge (the far one at its top,
  the end ones down the middle). Only the 50% line is a real cut now;
  the other edges stand off (`inset(50% -15% -60% -15%)`). And on a phone
  the ring (124% of the stage, 513px on a 440px screen) ran off both
  sides; it is `min(124%, 100vw - 9cqw - 1rem)` now (iPad unchanged).
- **Gate: `check_b318_flares`** (check-behaviour), all against 219bfea:
  the order on a real run for red/yellow/violet/white/core and with a
  badge and a rank-up; owed at the find, nothing owed after; a real
  relaunch mid-scene plays scene/card/character on Home once and nothing
  on the launch after; B4 (most cards up at once = 1, Void's banner
  shown); no level in the hint cards; the captions; Umbra's opening
  geometry; every ring flare through a lap on both reference devices
  (`B318_ORBIT_JS`: each flare's core mapped into its plane's own box
  against the clip, and against the screen); the Virtual Room selector;
  a resumed run keeping its find. check_b317_sflare's flow and Home-path
  assertions and check_b317_hometaps' unfound-caption assertion moved to
  the new decisions.


### Build 318 - every character's 100 is a celebration; the Ninja redrawn

*"Idk if it's just the ninja character or if it's all, but the Hundo
result screen, I don't like the ninja things it gets a hundred ... each
character should use its unique cool celebration"* and *"ninja character
looks a smidge rough around the edges."*

**What a 100 is on the results character:** its own reaction from the
table (`tools/reactions-table.py`, ~2s), then its special
(`CHAR_SPECIAL_DRAW`, `charSpecialFire(av, 2600)` in the results
reaction). Nothing was shared: every character already had its own
reaction. But the five starters had NO special, so their 100 stopped
after the reaction while the other 25 put on a show; and the Ninja's
reaction was the weakest in the set (below).
- **The five starters have specials now** (`Object.assign(CHAR_SPECIAL_DRAW,
  ...)` after the table, keyframes in the `STARTER SPECIALS (build 318)`
  CSS block, lengths in `CHAR_SPECIAL_MS`): Ninja - a katana rises at
  the shoulder, a glint runs up it, one red-white cut sweeps under the
  mask, leaves fly; Ghost - three little ghosts circle its shoulders
  (`spOrbit`), then a BOO bubble; Wizard - a magic circle draws itself
  behind him (`sp-draw` on `pathLength=100` paths) and turns, runes
  light, the orb charges and the circle flares; Grizzly - a salmon leaps
  from a splash and he catches it; Alien - a saucer swoops in and beams
  a cow up. Like every special they also fire now and then on the
  Profile card and Customize.
- **The Ninja's 100 is a smoke bomb**: a ray burst at the chest, one
  cloud, the ninja gone inside it and back on top of it, wisps and its
  own scene's leaves thrown out, a glint off the band's plate.
- **`puff()` puts the opacity on the GROUP, never on each disc.** Eleven
  discs each at .5 opacity printed a darker lens at every overlap - that
  is what read as "the ninja things", a heap of grey bubbles. Same flaw,
  fixed by the same change, in Wizard/Solar/Inferno fail props and the
  breath puffs.
- **The Ninja's drawing:** the hood was a seven-cornered polygon, the
  pale wrap band painted PAST the hood's outline on both sides, the
  headband was a bar floating on the forehead with its tails a gap away,
  and the eye slit a hard hexagon. Now one curved hood, the band and its
  light clipped to the hood (`clip-path`, static) so they end exactly on
  its edge, a knot where the band meets the edge with the tails out of
  it, a rounded slit. Same parts and classes, same head size (97 passes).
- Gate: `check_b318_celebrations` - every live character runs its own
  reaction keyframes AND has a special (cx-sp at opacity 0, 4+ finite
  animations under `.char-special`, 1.5-4.5s in `CHAR_SPECIAL_MS`, 3+
  shapes showing part-way); no two celebrations (reaction + special) and
  no two specials alike; no reaction prop is translucent overlapping
  discs; nothing on the Ninja's hood paints outside it (436px on
  219bfea, 0 now); a real 12/12 drill as the Ninja on the iPhone lands
  `rx-ninja` and then `char-special`; no special lays a flat fill over
  the whole drawing. Fails on 219bfea (7 checks).
- **A special's frame-wide light or dark is a ROUND gradient, never a
  flat fill over the box.** The results character's svg is a square
  inside a round frame, so Umbra's and Void's "lights go out" (a flat
  disc of r 20) and Zeus's flash (a 37-unit rect) showed as hard squares
  in the circle on a 100. They are r 17-17.5 discs, solid to ~72%, gone
  by the edge.

### Build 319 (b319e) - the daily button's row, its charge, Horizon's brow, the level note

- **The daily "?" is 6.8rem off the bottom on a phone (was 6.3).** *"The
  yellow pulse just barely touches the button tab."* The button cleared
  the bar by 12px, but its ready ring (`::after`, inset -3px, up to
  x1.35) reaches 13.6px past it, so at its widest it ran 1-1.4px into the
  bar on every phone. Lifted 8px it clears by 6.6-7px on all fourteen
  phone combinations; Start Studying does not move (it sits beside the
  "?", not over it). **Measure the ring, not the button**: check-fixes 9c
  samples the ring across its keyframes where it is visible and wants 4px.
  check-fixes takes `--against` now.
- **The "done" bubble's band asks above/below by a blocker's MIDDLE.**
  With the "?" lifted, Start Studying's foot passed the "?"'s centre line
  on a Pro Max, so by edges it was neither above nor below it, the band
  between it and the bar forgot it, and the bubble went up over the
  button (check-fixes 9b: 39px off).
- **The charge stands above the tab bar while it plays**
  (`.daily-question-fab.is-charging{z-index:201}`). *"The daily question
  loading circle, at the bottom it looks like it's cut off halfway and
  doesn't connect."* The meter itself was whole; the two rings that leave
  it (x2.3, x3.1) slid under the bar's glass (150 under 200), so they came
  out open at the bottom (on the iPad, the left side). Everything in the
  charge is pointer-events:none and the button never meets the bar, so
  nothing on the bar loses taps. Gate: `check_b319_daily` (pixel diff over
  the bar at 5.1s).
- **A special's parts that belong to the FACE go in `T.head`.** `T.front`
  lies over the whole drawing, but the head is fitted afterwards
  (`AVATAR_HEAD_SCALE` everywhere, `SIL_HEAD_FIT` on a cut-out), so
  Horizon's special drew the hole and the flare at the brow's raw (20, 15)
  - 1.6-1.9 units above his real brow, on the mask's top edge: *"his
  secret flare ... was not on forehead where it should be, it was like in
  his hair."* `T.head` is a `cx-sp` group appended last inside `.cx-head`,
  so every fit and every head motion carries it. Gate: `check_b319_horizon`
  (drawing, picker, cut-out, both scene copies, live on Profile).
  **Genesis and Void still anchor on raw coordinates**: Genesis's dive
  lands ~1.2 units under its planet's centre (head x1.1 about y 31.5), Void
  ~0.6 under its face. Not reported; move their face parts to `T.head` if
  they are.
- **"Your level was adjusted" is `levelGateNoteText(s)`**, two short
  paragraphs: levels now unlock one rank at a time; level N is the top
  level for <held rank> (or "before your first rank"), so your level went
  from A to N; you kept all of your XP and it still counts; earn K (more)
  badges to reach <next rank>; the next levels unlock then and your XP
  counts toward them right away. The old copy opened with "to keep leveling
  up, you now need the badges", which read as "badges to level up at all".
  Gate: `check_b319_levelnote` (0, 1 and 4 badges; nobody under the cap).
- **Penal Code #346, choice D: `"Manslaughter."`** (a slide's page number
  "1" had come in with it), asked for by name in the 319 list - the one
  exception to the 6 Oct "exactly like the study guides" rule above, which
  had reverted this very repair. **Choice text IS part of identity**: KEYS
  hashes `keyText || q` plus `keyChoices || choices`, so the question
  carries `keyChoices` with the original four and its key stays
  `Penal Code|346|243n1v`. `check_b319_penal346` loads 8aded7f beside the
  build and wants all 898 KEYS byte-identical and no other question
  changed; `check_b313_shuffle`'s "no keyChoices that differ" allows
  exactly this one.

### Build 319 (b319b) - a pale charge that starts the spin, an after-glow that cools, the shine broken by the blast

**The charge before the whirl is PALE again, and TIMED to the spin**
(supersedes build 318's "in the rank's colour"). Madison: *"The charge up
for the flare needs to be pale, and it needs to be timed. It needs that
feeling like oh that flare just made it spin."*
- `RANK_CHG_PALE` (#EEF3FA) for the charge and its release; `flareFx(cls,
  nRings, color)` sets `--chg` on its own layers (and the slot). The
  after-glow and the pulse at the stop keep the rank's colour.
- Nine rings now (`RANK_CHG_IN`), the LAST landing at offset 1 = T.ignite;
  the bubble squeezes to .88 over the last ~250ms. The charge's animations
  `fill:forwards` and `release()` - called first thing in the T.ignite
  callback - cancels them and takes the layers off in the same frame, so
  the release is on the whirl's first frame however the timers land. Its
  fallback is `release(true)` at D+600. Cancel matters: the squeeze's
  forwards fill on the slot's `transform` would come back the moment the
  whirl's own transform animation ended.
- The release: a pale flash in the bubble, two waves (`.rank-chg-wave`,
  gradient rings drawn at FULL size and scaled up from the last ring's
  1.18 bubbles - never a border scaled up), and the bubble springing out of
  the squeeze on the `scale` property (composes with the whirl's turn).
- **The whirl leaves with a push**: `RANK_CUTSPIN_KICK` (.14 of the top
  speed) at its first frame instead of t-squared from a standstill (17
  degrees in the first 0.1s, was 0.9). The speeding-up is
  `a u + (1 - a) u^2`, a = 2K/(1+K), as `ACC_EASE`; `PEAK_DEG` is rescaled
  so the speed stays continuous at the peak; `vh(u)` starts at KICK. Same
  times, same turns, ~6% lower top speed.
- **The after-glow was there all along and nobody saw it**: it lived in the
  new flare's SLOT, and the whirl faded that slot to .06 - so for the first
  ~2s of the slowing it showed at 6%. The new flare's BUBBLE melts now
  (the other slots still fade whole). The after-glow: a wider corona of the
  rank's colour holding full for the first third and easing to .3 by the
  stop (the pulse at the stop now starts from .3), and a white-hot core
  over the glass (`.rank-chg-hot`) fading out in the first ~2/3 - white,
  to the colour, to dim: "bright and slowly cool down".
- **Gate** (`check_b317_evolve`, four new assertions, all fail on 8aded7f):
  the charge pale (every channel 215+, within 30) and not the rank colour;
  the last ring still closing in the frame before the whirl, the release in
  the whirl's first frame, 5+ degrees turned in 0.1s; the after-glow as
  SEEN (times every ancestor's opacity) .85+ at the start and .6+ two
  fifths in; the hot core full, only fading, gone before the stop.
  `EVOLVE_ST` gained `aglowEff`, `ahot`, `rel`, `orbA`.

**The Supernova planet's shine carries the blast's damage.** *"The
supernova permanent effect, the big shining mark on the sphere, could that
change somehow because of the damage?"* The planet's specular highlight
(up and to the left) came through the explosion clean. `scarShineWound()`
paints a shattered patch over it in the scar's burn canvas: plates with
dark seams (Voronoi, thinning and breaking off at the edge), each seam's
lip lit or shadowed by the planet's light, soot over the plates, a few
chipped to char, a ragged scorch past them; and it cuts the plasma's mask
half off it. Same palette as the scar (no warm colour, no new ember -
planet2's "black charring" stands, and `check_b317_planet`'s "ember only
in the crater" holds), its own seed, the sphere's foreshortening. It is
part of the scar's art, so it arrives with the planet (`check_b318_scar`)
and fades in at the Supernova scene's `sn-scarred` beat like the crack.
A crater with fractures running out of it was tried first and read as a
black spider on the highlight. Cost: one region of ~50k pixels, the two
nearest seeds from a 5x5 cell lookup; ~14ms warm on the loaded sandbox
(the rest of the art 40-60 there), once per launch for a Supernova
account. **Gate: `check_b319_shine`** - on the 17 Pro Max at 3x, three
themes: the shine region with the scar against the same frame with it
hidden, dulled under 80% (51 against 88) with 3%+ of it dark seams (20%,
clean 0%). Fails on 8aded7f (88 against 88, 0%).

### Build 319 (b319f) - the case opens with the Badges screen; the head and the case one column

Madison: *"when you open the tab the case opens, would be a cool interactive
feature ... the top of the case is really close to that box and it's a bit
wider ... the spacing and that connection/transition ... could be better."*

- **The case opens as the screen opens** (`shutBadgeCase`,
  `openBadgeCaseLid`, `finishBadgeCaseOpen`, `CASE_OPEN`). The tab's own
  `buildOpenBadgeCase` case, built shut (`.is-shut`: the lid folded down over
  the tray at `rotateX(-180deg)`, its outside up - `.ncase-lid-out`, the
  cutscene's shell, trim and Nova plate, `scaleY(-1)` inside the lid so it
  reads upright, 10% taller so it covers the `.88` tray). `runFill` opens it:
  110ms hold, the cutscene's crack curve to -166, the cutscene's swing curve
  to -8; 1.1s, glints done by ~1.35s. WAAPI, transform/opacity only (the
  lid's z-index and face swap at the computed edge-on moment, where neither
  shows).
- **Shut, it sits right under the head**: the whole case starts lifted by the
  standing lid's height and comes down as the lid rises. Shut in place it was
  at the bottom of a phone, behind the tab bar, under 300px of nothing. The
  fall is sampled (20 keyframes) and clamped so the rising lid's top never
  passes where it comes to rest (unclamped it rose 28px into the head).

  anywhere on the case finishes everything at once, and the pressed slot is
  remembered - the case has just moved under the finger, so the click may
  land elsewhere, and that slot's card is opened instead (`check_b319f`

  edge-on moment, 360ms first to last.

  100%) is the head's width AND the width of the leaning lid's top edge
  (1.034 of the case: perspective 340cqw, rotateX(-8deg), lid .8 tall); the
  case is the column / 1.034. `--badges-gap` (1.5rem / 2rem) of air from the
  head to the lid's top. Was 9px and 6px overhang each side on the phone, a
  746px head over a 496px case on the iPad. A connected "label plate" was
  rejected: the lid moves, and the case already carries its plate on the
  front wall.

**Gate: `check_b319f_casespace`** (fails 8 of 10 on bc2986d): shut on the

### Build 319 - the rank-up lives on Profile's road map

Madison, on 318's: *"lots of improvement needed here, the effort seems
minimal. It does the white curser thing ... whatever the last challenge
completed one, show the progress bar of it fulfill, animate the checkbox
... it doesn't follow the progress bar, it skips ahead ... the progress bar
is already coming out of it. It should be AT 0 ... it needs to go under it
and center for the unlock part ... the current rank card doesn't shake or
fade ... it doesn't zoom out ... to show what the next rank is and it's
rewards ... the screen should slowly fade out and back into it ... the
challenge box should do a better animation ... if you have left over xp
this is where it would show it loading/leveling up"*, and *"at the test
result screen it does all the rank reward popups ... those popups should
happen in the road map when that cutscene happens. This would include the
rank up cutscene."* One block after `buildRanksTab()` (all `var`).

- **NOTHING OF A RANK-UP PLAYS ON THE RESULTS OR ON HOME.** summarize() no
  longer sets `pendingTierCutscene`/`pendingSupernovaCutscene`; an older
  build's flag (a synced doc) is turned into an owed rank-up by
  `rankUpAbsorbPending()` (showHome/Profile/Rank/Settings, and every owed
  check). The results show one row, `rankWaitItem` (kind `rankwait`, "Rank
  up / Gold rank / Waiting for you on Profile"), no pop-up; the rank's
  theme, flare, character and banner rows and cards are gone from there
  (`rankUpHolds(rank)`), and Home's queue holds the rank's character and
  banner back too (pendingHomeUnlocks). The results card's rank is the
  last one SHOWN (`rankUpShownRank`) and its level uses the badges the
  rank-up went in with (`store.rankUpFrom.b`), so XP saved behind the old
  gate stays saved there. Home's flares keep the owed rank's flare dark
  (buildCosmicHero) until its cutscene has lit it; afterwards Home shows it
  newly lit. The Home lock (Profile tab rings, Start Studying etc. refused)
  is 317's, unchanged.
- **WHAT IS OWED IS ONE NUMBER: `store.rankUpShown`** - how many ranks
  have had their rank-up shown (a count: 0 = none). Owed = the rank held
  is past it (`rankUpOwed()` -> `{fromIdx, toIdx}`). NULL for every
  existing account on the update, which owes nothing until summarize()
  seeds it (`rankUpSeed`, at the top, before the run can award anything)
  from the rank held then - nobody is walked through an old rank. A new
  sign-up starts at 0 (the store literal), a reset sets 0, merges take the
  max (mergeSameAccount). Fixtures that do not run a test (USED_ACCOUNT)
  stay null and never meet the lock or the scene. `store.rankUpFrom`
  (`{r, b, p}`: the rank shown, badges and XP before the first owed
  rank-up) is written by summarize() and cleared when it is shown.
  `rankUpMarkShown(toIdx)` also moves `rankMapSeen` and sets
  `rankMapFx244`, so the map's own show never repeats it.
- **The journey** (`armRankUpProfileScene` from showProfile, or
  `armRankUpMapScene` from showRanksScreen when Profile was skipped):
  1. Profile AS IT WAS: `rankOfStandIn` (the old rank) and
     `levelStateStandIn` (levelStateFor's stand-in: the level the old
     badges allowed) for that one build. `rankUpPatchGoal` puts each
     challenge the rank-up met back where it stood (`.pf-task[data-kind]`).
  2. `rankUpSceneTick`: no cursor. The card glides into view, each such
     row's bar fills (`.sbar`), its count runs up, its box pops with a
     drawn tick (`.ru-checkmark`), "2 of 2 done", "Rank challenges
     complete", the card turns green-edged.
  3. LOADING RANK UP ADJUSTMENTS (2.6s), the map built under it.
  4. `rankUpMapShow` -> `rankUpArrive` per new rank: the camera follows the
     light (`rankUpFollowY`, 42% down the screen) from where the road stood
     (`rankMapProg`, `ruP0`) - never jumping to the target - along a
     `.ru-rideline` that runs to the next circle's CENTRE, under it (the
     node is drawn over the light; its disc turns to glass, `.ru-under`,
     and its middle lights, `.ru-core`). Then shake, and the map's own
     unlock (is-celebrating). The road on from the last new rank is held
     at nothing (`data-ru-climb`; no stub, no light - and in general no
     stub or light at 0 progress any more).
  5. `rankUpCutscene`: the existing playTierCutscene/playSupernovaCutscene,
     inline, once, for the highest new rank (two at once: one cutscene,
     Platinum's, "Silver -> Platinum"). Its visuals are not this block's.
     (superseded in 326: one journey per rank crossed, Home and the tab's
     call between them, a cutscene each - b326c.)
  6. `rankUpCards`: each new rank's ONE reward card (Theme, Flare,
     character, banner - `rankRewardParts`, build 308's single card),
     one rank at a time, "1 of 2". The input layer lets taps through to
     `.rs-spot`/`#supernova-cutscene` only (`rankUpAllowTaps`). Muted:
     recorded shown, not played (the cutscene still plays, 217's rule).
  7. `rankUpClimbNext`: only if there is progress to the next rank.
  8. `rankUpHeroUpNext`: back at the top the card draws back
     (`.ru-zoomout`), "Up next" rises under it (`buildRankUpNext`: the rank
     after, its level and badges, its unlock chips), then the card shakes
     (`.ru-cardshake`), fades (`.ru-dissolve`) and turns over to the new
     rank ("Rank up", the rings fill again).
  9. `rankUpSceneBack`: a slow fade (`.ru-curtain`), MARKED here, Profile
     built; `rankUpProfileReturn`: the completed card is shown again,
     flips away (`.ru-flip-out`), the next rank's card flips in and its
     head, rows (bars filling) and tiles come in one at a time
     (`.ru-goal-pre`/`.ru-goal-in`, `--ru-d`); then `rankUpStandingClimb`
     climbs the XP bar through the saved levels, the level challenge
     counting with it. Then the layer comes off and the character's
     special plays.
- **Never stuck, nothing twice.** A watchdog per phase
  (`rankUpSceneWatch`); what has played is kept on the DEVICE in
  `class26e.rankup.prog` (`{to, cut, cards}`), so an app closed after the
  cutscene plays the rest without it. Reduce motion (app or OS,
  `ruStill`): the same steps, still, ~11s plus the still cutscene.
- Copy: "Rank challenges complete", "Up next", "Saved XP · climbing to
  level N", "Waiting for you on Profile".
- **Gate: `check_b319_rankup`** (replaces check_b317_rankup; fails on
  8aded7f): a real 100% that tips Gold by its badge, both reference
  devices - no cutscene or rank card on the results, the waiting row,
  Level 49 held there; Home locked with Gold's flare dark; Profile as it
  was; no cursor; the tick; the light ending on the circle's centre under
  it (within 2px); nothing out of Gold at 0; shake, unlock, then the
  cutscene inline on the map; the card on the map and tappable; Up next
  (Platinum) while the card still says Silver; shake, dissolve, "Rank
  up"; curtain, flip-out, goal-in; Level 49 -> 53 one level at a time;
  marked, nothing left; Home free with the flare lit; once only. Plus two
  at once, Reduce motion, a reload after the cutscene, the watchdog, and
  the Rank screen opened directly. The cutscene is stood in for there (it
  is check_b317_evolve's). check_b308_unlocks, check_b318_flares,
  check-curve 7 and check-studyflow 3 now assert the rank is NOT played on
  the results / Home. check_b317_flow's lock fixture sets `rankUpShown`
  (the lock follows the count now, not `rankMapSeen`), and check_b236's
  "light where you are" fixture has some progress (level 44), since at
  none there is no light by design. A fixture that wants the lock or the
  journey sets `store.rankUpShown` below the rank it holds; one that does
  not leaves it null.
- **The seed sits after `retroHideBadges`/`mergeHidePoints` are set** in
  summarize(), not at its top: a rank the handed-out badges or a merge
  tip is that run's, and seeding before they were hidden lost it
  (check-curve 7 caught it).
- **EVERY CHALLENGE COUNT STOPS AT ITS GOAL (build 319).** Madison's
  screenshot: with 7 badges a Silver challenge read "Earn 3 badges 7 / 3".
  `buildProfileTask` now shows `min(now, need)` for every kind (badges,
  level, anything added later) - "3 / 3", bar full, ticked, and the

  it. Gate: the cap section of `check_b319_rankup` (both reference
  devices, plus a rank-up whose badge row is already over: no count past

### Build 319 (b319g) - badges beside the level, the case shut, the Class tab

> **Partly undone by b319h, below.** The Class tab, the Friends and Class 26E
> boxes leaving Profile, Profile dropping presence and the case's materials
> are superseded; the badge count beside the level and the shut case's
> idea stand.

- **The Profile card's top line is "Rank · Level N · N badges".** The count
  is `.pf-badgecount`, in the level's own type, and a tap on it opens the
  Badges page while a tap anywhere else on `.pf-standing` still opens the
  Rank screen. It is a SPAN inside that button on purpose: a button in a
  button is invalid, and check-curve holds the blocks to no nested controls.
- **No open case on Profile.** `buildProfileCase` draws the FRONT of the
  shut case (`.pf-case.pf-case-closed`): the handle on the lid, the lid's
  front, the seam, latches with their hasps over it, the BADGE CASE plate
  (`buildCaseSidePlate`) and "N of 16 badges ›". All from the shared
  `.nova-case-*` materials; never a second style. ~74px on a phone. The
  open case stays in the cutscene and on the Badges page.
- **The bottom tab is Class** (id and dest still `bottomtab-rewards` /
  `rewards`), icon two people. `showClass(tab, {board})` is ONE screen
  with three tabs - Rankings, Friends, Calendar - each built the first
  time it is shown. The panes keep `.screen-rankings`, `.screen-friends`,
  `.screen-calendar`, so selectors that found the old screens still find
  them. `showRankings(board)`, `showFriends()`, `showCalendar()` and
  `showLeaderboard()` all land on their tab; `CLASS_TAB_ALIASES` and the
  board keys resolve too. `showFriends()` while Friends is showing redraws
  that pane in place - that is how accept, send and presence repaint it.
  The Class 26E box (`buildClassCard`) heads the Calendar tab.
- **One swipe moves one switcher.** The screen swipes between Class's
  tabs; a swipe that STARTS on a tab's own switcher (the boards, Month /
  List - `.class-subseg`) moves only that switcher. `attachTabSwipe` takes
  `{ zone }` / `{ skip }` for this.
  Its listeners sit on the document now and also take a touch that
  starts on the bare page under a short tab (`<html>`/`<body>`): `.wrap`
  is only as tall as its content, so on an iPad a swipe under Friends hit
  nothing - and in Chromium went to the browser as a back gesture.
- **A second switcher on a tab is words with an underline**
  (`.class-subseg`), never a second glass pill; the shared slider is
  restyled to the underline with `!important` because `attachSegSlider`
  copies the active button's look inline.
- Presence is attached by the Friends tab only now; Profile no longer
  counts who is online (`PRESENCE_SCREENS` is `.screen-friends`).
- **Gate: `check_b319g_layout`** (both reference devices and a 320px
  phone). Fails on bc2986d.

### Build 320 (b320f) - Nova, the narrator: the introduction, his tooltips, a narrated What's New

Madison: *"the badges and ranks are missing a storyline ... a random character
that looks like one of the ultimates and secrets flares but mix pop up and
talk ... give him professor/instructor vibes ... His name will be Nova of
course ... For newcomers ... Hello I am Nova, the app maker, I lost my
badges ... For existing he will meet you and say your name ... At the end he
will talk about speaking again."*

- **Nova is drawn by `buildNovaSVG({ crop })`, and he is not a character.**
  He is not in `AVATAR_CHARACTERS`, so no picker, board, count or ultimate
  ("every character") can ever include him. viewBox `0 0 48 56` (a bust);
  `crop: "head"` is the tooltip face. Parts: `.nv-back` (halo, nebula,
  corona, stars), `.nv-fig` > `.nv-body` (white lab coat, starry hem, midnight
  shirt with a constellation, gold planet pin, pens), `.nv-neck` (collar, gold
  bow tie), `.nv-head` > `.nv-head-art` (the drawing's own transform is on the
  INNER group, so a CSS transform on `.nv-head` never replaces it), eyes,
  round gold glasses, white moustache and beard, `.nv-mouth-shut` /
  `.nv-mouth-open`, `.nv-hand`. Life is CSS only (transform/opacity, no
  filter): breathe, sway, blink, hair, corona, twinkles; `.is-talking` opens
  the mouth in an uneven beat; `.g-wave` / `.g-raise` / `.g-nod` gestures.
- **`novaTalk(o)` is the one dialogue** (`.nova-talk`): dark sky, dots for
  progress, a quiet Skip, the stage (what he is talking about), his bubble
  and him at the foot of the screen (beside him from 40rem). `novaType()`
  types a line WITHOUT changing what it says: the untyped part is a
  transparent span, so the bubble is final-size from frame one and
  textContent/innerText always read the whole line (gates rely on this). A
  tap finishes the line, the next moves on; Space/Enter/right arrow too,
  Escape = Skip. The last line ends on a button. `el.__nova` exposes
  `advance / skip / close / index / count / typing` for tools.
- **New accounts:** `pendingMainMenuTour` -> `playNovaIntro(startMainMenuTour)`
  (`#nova-intro`, `novaIntroLines()`): hello, the shipwreck (a planet like
  the one on Home cracked apart beside his ship; badges and flares scattered),
  badges (one per unit, hundos), flares (dark on Home, lit by ranks, secret
  ones in tests), ranks Bronze..Supernova, XP and levels, Drill/Exam/Review,
  "I'll show you around". Skip goes straight to the tooltips. Sign-up still
  marks What's New seen, so he does not come back until the next INTRO_REV.
  `#nova-intro` is in every list that waits on What's New (`whatsNewHolds`,
  `noticeAllowedHere`, the save-code/friend/invite checks, CHAR_SPECIAL_COVERS,
  RANKUP_BLOCKERS).
- **Tooltips are his:** `startSimpleTour` puts his face (`.tour-nova`) and
  name in `#tour-tooltip.has-nova` and types each step at 72 cps; Next always
  advances, a tap on the bubble finishes the line. Ids unchanged.
- **What's New (INTRO_REV 4, version 7.8 = builds 319 + 320)** is
  `showIntroPopup()` -> `novaTalk` with id `intro-pop`: greeting by
  username, rank and level, "it appears you have found N of my lost badges"
  (a card with your character, rank, level and "N of 16 badges found"), the
  shipwreck, then `WHATS_NEW_320` - each item a line he says and a row
  (`introRow`) added to the card as he says it. "Your level was adjusted" is
  his too: the same `levelGateNoteText` sentences, and the blue
  `.intro-gate-note` row. Skip puts every row up and goes to his last line
  ("I'll speak with you again..."). The old 7.7 card is gone; "Save A Test
  For Later" moved from RELEASE_NOTES 7.7 to 7.8.
- **Gate `check_b320f_nova`** (fails on a73c681): intro before any tooltip,
  tap-to-finish then advance, the story's words, every tooltip in his bubble,
