- **Quiz is "Mock".** Exam, Qualifier, Quiz and "Mock Test" were each turned down or tuned ("a name that sticks, like Drill"; then "what about just mock?"). The stored mode is still `"exam"`. `modeTitleOf("exam")` and `ACTIVITY_TEXT` are where the name lives; changing it again is those plus the notes. Its icon is a card holding a 2x2 grid of answer bubbles, two solid (chosen from a sheet of options after the ? card and an A+ were turned down); Review's is a front flashcard fanned over two more (also picked from the sheet). Both are plain paths with the tilt baked into the coordinates - no group transform, or check_b323u's ink measure drops it. **Pause names what you are in** ("Your Drill test is on hold", "Your Mock test and its timer are on hold") and **Save and exit is a matte grey** (#3E4249) - black, glass, grey, green and blue had each been turned down before.
- **The mode chip on unit selection** (`.rs-mode`, the same chip as the results screen's) has the results boxes' soft edge: border .46, a faint hairline inside, a glow out and a glow in - never a flat line.
- **Release History has a back link at the top** as well as the button at the foot. Version 9's notes cover this round.
- **The calendar says whose it is**: the top label reads "Class 26E calendar" and a line under it "Class 26E · police academy".
- **LETTERS, NOT BOXES.** A Back pill whose box was exactly centred still looked wrong: a font's letters are not centred in their line box (about 1.5px high in Inter, about 2px on an iPhone's own font, measured off a screenshot). Nothing that measures boxes sees this. `tools/check-ink-centre.py` screenshots each text control twice (as drawn, and with its text transparent) and the difference is the letters; the gap above and below must match within .8px (and left/right within 1.5px). The fix is `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` on the label, which centres by the font's own capital height and baseline, with the padding giving back what trimming takes so no control changes size (`padding-block: calc(P + (1lh - 1cap)/2)`; the rules sit at the END of the stylesheet, or a later `padding` shorthand undoes them). Applied to Back, Customize, the friend buttons and the version label (phone and tablet). **Global trimming was tried and is wrong**: it shrinks every button (the top tabs 29 to 20px, Start Studying 62 to 52). The audit uses Chromium's Inter, so its numbers are not the iPhone's; the fix does not depend on the font, but a control it does not cover can still sit a pixel off on a phone. Send a screenshot of any that does and add its class to the block.
- **The white buttons' edge.** "Why is the edge of the white buttons like that? ... the weird looking edge with the gap." The white `.next` (and `.chip.on`) had a 1px border OUTSIDE the inset shadow that darkened its lower edge - a pale ring, then a dark band, then the fill - and its highlight gradient was painted on the padding box and repeated, so the repeat's bright top edge showed in the border along the bottom. The border is transparent now, the gradient is `no-repeat` over the border box, and the two INSET shadows carry a -1px spread so their light and dark edges run to the button's real edge. **The first fix flattened the shadows to get rid of the ring and lost the 3D feel the other buttons have - it was rejected on sight; keep the original shadow recipe and move only what makes the ring.** Seen at 6x on the Pause sheet and Home's Start Studying. Not measured by a gate: **zoom a button to 6x before calling its edge clean**.
- **The calendar, simplified** ("a little confusing and overwhelming ... no redundancy ... it needs to feel so useful"). Order now: Today, Next test, the month with its key, the Final Exams, The course. Removed because they said a thing twice: the week strip (the month is the week), the day card when today is the picked day (it was the Today card again), the Go to today button when you are already there (`hidden` follows `renderDayCard`), the course hero's "N of M class days done" (the ring says the percent, a tile says days left), and the top label "Class 26E calendar" (the line under it says it). `buildWeekCard` is left in place, unused.

- **Haptics through Nova's introduction, the What's New card and the tour (round 9).** "I need it to work through the nova introduction ... and feel like the app is legit." Found and fixed with real touch taps (`check-b327z` z8, which counts every tick by the event it happened in): (1) a tap on Nova's bubble made no tick at all - `.nova-talk` and `#tour-overlay` are in `SND_SCENE_TAP` now; (2) a button tapped mid-sentence was silent, because his typing blips (`nova.blip`) counted as "the sound this tap already made" and the generic tap gave way to them - blips carry `ambient: true` and no longer set `st.lastAt`; (3) `nova.arrive` asked for a haptic on a timer, outside any gesture, which iOS ignores - its `hap` is null. Chromium cannot feel any of it; the gate holds the path (every tick inside the finger's release, none on touch-down, none on its own). **A real iPhone is still the only proof the Taptic Engine answers.**

### Build 327 (b327l) - Haptic Touch through a real switch under the finger, Nova stops reciting a rule

Madison: *"Haptic Touch is not working. Please look into this"* and *"Novas
message says it's never more than once a day? Remove that and fix that
message some seems weird"*, with *"There's still a bunch of lag with the
bottom tab, still some lag loading screens."* Gate: `tools/check-b327z.py`
(z1-z11, `ONLY=`); the haptics sections are z2-z11.

- **WHY THE TICK STOPPED (reported, not verified here).** `taptic()` plays
  the iPhone's tick by flipping a `<input type=checkbox switch>` from script
  (`label.click()`), which is what the ios-haptics package did up to v2 and
  what worked from iOS 17.4. Apple is reported to have patched that in iOS
  26.5: a switch flipped from script is ignored; only a real finger toggling
  a real native switch plays the tick (ios-haptics 3.x and "Project
  Fathom", both written after the patch and reported working on a physical
  iPhone on 26.5). `taptic()` is KEPT as the fallback for iOS 17.4-26.4 and
  for a tap that did not land on a switch.
- **EVERY TAPPABLE CONTROL ON AN IPHONE CARRIES A SWITCH** (`hswAttach`, in
  NovaSound "A REAL SWITCH UNDER THE FINGER"). `<input type=checkbox switch
  class="nova-hsw">` is the LAST CHILD of the control (`HSW_HOSTS`: buttons,
  `[role=button]`, the Customize tiles, the Home flares and rank bubbles),
  absolutely placed over all of it, `opacity:0`, `aria-hidden`,
  `tabindex=-1`, `touch-action:pan-x pan-y`. A real touch lands on it, iOS
  plays the tick, and the CLICK bubbles to the control's own handlers
  because the switch is inside it. A MutationObserver attaches them in idle
  slices (`HSW_BUDGET_MS` 5, never a long task); `hswStop()` removes every
  one and the page is exactly what it was.
  - **Never `appearance:none`, `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` on
    the switch** - a stripped switch plays nothing. `opacity:0` is fine.
  - **The host is positioned by a zero-specificity rule, never inline**:
    `:where([data-hsw]){position:relative}`. An inline `relative` set while
    Pause was still static overrode its later `position:fixed` and moved it
    (and the chat button beside it) 20px inside a test. Found by
    `check-b327z` z11 on the Question screen. Never set an inline position
    on a host.
  - **Only controls that hold no other control** (`HSW_INNER`): a card with
    buttons in it would have them covered. Skipped on purpose: inputs,
    selects, labels, `.nsw` switches, `.opt` rows, a locked `.choice`,
    anything in `.ru-blocker`, `[data-no-hsw]`.
  - **The switch's change/input/focus/blur never leave it** (a window
    capture listener); its click does, deliberately. Code that refuses a
    touch that starts on an `<input>` (the question swipe, the sheet swipe,
    the chat sheet's `sheetScrollAxes`) is told to ignore `.nova-hsw`.
  - A touch that turns into a drag (more than 10px) leaves the switch
    un-toggled. A tap on a switch is that tap's tick: `taptic()`'s first
    tick is skipped for `HSW_TAP_MS` (600) so a tap never ticks twice.
  - **The Home planet is an SVG circle and cannot hold a switch**, so a
    round HTML box of its exact size (`.cosmic-sphere-hsw`) lies over it and
    runs the same tap (`planetRun`, bound with `homeTapBind`).
  - The Haptics switch in Settings calls `NovaSound.sync()` now, which
    adds or removes the whole layer. iPhone only (`canTaptic()`); an iPad
    or Android never gets a switch.
- **WHAT NOBODY CAN PROMISE.** Chromium has no Taptic Engine, so the gate
  holds the WIRING (a real native switch is there, inside, covering the
  control, and the click reaches it, nothing moves, nothing leaks, off
  reverts), not the buzz. Only a real iPhone on 26.5+ can say whether it is
  felt. It plays iOS's one system tick on a DIRECT tap; a haptic asked for
  from a timer (the grade landing, a cutscene, the XP count) has no finger
  under it and cannot tick; a multi-tick pattern ticks once (the follow-up
  ticks are timer-driven and are only a hope on older iOS).
- **Cost, measured:** with an iPhone user agent at 4x CPU, twelve tab
  switches with the layer on and off were the same within run-to-run noise
  (home 248 against 234ms worst gap, profile 166 against 168ms; long
  tasks 38 against 37). That is Chromium; WebKit's native switches were not
  measurable here.
- **Nova no longer recites a rule.** His hello said "I'll message you after
  a rank-up, when you find something of mine, once a week with a challenge,
  and when there's news. Never more than once a day." - a list that ran on
  and read as terms and conditions. Now: "I'll check in when you rank up
  or find something of mine, and I'll challenge you to a match every week.
  You can message me too." The tooltip and the Version 9 note say the same.
  **The scheduler still sends at most one a day and one a session** - that
  is behaviour, not copy; only the promise is gone.
- **Lag, profiled and NOT changed** (4x CPU, 440x956 at 3x, a used
  account): the working tree and the committed build are within noise on
  twelve tab switches (long tasks 27-43, 2.4-3.9s) and on LOADING TEST
  (two frames over 50ms, worst 79-87ms; the one hitch is the 70-80ms
  question build as the bar hands over). A tap on a tab is answered in
  under 20ms; what is left is the new screen's build (Home heaviest, ~230ms
  worst gap at 4x). The splash has one 1.1-1.3s main-thread stall ~1.4s in -
  `EvaluateScript` of the main script (top level ~800ms, compile ~190ms, the
  first Home build under it) - identical on the committed build; the splash
  bar is a compositor animation and keeps moving through it. Nothing there
  is a regression, and none of it was cut. If a real phone still lags, the
  next lever is to defer the first Home build until after the splash's
  first paint, which changes boot order and wants a device to judge.

### Build 327t - the loading screen finishes on a timer too

Madison's iPhone sat on the splash at "> ready." with the bar full and
nothing else, in Safari and an in-app browser. The splash hid ONLY from a
`requestAnimationFrame` tick, and iOS can hold frames back (Low Power Mode,
an in-app browser sheet, a busy compositor), so the hide never ran and
`.wrap` stayed `visibility:hidden` under it. Classmates on the same build
were fine. Reproduced in WebKitGTK by making `requestAnimationFrame` a
no-op: 327s stuck forever, 327t through. The splash now also finishes on
`setTimeout(duration + 120)`, once (`splashDone`); the rAF tick reads
`performance.now()`, never its own timestamp. With frames off, Welcome,
Sign in, the four tabs, Start Studying and Nova's introduction all still
work. **Nothing that must happen may wait on animation frames alone.**

### Build 327w - no sound engine in an iPhone browser tab

Madison's Safari recording: past the splash, he tapped I'm new here, reached
NEW TO NOVA?, Safari's audio indicator came on, and the page froze with no
taps registering. WebKitGTK and Chromium (iPhone UA, CPU throttled) do not
freeze, so the cause could not be pinned on a phone. What starts at that
moment only on iOS is the sound engine: the AudioContext on the first tap,
the app.start sting, the scripted haptic tick, and 4s later the offline
render of the Home ambience. `NovaSound`'s `iosTab` (an iPhone/iPad, not
standalone) now makes `on()` and `hapticsWanted()` false, so in a Safari tab
none of it ever runs; Settings' Sound & vibration card says sound and haptics
play in the installed app. The installed app is unchanged. If Safari still
freezes on 327w, audio is ruled out.

### Build 327x - a touch-freeze diagnostic in iPhone Safari tabs (temporary)

327w did not fix it. Madison: it works for 5-10 seconds, then no touch does
anything while the planet keeps moving, and leaving Safari and coming back
makes touches work again. Neither WebKitGTK (at 2x and 3x) nor Chromium shows
a stall. In an iPhone/iPad Safari tab only, a line in the bottom-left corner
(after the requestIdleCallback polyfill, "TOUCH-FREEZE DIAGNOSTIC"):
- ticks four times a second; if it STOPS during the freeze, the page is stuck
  on one long piece of work (CSS animations like the planet keep running on
  the phone's compositor);
- counts arriving touches and names what the last one landed on; if it keeps
  ticking and the taps land on something unexpected, an invisible layer is
  catching them;
- times every timer, interval, frame, idle, MutationObserver and event
  callback (setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame, requestIdleCallback,
  MutationObserver and EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener are wrapped)
  and keeps the three longest over 300ms, with the longest stall, in
  localStorage `class26e.diag`.
Remove the whole block once the cause is known.

### Build 327y - the badge outlines are a table, not a layout

Madison's splash showed the boot trace from the launch that froze: it
stopped 4.5s in, inside the after-first-paint queue's `step`. On Home the
only jobs in that queue then are the sixteen badge-outline measurements
queued 4s after launch, each a `getBBox` that forces a layout of the whole
page. The boxes never change, so they are written down
(`BADGE_BBOX_PRESET`, seeded into `BADGE_BBOX_CACHE` beside
`BADGE_CENTRE_OF`); every viewBox is identical to 327x's (compared in
Chromium). A shape redrawn in `BADGE_SHAPE` needs its row re-measured with
`badgeMeasure()`; a missing row is simply measured. The boot trace now
names the queued job itself ("paint <source>"), not the queue, and the
327x touch HUD stays until a launch is confirmed clean.

#### notes-b
#### b327z5-b - sheets you can pull down from anywhere, a close X you can see

Madison: *"The chat box when it's up, you can't swipe down from it unless you
are swiping down from the very top."* and *"The test start menu with all the
options. The swiping down function is broken. It doesn't swipe down similar to
how the chat one doesn't. The x button in the top right you can't see it cause
color. When you do swipe down it glitches and changes colors."*

Base 619542a. Gate: `tools/check-b327z5-b.py` (`B327Z5B_ONLY=A|B`,
`--against FILE`): 24 failures on 619542a, ALL PASS here. Real CDP touch on an
iPhone 17 Pro Max (440x956 at 3x) and an iPad Pro 11" (834x1194).

##### The start sheet (`attachSheetSwipe`: Drill/Quiz/Review and the VR Match settings)

- **From anywhere, when the scroller under the finger is at its top.** It used
  to take the sheet on the first pixel of any move (a tap that slid moved it,
  a sideways slide pulled it) and asked only the sheet's own scrollTop. Now it
  finds the nearest vertical scroller under the finger: scrolled down, or a
  sideways first move, is a scroll; at the top, every move is claimed from the
  first (iOS will not give back a move it committed to a bounce); past
  `SHEET_SWIPE_SLOP` (12px) a down drag follows the finger 1:1 (translate3d
  written once a frame), an up drag scrolls the list by hand. Sliders, fields,
  selects are skipped.
- **No colour change.** `.is-dragging` carried its own lighter blue-grey fill,
  which out-ranked the start sheet's `#0F1115`; it now only drops the blur
  (both dragged sheets are opaque, so the blur shows nowhere).
- **Closes or springs back smoothly**: past min(110px, 22% of its height) or
  a flick, it slides all the way out at about the finger's speed (180-300ms)
  and only then closes; short of it, a .32s spring back; a generation counter
  stops a stale timeout touching a newer drag.
- **The close X is visible**: the white button recipe out-ranked the round
  icon's rules (a near-white X on a near-white disc, 1.0:1). It is a glass
  circle again (13% white lift, lit rim, white X drawn by ::before/::after):
  13.4:1 phone / 10.7:1 iPad, the 44px target unchanged.

##### The chat sheet

- **Down from anywhere.** The head is unchanged (every move ours, down closes,
  up resizes). Anywhere else that is not a text field, the tablet's size
  handle or the emoji tray: a drag that goes DOWN with the list under the
  finger at its top pulls the sheet; up, sideways (the roster), or starting
  with the list scrolled is the list's, and the page guard keeps it off the
  page. Outside the head the slop is `DRAG_SLOP_BODY` (22px, a thumb's tap
  jitter), only a downward move arms, and coming back up only returns the
  sheet to rest - it never resizes. The delayed flat fill (`DRAG_FLAT_AT`)
  is unchanged, so a tap still never moves or recolours the glass.

  `loopWallMs(lag)`), and every running infinite animation is paused while

  The return also counts as a touch for `recordingShouldWait()`, which now

  to Home" button is gone (check-fixes moved).

### Build 327z9 - no strips at Safari's edges

Madison, with a Safari screenshot circled top and bottom: *"Layout and
scrolling function is still broken on safari. The things at the top and
bottom are still."* The 327z3 strips did what they were built for: Safari
read them and painted its status-bar band and the band round its toolbar
solid in their colour, so the page read as boxed between two flat bars.
`EDGE_TINTS_OFF` (beside `refreshEdgeTints`) removes the strips and the
inline root colour, so Safari 26 can run the page under its glass the way
the installed app runs under the status bar. Pull to refresh stays off on
the root only (`html.is-browser{overscroll-behavior-y:none}`); the body no
longer carries it. Not verifiable here (no WebKit); what "scrolling is
broken" means exactly was asked of Madison. check-b327z3 A moved.

### Build 327z9 (continued) - the theme is the last one picked, sound and haptics back in Safari tabs

- **A theme survives updates.** Every update makes each device save once on
  its first boot (327's sound-on), so a device still on Default (a second
  phone, a Safari tab) became the newer copy and pushed Default over a
  picked theme; preferences came whole from the newer copy, and the
  in-memory `theme` never followed a copy applied from the cloud, so the
  next settings save wrote the old one back. Now `store.theme.accentAt` is
  the time the accent was PICKED (Customize, a rank-up's `setNewTheme`),
  `mergeSameAccount` keeps the later pick (no stamps: a set theme beats
  Default), and `themeFollowStore()` puts the merged accent into `theme`
  after `syncSameAccount`, an adopt and an account move. Live on Oct 23: 18
  accounts on Default, 8 on a rank theme; anyone already reset everywhere
  has to pick theirs once more (no backup holds the old ones).
- **Sound and haptics are on in Safari tabs** (reverses 327w/327z2), the
  haptic switch layer included. `NovaSound.tabOff()` is the switch:
  `"safariSound": false` in version.json turns them off in iPhone browser
  tabs on every phone at the next update check, no build needed - the
  escape hatch if a Safari freeze comes back. Not testable without an
  iPhone.

### Build 327z10 - the chat sheet slides down when swiped away, and smoothly

Madison: *"The chat when swiping down, it just disappears, it doesn't do the
animation that it goes downwards, and it's laggy."*

Traced frame by frame on an iPhone 17 Pro Max (modern dark, the default):
- **Laggy**: the modern layout's chat glass (`[data-theme="dark"][data-layout="modern"]
  .chatdock-panel`, round 10) sets `backdrop-filter:blur(30px) ... !important`,
  which out-ranked `.is-flat` / `.is-settling`, so the 30px blur was resampled
  on every frame of the pull and the slide out. A phone-only rule after it
  drops the blur for those two classes (same tone, 95% fill).
- **Disappears**: `endDrag()` closed into the class's `.26s
  cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.25,1)`, which covers about half the remaining way in
  its first frame (665 -> 809 of 969). It now slides out as the start sheet
  does (`attachSheetSwipe`): an inline transition at the finger's speed
  (180-300ms, `cubic-bezier(.3,.6,.4,1)`) to `translate3d(0,102%,0)`, the
  closed class's own resting place, so clearing the inline style moves
  nothing; `closeChatDock()` runs at release (state and sound), `.is-settling`
  stays on until the slide ends; reopened mid-slide, the class brings it back.

Gate: `tools/check-b327z10.py` (`--against`): no blur on any frame of the pull
or slide; at a quarter of the slide's time no more than 58% of the way (new
~51%, old 64-71%); closes, reopens at the same rest, a short pull springs
back. 2 failures on 327z9, ALL PASS here. check-b327z5-b, check-behaviour
b314h_sheet / b314h_chat / b314h_chat2: ALL PASS.

Not verifiable here: how it feels on a real iPhone (Chromium has no backdrop
blur cost to speak of, so the lag fix is shown by the computed style, not by
frame times).

### Build 327z10 (continued) - the tab bar's glass rolls over, the planet answers once, the tab's character moves, the Ghost centred, the daily ring on the glass

Madison: *"The bottom tab is laggy ... when clicking to other tabs it shoots
over instantly, the glass bubble does not roll over to it like the video"*
(an iOS 26 three-tab recording, 1320x2868 at 60fps), *"When tapping the large
planet back to back, it brings up two different messages, shouldn't that just
be combined to one message?"*, *"The ghost character is not centered in the
circle"*, *"The characters aren't animated on the bottom tab"*, and *"The daily
question button, it still stands out, maybe it needs a Liquid Glass look? The
loading bar around it could also look better"*.

#### The tab bar: what was measured
- His recording, frame by frame at 60fps: the press lifts the lens at frame 7,
  it is over the new tab by 12, and **the page only starts to change at 13**
  (a ~100ms cross-fade). The lens's own timing (`LENS.glide`, ~75ms to 90%)
  already matches it.
- Ours, real CDP taps at 4x CPU, read in-page (the screencast lags ~80ms, do
  not time off it): steady state, the lens track runs from +23ms; the screen
  was built on the frame after the click, i.e. ~70ms after a quick tap's
  press, on top of the glide. During the first ~45s after a launch with no
  cached flip-books (every launch after an update) the main thread is ~80%
  busy: the character/rank flip-book recorder (`recordRankSheet`,
  `recordCharSheet`: one frame's clone + serialise + SVG parse is 45-65ms at
  4x, past its idle slice) and the badge warm-up (`warmBadgeStrikes`, 60ms
  unsplittable jobs). A press there waited up to 170ms before its handler
  ran, and the lens was first drawn already across. At 1x the same window is
  ~12s with stalls under 50ms. Home is fully idle once they finish.

#### Changes
- **The screen waits for the glass** (`navigateTab`, `TAB_SCREEN_AFTER` =
  110ms from the lens's lift, `bar._lensPressAt` set in `lensDown`): the
  highlight moves at once, the page is built after the lens has crossed. A
  drag released over a tab (lifted long ago) builds as before.
- **The dark bar's sheen is still** (`[data-theme="dark"][data-layout="modern"]
  .bottomtabs-sheen::before{animation:none}`): 5% white, next to invisible,
  but moving inside the bar's 30px backdrop blur, which iOS then redoes
  every frame. Cannot be measured here (no WebKit, no GPU cost in Chromium).
- **Not changed:** the background recorders/warm-ups. They are cached per
  build and finish in seconds on a fast phone; moving them off the main
  thread is a bigger job (badge renders are canvas pixel loops, flip-books
  need SVG rasterisation). Worth it if the lag is still felt in the first
  seconds after an update.
- **The planet answers once** (`homeTapCopyPlanet()`, no argument): where you
  stand and what is next in one caption; a second tap while it is up keeps it
  (`homeCaptionShow`: same key and words). `homeCaptionState.planetN` is gone.
  check_b317_hometaps moved.
- **The tab's character plays its special** (`CHAR_SPECIAL_PROMINENT` gains
  `#bottomtab-profile .bottomtab-icon-avatar`): its resting loop is a blink
  and a few specks, which at tab size reads as a still. The flip-book was
  playing all along.
- **The Ghost is centred** (`AVATAR_CENTRE_DY.ghost` 2.3 -> -2.5): build 325's
  solve counted its cold light (an ELLIPSE, `-gaura`, not set aside like the
  halo circles) and its floating wisp, and sank the sheet to 59% of the
  circle. Without them it is 50.6% at -2.5, the hem in view. check-b325-a's
  centre section now sets both aside for the Ghost (fails on 327z9 at 59.4).
  Its flip-book re-records on its own (sheets are keyed by drawing).
- **The daily question's ring is a line on the glass rim** (block at the end
  of the stylesheet): the unlit track is the chat button's 1px .16 white rim,
  the progress a slim (3.2/100, ~1.8px) line of the rank colour with a soft
  glow of itself; still on the rim (327z5), border still stood down, round
  ends. Answered, the line is at .85.

### Build 327z10 (continued, round 2) - haptics on wide buttons and switches, Profile and people cards, friends' buttons, Select all, the rank box and case, the start sheet

Madison's list: haptics missing on "a lot of the buttons"; the Profile banner
"loads in laggy"; the Profile box's border "has a strange color"; leaderboard
characters' "bottom half slightly comes out of the circle"; a person's card
"Liquid Glass has a delay" and banners "should fade better into the liquid
glass"; See every rank and the case "not obvious ... if you click anywhere on
either it opens? How could we fix that"; Manage friends' Copy and Send "all
white"; Select all "shouldn't that look better?"; switches "slightly laggy";
Max / All "aren't changing properly, it's not a fast smooth thing"; swiping the
start sheet down moved "the stuff behind it".

- **Haptics** (NovaSound "A REAL SWITCH UNDER THE FINGER"). Audited on an
  emulated iPhone: every label (`.opt` switch rows, `label.pick` unit cards)
  and every control wider than 260px or taller than 70px had no switch.
  Now: (1) **wide is not big** - a `button`/`[role=button]` up to 60px tall
  carries its switch at any width (`HSW_WIDE_H`, `hswTooBig`): Add friends,
  Begin, the calendar's rows; (2) **the switch rows' own input is the switch**
  (`HSW_OPT`, `hswOptAttach`, `.opt > input.hsw-opt`): on an iPhone the row's
  checkbox gets `switch` and lies invisibly over its track (80x46 over the
  64x30 `.box`), so a finger on the track flips a native switch and the row's
  own change runs; a press on it is a press on the box for the lens
  (`NSW_SEL` mapping) and a drag is left to the native switch (`a.native`).
  `hswStop` reverts both. **Still none, on purpose:** the unit cards and the

### Build 327z14 - Safari tabs: the sky under the bars, the tab kept over a reload, sound off; a silent exit; the hundo preview matches results

Madison (Safari tab screenshot, top and bottom bands circled): *"The boxes at
the top and bottom are still there. It also randomly refreshes."* Then: *"The
app randomly freezes again in safari, I think the sound may be breaking it"*,

- **The sky runs under Safari's bars** (`html.is-browser`, "THE SKY RUNS
  UNDER SAFARI'S BARS"). Safari 26's bars are see-through and show what is
  under them; `body::before` (glows + paper) and `body::after` (stars) are
  fixed and one viewport tall, so under the bars only the root's own colour
  (`--edge-bottom`) showed - the bands. In a browser tab both layers run
  `--bleed` (200px) past the top and bottom, with every gradient restated
  from the bottom so the visible pixels do not move (compared against
  non-browser mode in Chromium: within 3 levels except Home's animations),
  and the root's colour is `var(--paper)`. Only confirmable on an iPhone.
  check-fixes' SE 1st gen 568x260 browser "GREY BAR, 10 levels" is
  pre-existing (identical with the bleed block removed) - the scrolled
  html fallback's known limit, see the 11% ceiling note on body::before.

  ~61MB, blob URLs plateau at 9, no leak measured). A browser tab now keeps
  its tab: `LAST_TAB_KEY` (`class26e.lastTab`, sessionStorage, which
  survives the reload) is written on every tab press and, after `showHome()`
  at boot, a non-Home tab is pressed again. `applyUpdate` clears it, so an
  update still lands on Home.
- **Sound is off in iPhone Safari tabs again; haptics are not.**
  `version.json` `"safariSound": false` (the 327z9 switch). `hapticsWanted()`
  no longer reads `tabOff()`, and Settings' Sound & vibration card in such a

  freezes, which have twice gone with sound. `"safariSound": true` puts
  sound back with no build.
- **Leaving is silent.** `suspend()` cut the output mid-wave (a click, then
  iOS tore down the session under the rest). `away()` fades the master to
  nothing (time constant 12ms) and suspends 90ms later; window `blur` (the
  home swipe beginning) fades too; `back()` / `resume()` bring the master

### Build 327z15 - fast tab taps: the last tap wins, nothing extra is built

Madison: *"When clicking the button tabs fast sometimes it lags, the bubble
pill lags and the screen lags ... Check all possible sequences and
combinations and make it run so smooth."*

Traced with real touches (iPhone 17 Pro Max, 1x and 4x CPU), event by event:
- **A 130ms lock dropped taps**, and a long build held that lock's own timer
  shut (one Profile build: 830ms). Gone.
- **The wrong tab won.** A screen waits TAB_SCREEN_AFTER (290ms) for the
  glass, so the old screen is still up meanwhile: Profile then Home found
  Home "already showing", refused the Home tap and then built Profile.
  Against 327z14, 53 of 153 pair/triple sequences ended on the wrong tab.
- **Every intermediate tab was built**, one long task per tap.

Now `bar._navPend` holds the one navigation waiting to build:
- a tap on another tab cancels it before anything is built; a tap on the
  same tab is already on its way; Home "already showing" counts only when
  nothing is pending (then the highlight is put back on Home);
- a press anywhere on the bar re-times the pending build from that press
  (`me.schedule()` from navrow's pointerdown), so no build lands under a
  glide or a held finger;
- a tab whose root screen is already up (`ROOT_OF`: `.screen-profile`,
  `.screen-rankings`, `.screen-calendar-tab`) scrolls to the top instead of
  being built again, as on iOS. From a sub-screen (Customize, Friends) the
  tab still goes back to its root;
- `bar._navBuilds` counts builds (for the gate).
- `orbitGeomKey` reads a kept viewport size (`orbitVP`, cleared on resize):
  `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` mid-build laid the half-built Home out on the
  spot, 56-83ms of a Home switch at 4x CPU.

Gate: `tools/check-b327z15.py` F (every ordered pair and triple from Home at
60/150/300ms: 153 sequences) and G (the reported runs at 4x CPU, 120/250/
400ms). ALL PASS here; 53 + 8 sequences fail on 327z14.

#### 327z15, round 2 - a silent exit for real, no black restart, the answered daily button, the version history, the back button

- **Leaving with sound on still glitched.** 327z14 faded the master over
  ~40ms and suspended 90ms later on a timer; iOS throttles a hidden page's
  timers, so the suspend could come late or never and the audio thread ran
  on starved. `away()` now needs no timer: master set to 0 at once
  (`g.value = 0` and on the next quantum), the ambience loop and every voice
  stopped outright (the ambience is still wanted, so it comes back with the
  page), the context suspended in the same call. Blur mutes the same way.
  check-b327z14 A also holds that no voice and no loop is left running.
- **Black for a few seconds on coming back** is a fresh start: iOS closed the
  app or an update was waiting, and the 8MB page downloads and parses. The
  splash group's reveal waited on animation frames that cannot run until the
  main script is parsed, so it was a dark splash with nothing on it.
  `#splash-group` now also reveals itself from CSS (`splash-in .4s .45s`),
  which the compositor runs; the pixel placement script still runs first.

#### 327z15, round 4 - specials hand back on the frame; secret flares that move

Madison: *"The animation of void, when it does the cool effect and finishes
it, it lags or kinda moves back to the other animation but it's not smooth.
There's like a pause ... Ensure each character's way of doing this is fixed
in every way"* and *"Could the secret flares look a little better ... they
don't look animated except the flashing part. Ensure whatever change you
make reflects app wide"*.

Specials (`playCharSpecial`), measured for all 30 characters:
- **Cut or held.** CHAR_SPECIAL_MS was set by hand; eleven specials ran past
  it (Void 220ms, Genesis 530, Ghost 450, Celestial 360, Oracle 330...) and
  were cut mid-move, Inferno ended 200ms early and stood still. A special
  now ends 20ms after the last of its own animations (read off
  getComputedTiming().endTime, 400-8000ms, else the table).
- **Snap back.** Parts left away from rest on the last frame (a glow lit, a
  layer showing) snapped when the class came off. Every special target and
  `.cx-sp` group whose opacity/transform/translate/rotate/scale differs
  between the last frame and rest eases back over 260ms (WAAPI, no filter).
- **The loop's pose jumped (small tiles).** `.char-special .char-flip-play`
  (and the react/sleep ones) was `display:none`, which cancels the sheet's
  CSS animation; it restarted from its old delay. It is `visibility:hidden`
  now, so its clock runs on. And `charSyncLiveToSheet(el, svg)` puts the
  live drawing's loops on the sheet's clock for the special (currentTime =
  tau * c * P / L, playbackRate = c * P / L, exactly as recordCharSheet
  plays them; a loop the sheet holds still is held still), restored to 1
  after. Sheet vs live at the same instant: Void 1168 differing pixels
  unsynced, 168 synced (the rest is raster difference).
Secret flares:
- `buildFlareOrb` (a test's glint, the found banner, every flare cutscene,
  the unlock card, a character's hint card) gains `.fo-rays` (two unequal
  streaks in its colour, turning 16s), `.fo-orbit` (a white mote circling,
  5.8s) and a breathing `.fo-core`.
- Home's dots gain `.cof-rays` (turning, 3x --fo) and `.cof-orbit > b` (a
  mote circling at --fo, twinkling) when found, and `.cof-sheen` (a band of
  light across the glass every --fo + 1.5s) when not found - still no
  colour on one not found. Per-flare clocks (`--fo`). Reduce motion: none.
- Gate: check-b327z15 N and O.

#### 327z15, round 6 - switches follow a swipe; bug reports go to the Nova admin

- Madison: *"The toggle switches, they only switch if you tap, they also need
  to work if you swipe, similar to the bottom tab."* The glass-knob layer
  (NSW_SEL, build 325) already dragged - but on an iPhone the press lands on
  the row's own input laid over the track as a native switch (hsw-opt), and
  pointermove returned for it ("a native switch drags itself"): invisible,
  it moved nothing you could see and committed nothing. Reproduced in
  Chromium with an iPhone user agent (the hsw layer then mounts). Now the
  knob follows the finger from any start, including a switch button's
  `.nova-hsw` (mapped to its `.nsw`); the release decides by where it is
  let go, or by direction for a flick (velocity) or a 14px move away from
  where it started; a native switch's own flip during the drag is put back
  first, and `nswHold` keeps a late native flip (change/click within 500ms)
  from moving it again. A tap is unchanged. Haptic tick on a scripted
  commit is not guaranteed on iOS (only a native flip ticks) - phone only.
- Report a bug: "Your report goes to the Nova admin" / "It's with the Nova
  admin now." (was "whoever maintains Nova").

  finger, tap still flips) and X.

## Build 327z15 round 35 - the unit search's x, Review's bar as every other, no lag in Review, tabs answer sooner

Madison: *"when searching the leaderboard by name, there's an x there to
erase it. The unit selection screens search bar is missing this"*; *"In
review ... The bottom tab becomes a lot different, the bottom tab gets
pushed together, it should still look identical ... Ensure the search
button is fixed along with it"*; *"I'm still seeing a lot of lag, like when
in review, using the search function it lags, when hitting the drop down
there is lag. When using the bottom tab, there is lag, when opening
different screens or clicking stuff, there is lag/delay."*

- **addSearchClear(wrap, input)**: the board's x (`.rank-search-clear`) in
  the unit picker's and the Virtual Room's "Search units", there only while
  something is typed; clearing fires the field's own input event, keeps
  focus. Safari's own cancel button is hidden in `.searchwrap`.
- **Review's bar is the bar** (327z10's narrowing and side-by-side pair
  removed): `#tabsearch` is a 52px glass circle over the bar's right end
  (TS_GAP+4 above it); tapped, it opens into a field the bar's width just
  above the bar (clear x, Enter keeps results); an empty field that loses
  focus folds back; a touch on the bar closes it on the way. The keyboard
  lifts the field only. `.backtotop` stands its height + 10px higher while
  the search is registered.
- **Review's list builds lazily and filters in place** (showAnswerReview):
  a unit's questions are built the first time it opens or a search reaches
  it and kept (`nodeOf`); a search shows/hides built ones (110ms after the
  typing stops; an emptied field at once); `.review-question` has
  `content-visibility:auto`. Six units at 4x CPU: open 630ms -> ~130ms,
  nodes 4,251 -> 66; a keystroke ~260ms -> ~30ms; a drop-down's slide six
  50-120ms frames -> one ~60ms (with the idle warm-ups waiting, as they do
  under a finger).
- **TAB_SCREEN_AFTER 290 -> 170ms** (from the press): his iOS reference
  changes the page at ~215ms; a tab's screen now starts building just after
  a quick tap's release, while the glass is still crossing. check-b327z15 F's
  "closer than the glide" threshold follows (170).
- Measured, not changed: the idle badge warm-ups (warmBadgeStrikes, 50-240ms
  slices at 4x, one 66ms at 1x) already wait 2s after any touch and 1.6s
  after a screen goes in; Home's cost in headless Chromium is software
  raster, which a phone's GPU does not pay.

## Build 327z15 round 36 - no frost on what scrolls

Madison: *"Ensure the bottom tab lag is not there, the pill/bubble lags and
isn't extremely smooth. Ensure each page opens extremely smooth."*

- Measured first. The lens, the platter and the bar's swell are all Web
  Animations of transform/opacity (compositor; builds 310, 327z5-13). At 1x
  CPU every screen idles at 60fps; a tab switch's own code is small
  (navRun ~15-18ms at 1x, Home 18ms, no long tasks in 2.5s after arriving).
  What is left of a switch is drawing - the GPU's on a phone.
- **No backdrop blur on anything that scrolls.** 30 kinds of card, row and
  section (`.pick` x16 on the unit screen, `.pf-goal` 360x562, `.cal-monthview`
  360x512, `.cal-month-head`, `.rank-row`, `.modecard`, `.settings-card`,
  `.points-progress-sect`...) carried the floating controls' 24px frost with
  `will-change:backdrop-filter` (a layer each). A blur behind something that
  moves is redone every frame on iOS - every frame of a scroll and of a
  page's entrance. Their fill was 62% dark over the dark sky (the next-rank
  card opaque), so the frost was all but invisible: one override at the end
  of the main style block takes it (and the will-change) off and makes the
  pane 70% (`--surface-1/2` on those elements) so no star shows through.
  Pixel diff against before, seven screens: mean < 0.8 levels, < 0.03% of
  pixels over 20 levels (a star's 3px dot, and the tab bar's own glass now
  seeing crisp cards under it). What floats keeps its glass: the tab bar,
  the chat / daily question / room chat buttons, Pause, the search pills,
  Find me, Select all, back to top, every pop-up.
- Not measurable here: the phone's GPU (headless Chromium rasterises in
  software). Confirm on an iPhone.

## Build 327z15, round 38 (2026-10-25): Version 9.2, Firestore savings

"This is gonna be version 9.2". RELEASE_NOTES gains a 9.2 entry at the top
(New In / Better In Version 9.2) describing this build; Version 9 keeps only
what shipped with it. Home's "Version X" / "vX" read RELEASE_NOTES[0], so they
say 9.2. The What's New card (WHATS_NEW_320, INTRO_REV 5) is unchanged.

Firestore check (live, via tools/firestore-admin.py helpers): progress 162
docs (62 __floor) ~8.8MB, largest 249KB; leaderboard 43 rows 62KB; vrooms
164 docs 237KB. Storage is under 1% of the 1GiB free tier. Reads are the
tighter limit (~18-22k a normal day, 35-45k heavy, of 50k), ~60% of them
whole-board reads. Done, all invisible:
- fetchBoardForInvites: the first fetch of a launch (and one every
  BOARD_FULL_MS = 6h) reads the whole board; later ones query
  lastModified > last fetch - BOARD_DELTA_SLACK_MS (10 min, for slow phone
  clocks) and merge by pub. Removal is only taken from a full answer. A
  refused query (boardDeltaOk=false) goes back to full fetches.
- sendOffline writes once per hide (offlineSent, cleared by a beat): iOS
  fires visibilitychange then pagehide on a close. Same for the chat's away
  mark (chatAwaySent); the hide now also clears the typing dot.
- writeLeaderboardRow no longer sets lastHeartbeatAt: presence is read from
  the presence doc first (isOnline), so a row push that reset the beat left
  it up to 4 min stale and friends showed offline mid-test. (Bug fix.)
- The Friends screen's whole-board listener detaches when no
  .screen-friends is on stage (it used to live for the rest of the session).
Left alone on purpose: room beat while hidden (a host could drop a player
who switched apps); marking vrRetroDone at publicId mint (could skip an
old account's backfill; saves ~330 reads per new account only).
Asked Madison (not done): chat beat only while the dock is open; __floor
cadence on hide; leaderboard rows publish `chats` (group chat codes).
Gate: tools/check-b327z15-fb.py (A-D), fails on the previous build.

Sign-up with Nova: Home is built under him before the name is asked, so the
fade showed "Good evening" and then ", <name>" popped in on the rebuild.
homeGreetingText() is shared and novaSignupCreate() refreshes .homegreeting.

"Ensure the what's new card doesn't show up for users signing up.. wouldn't
make sense." Both sign-up paths already marked it seen (novaSignupCreate,
showHome's pendingMainMenuTour branch). Gap closed: maybeShowIntro's attempt
now waits while #nova-intro is up, and during a sign-up (signupInNova) it marks
What's New seen and stops - a device whose older account never saw the card
showed it over Nova. Gate: check-b327z15-fb.py E (fails on the previous build).

  public - it keys leaderboard rows - so it may live in the repo; codes may not).

  script (first <script>) honours it only when the academy's saved copy on this device is

## Build 329 (Oct 26, "More fixes", for the chiefs' presentation) - on the branch claude/b327z15-tabs, NOT main

Corrections round after the class bubble (earlier this day, all pushed): auto-pause when the app
is left mid-test (`autoPauseOnLeave`), `rsTapGuardUntil` (a tap in the 0.7s after results settle is
ignored - the review-tap bug; gates wait 900ms before tapping), the classes screen as a 2-up
`.class-cards` grid with a "More classes / Coming soon" box and "Enrolled" wording, the dropdown in
glass, "Ref. IFC 2021, 1003.2" / "Ref. HC Amendments, 101.2.1" references, planet sizes per device
(iPad 12.9 60vh, tall phones 3.5% smaller, Dell hero 440), smooth CDP-screencast videos.

This round:
- **Every button centred, and a gate for it.** A flex box does not trim its text, so
  `.cc-status` (Enroll / Enrolled / Selected / Coming soon) and `.csi-label` ("Add a class") are
  now blocks the height of their capitals with equal padding (`text-box:trim-both cap alphabetic`
  + `calc((H - 1cap)/2)`); a word with ascenders (Enroll, Add a class) takes a 0.65-1.2px optical
  nudge so the ink, not the cap box, is centred. `tools/check-ink-centre.py` now measures the
  classes screen, the enrol screen and the open dropdown (the seed carries the owner's publicId)
  and fails on the old build (6 fails) - the dropdown rows are skipped when closed.

## Build 338 - the app runs under Safari's bars on a phone (the black bands)
Madison, with the top and bottom circled on an iPhone 17 Pro Max in Safari: *"Safari fix (I've asked for this to be fixed
over 15 times) is not in. THE APP ISN'T VISIBLE ON THE TOP OR BOTTOM WHILE IN SAFARI."* Measured off his screenshot:
the band behind the status bar and the strip under the toolbar were flat (20,22,26), the paper, and the page's own
content (a card at the bottom) faded to it. Cause, in our own CSS: in a browser tab on a phone (no mouse) body::before
(the sky) carried 327z15's "no line under Safari's bars" fades - solid paper in the 200px under the bars, fading out over
the top 6rem and the bottom 5.5rem - and its base was the `var(--paper)` background COLOUR on a fixed, full-width element,
which Safari 26 reads as the tint of its bars. So the bars were flat black boxes where the installed app has its warm glow
and stars (measured in Chromium with touch: the top row (19,22,27) in a tab against (41,33,32) installed). Now:
- the fade layers use `var(--fade-paper, var(--paper))` and `html.is-browser{ --fade-paper:transparent }`: no fade, the
  sky runs under the bars exactly as installed (Chromium, touch: within 2 levels top and bottom);
- every `html.is-browser ... body::before` ends in `linear-gradient(var(--paper), var(--paper))` (an image layer) instead of
  the colour, so no fixed full-width element carries an opaque background colour;
- the root's colour (what Safari fills its status-bar band with) is `--band`, set by refreshEdgeTints (EDGE_TINTS_OFF
  stays on): the sky's top colour averaged across the width, mixed with its bottom colour (one colour has to do for
  both bands) - (33,29,33) on the default theme.
Only an iPhone shows Safari's bars: if its bands are still a different colour, `--band` is the one number to move. Gate:
`tools/check-b338.py` (fails on 337: 14 levels and an opaque fixed body::before).

## BUILD 340 — the tab bar's platter is checked against its lit tab

Madison (screenshot, twice): after tapping Home the grey platter sat about a dozen points left of the Home tab, out past the bar's left edge, and stayed. Not reproducible in Chromium (the platter always lands 10px inside the bar, tapped from every tab, at 1x and 4x CPU), so the cause on iOS is unconfirmed: a measurement taken at the wrong moment, or Safari reading CSS `zoom` (the bar has `zoom:.9`) differently from Chromium.
- `verifyBubble()` (tab bar block, next to `slideBubbleToActiveTab`): once the bar is at rest (no lens, no drag, no swell or tab transform running, platter fully visible) it reads the platter's box beside the lit tab's - same engine, same units - and if centre differs by more than .75px or width by more than 1.5px it re-places the platter (forced, no animation), then, if still off, moves it by the difference it shows. Run 480ms and 1300ms after `lensFinish` and after each navigation's `navRun`. Nothing moves when they agree.

- Findings for the lag (not fixed): Leaderboard idle forces ~270 layouts/s from the animated character avatars (SVG parts redraw each frame); Calendar ~0. Offered: keep only visible avatars animating and freeze them around a tab tap.

## BUILD 344 — Liquid Glass orbs on Home; the tab bar records what a phone does

Madison: the tab bar still lags "for over a week"; the daily question button "when it's ready ... doesn't go with the app, it needs a nice Liquid Glass look"; the class button and its list "the same look but a different thing in the middle".
- **Orbs:** the daily question (all states), the class button and the list's buttons share one glass recipe (end of the main stylesheet): a clear body with light pooled at the top-left (`radial-gradient(130% 100% at 28% 0%, ...)`), a faint return at the foot, a hairline rim with its specular catch (`inset 0 1.5px 1px`), a soft shadow, a 6px backdrop blur (the list's buttons have none: they move). READY is the same glass with the rank colour (`--dq-c`) washed up from the foot and in the rim, the "?" white (it was a lit coloured orb); its ring is kept, thinner. The daily's done state is the dimmer glass with its arc. No `will-change` layers.
- **Tab perf record (the lag, measured on his phone for the first time):** `tabPerfStart/tabPerfSave/tabPerfText` (top of the bottom-tab block). For 1s after a burst of tab taps: rAF frame gaps (worst, counts over 34/50/100ms), frames, and the screen's build time (`go()`); the last 12 bursts in `class26e.tabperf`; `Report a bug` sends them as `perf`; `firestore-admin.py bugs` prints "tab perf:". ## Build 350 (2026-10-29): the tab speed test finds the cause

were large - Leaderboard worst 170-180ms with 13 slow frames and ~47 frames in 1.5s, Home ~100-130ms, Profile ~100ms,
Calendar ~45ms. So the stalls are the graphics side (raster/compositing), not script. Leaderboard (44 characters),
Home (planet + sheets) and Profile (big character) are worst; Calendar, with no character art, is fine.

[flat] backdrop blurs off, [nofx] filters off, [nosvg] character drawings hidden; per pass and tab it reports
worst main-thread hold, worst frame gap, slow-frame count and frames. Read with
`python3 tools/firestore-admin.py bugs`; whichever pass brings Leaderboard/Home/Profile frames down to Calendar's
~45ms is the cause to remove. Gate: tools/check-b350.py.

## Build 353 (2026-10-29): the grey platter's flash and overshoot, and the glass leaving the icon big

Madison's screen recording of the build 352 speed test (iPhone, 60fps crops of the bar): tapping Home, the platter
showed on the tab he had LEFT for a moment, glided to Home overshooting out past the bar's left edge, and settled;
and the Leaderboard tab's icon and label stayed enlarged and soft for ~6 frames after the glass had gone.
Cause 1 (traced at 4x CPU with a log in placeBubble): `new MutationObserver(syncActive)` on the whole stage
(subtree, class/hidden attributes) ran syncActive on every class change anywhere - and in the ~half second between
a tap and its screen being built (the screen waits for the glass), it read the OLD screen, lit the old tab and slid
the platter back to it (animated, with the lens' overshooting ease); navRun's own syncActive then slid it back to
the new tab. Now the observer ignores everything while `bar._navPend` is set, and reacts only to a change of SCREEN
(stage's own children, screen-* classes, [hidden]). Also far fewer syncActive runs (each is a dozen
querySelectors; ~100ms at 4x in the profile).
Cause 2: lensMagnify's way back (260ms, spring ease with overshoot, starting greyAt-60) finished after the glass
handed over. It is now 150ms from greyAt-110 with a plain ease, so it is over before the hand-over.
Gate: check-b353 (platter on the tapped tab for the whole time it shows; fails on 352 for Leaderboard -> Home).
Still open: Home's frame stalls (planet system; syncLoopClock's getAnimations ~70ms at 4x on each Home mount is
the largest JS item in the Home mount profile), the Leaderboard fill-in smoothness.

## Build 355 (2026-10-29): coming back when the page was never told it was hidden

Madison: the planet system still lags weirdly after leaving the app and coming back. Build 350 held the loops on
their pose until four steady frames - but only if the "hidden" event had run. iOS can freeze a Home Screen app
before that event (and `if(!loopHiddenAt) return` then did nothing), so the loops ran on the wall clock while the
app was away and the planet system appeared already moved on. Now: a 1-second tick (`loopAliveAt`) says the page was
alive; `loopsBack()` (visibilitychange visible and pageshow) sees a stale tick (>2.5s) with no hidden mark, pauses
every infinite loop, puts each back by the time away, and holds it until frames are steady as before. The time
they stood still is also taken off the loop clock (`loopHiddenMs`), so a Home built afterwards lands on the same
pose. Every way back is noted in localStorage `class26e.resumelog` (told/NOTTOLD, time away, first frame, time held,
loops held) and shows in the bug report's perf line as "resume: ...". Gate: check-b355 (fails on 354).
Folded in: build 354's speed test (steady / fast / spam taps with an end-state check), PR #23.

## Build 356 (2026-10-29): coming back by pose, the Leaderboard filled in, a run of taps builds once

Madison's recording of build 355 (leave, come back, then the speed test):
- COMING BACK: in the first ~0.35s the planet system stood still, then the secret flares jumped ~25 degrees (the
  inner layer turns 7 deg/s, the outer 3: a few seconds' worth) as the loops were let go. 355 rewound loops by
  Date.now() minus the last alive tick - an assumption about the page's clocks across a freeze. 356 reads the
  reference loop's POSE instead (`loopRef`, the outer turning layer; `loopRefSnap` kept every second): the shift is its
  pose now against its pose at the last tick (+ half a tick), never negative; and when the loops are let go the
  loop clock (`loopHiddenMs`) is re-made so that `loopWallMs` agrees with the reference loop's real pose, so
  nothing that re-syncs later (a Home build, startRankMarks) can move them. Every return is noted
  (`class26e.resumelog`: told/NOTTOLD, away, first frame, held, loops, `drift` = how far the reference moved in 600ms
  against 600) and the speed test's report now carries "resume: ..." (355 put it only in the manual bug report).
- LEADERBOARD: rows below the first screenful sat bare (empty frames where the character and flare go) for ~4s

## Build 366 - THE CRASH: every Leaderboard visit kept its whole list in memory

His speed test crashed (white screen, splash, back to the menu) when it reached the Leaderboard, on 361/362/365 - "inexcusable". Measured here: the renderer's
RSS over the full speed test went 469MB -> 2.9GB (186s, +14MB/s); 30 Leaderboard<->Home visits 535MB -> 1.5GB; 30 Profile<->Home visits flat (~775MB); Calendar flat.
`Performance.getMetrics` Nodes (after forced GC) 9k -> 401k over six rounds of the four tabs; JSEventListeners 279 -> 876. Bisected by stubbing: `lbFillArt` off = flat;
`buildAvatarCharSVGSafe` stubbed = flat. A V8 heap snapshot (3-6 visits) and a reverse walk from detached SVGs to the roots found the retainers:
1. `showRankings`/renderRankingRows added `document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", onVisible)` on EVERY visit; it only removed itself when the event fired after
   the list had left - tapping through tabs never fires it - so each visit's closure kept `rows` and with it the whole list (43 rows x ~250-part characters): ~35MB a visit.
   Now one document listener at load, and `rankingsOnVisible = { rows, paint }` holds only the latest screen.
2. `charFlipWatched` (swept only above 60), `charRecWaiters`, `orbitRecWaiters` (pruned only when asked): each held a tile and through it a row and its screen. Swept from 24, on
   every add, and every 4s by a timer.
3. recordRankSheet / recordCharSheet left their 5-8MB canvas to the collector on every early exit (a visit that ended); freed in `finally`. A recording now waits until the
   screen has been up 3s (REC_VISIT_MS, CHAR_REC_SETTLE_MS 700 -> 3000) so a visit that is about to end does not start 100+ frames of work and abandon it.
4. artQuiet queued the art of EVERY row; now the rows within 1.6 screens below / .6 above (the lazy observer, 500px out, fills the rest as they are scrolled toward).
Result in the sandbox: Leaderboard<->Home x18 +600MB -> +106MB; the whole speed test 469->2886MB -> 377->1741MB (still growing: Chromium keeps its heap; the retained
screens are gone - the remaining retainer is the latest screen only). check-b366 (no listener added per visit; no stale tile in the sets). iOS may still end a page
for other reasons; the `ended:` log in Send tab timings says when it does.
Build 366, gates updated for what it changes on purpose: b352/b356/b358 expected every row to have its art (now the rows within 1.6 screens below / .6 above the view; `lbNearRows`, also what
restoreAfterBackground queues - it queued all 43), b357 waits for Home's first emblem sheet before the return (a recording starts once the screen has been up 3s), b366 also checks that
scrolling to the bottom fills the far rows. His 11:41 recording on 365 (28s of tapping, many Leaderboard visits): press-to-screen 0.2-0.65s and spikes - that is the leak at work (each
visit +35MB, GC pauses and memory pressure grow with it), not the tap code; 366 is the answer.

## Build 368 - the "ding" when sliding across the bar from the Leaderboard

Madison: "at random times, if I'm on the leaderboard, and start swiping to other tabs, the sound effect is different ... like a ding". attachTabSwipe (the Leaderboard's board swipe,
Profile's top-tab swipe, ...) listens on `document` and accepts a touch whose target is `<html>`, `<body>` or inside `.wrap` - "the bare page below the screen". The tab bar is a
floating pill with a margin round it; a slide that starts in that margin has `<body>` for a target, so it was read as a swipe of the screen: on the Leaderboard it changed board
(overall -> hundos) and played the board switch's sound; on Profile it changed the top tab. Random because it depends on where the finger lands. Reproduced with synthetic touches
(a slide starting 6px below the bar, and 8px above its top: board overall -> hundos on 367; unchanged on 368; a swipe on the screen itself still changes it). onStart now ignores a
touch whose y is within the bar's box -14px above / +30px below. check-b368. (368 also carries 367's Drag test.)

## Build 375 (2026-11-01): the glass lands after the new screen is drawn; the Leaderboard arrives with its art

Madison: "The clear bubble ... when swiping/sliding it's still laggy ... laggy when it shrinks down and goes when you swipe to the tab you want.
The leaderboard tab also doesn't load because some of the rows and the stuff on them aren't loading properly, same goes for home and profile."

READ OFF HIS 21:06 RECORDING (120fps, 12 tab changes), per event, the bar crop's frame-to-frame change and the header's change (= the new screen
on the glass): the new screen shows 225-425ms after the press, and in that window the lens - whose lift, glide and landing are already
Web Animations tracks (the compositor's) - stood still for 50-180ms at a time and then jumped (e.g. ".#......#..................#....."
over 400ms). So on his phone drawing a new screen takes the frames the glass needs, however the glass is animated. The 371 Drag test
(Low Power Mode off) showed the slide itself at a clean 60Hz in every look: 97% of intervals exactly 2 frames at 120fps. Safari renders
the page at 60fps on his 120Hz screen (rAF median 17ms; even the WAAPI tracks were 60Hz in the video) - 120Hz is not available to the page.
Home, Profile and Calendar arrived complete in one frame in that recording; the Leaderboard arrived with every character a soft disc and
every flare an empty ring, the characters coming one at a time from ~450ms (the queue's hold, build 363).

1. THE LANDING WAITS FOR THE SCREEN (bar code, near lensRelease): when a release is followed by a navigation, navigateTab calls
   bar._lensAwaitScreen(): the release track is replaced by one that stays (or keeps arriving) at the lens's held size over the tab, glass
   clear, platter hidden, bar swollen; navRun, after building, waits two frames (the frame after the one that drew it) and calls
   bar._lensScreenIn() -> lensRelease(tab, true): hold = max(0, minUp - upFor) (no linger, it has waited), then the normal settle.
   LENS_AWAIT_MAX 650ms caps the wait. lensDown/lensHide/lensRelease clear the wait. A tap on the tab already up (no navigation) lands as before.
   A still lens cannot stutter, so the drawing happens under a still glass; the shrink then has the frames to itself. TAB_SCREEN_AFTER (40)
   is unchanged - the tap->screen timing he liked is the same; a tap's glass stays up until its screen is drawn, then lands.
2. THE LEADERBOARD'S FIRST FRAME IS THE FINISHED BOARD. Building the art in the tap was measured (4x CPU): ~13ms a row (the ~250-part
   drawing built and painted) = ~a second on the phone for a screenful; NOT shipped (an in-view fill was tried first and measured 150ms
   task / 317ms to two frames vs 11 / 56). Instead: what a row SHOWS is its character's recorded loop and its flare's loop. When the loop is in
   memory (charAnimReady: every sheet that resolves; orbitAnimReady for flares) and the row's geometry is known (lbGeom, measured by the
   first real charFlipAttach / startOrbitEmblemAnims on a board row and kept in localStorage `class26e.lbgeom`, keyed by viewport+dpr),
   the row is built with the loop playing (lbFlipKnown: the same .char-flip-play charFlipAttach makes, from the kept left/top/cell) and the
   flare is the real mark with its sheet attached immediately (lbMarkKnown). The drawing still goes in later from the queue, under the loop
   (lbFillArt keeps a pre-attached loop: svg inserted before it with .char-under-flip, char-flip state set without setCharState, which would
   remove the loop). `.rank-avatar-wrap[data-lazy-av]:not([data-flip-pre])` keeps the soft disc only for rows with nothing to show.
   lbArtPreload() reads the saved loops (Cache Storage) for the characters and ranks on the board in quietIdle slots - at 3.5s and 1.5s after
   every board fetch (lbArtPreloadSoon) - so the first board after a launch is finished too. It never records.
   First board ever on a device (nothing recorded, no geometry): as before (discs, then the queue), and that visit records what the next needs.
Sandbox: second visit and post-relaunch first visit: 8 of 9 visible rows looping and flaring in the mounting task, 0 discs; the first frame and
the settled board differ by 0.025 mean (flare column mid-frame). check-b375.py fails on 374 (all three parts).

- "When you start the swiping animation, the screen you are on stops moving" = build 373's pause (html.tab-dragging #stage * paused). TAKEN OUT;
  the class is still set during a slide. check-b373.py removed; check-b375 (3) asserts >= 80% of the page's animations keep running mid-slide.

## Build 2026-11-01-378 - Leaderboard first draw: the measurement, and two candidate ways to play a board loop

Madison, on his 08:22 recording of 377: "I think all the switching tabs by tapping is good to go except the leaderboard still. The
leaderboard still takes a minute can you tell?" Yes: read frame by frame, the Leaderboard's screen came up 258/317/325ms after the
press, every other tab 42-108ms. His 377 "Tab timings (in use)" agree and say where: the board's screen is BUILT in 5-18ms (build10x1 ..
build11x1) but first drawn (p, tap to the second frame after it) 265-370ms after the tap - Profile ~93-122, Home ~150-170, Calendar ~43-83.
So it is not the script; it is what the phone does to draw the board, which the sandbox (Chromium) cannot show.

What the sandbox can show (tools: LayerTree over CDP): the board's first frame makes ~110-190 layers (Profile ~70). Per row on screen:
the character's loop window (.char-flip-play, masked round), the loop's <img> - the WHOLE recorded sheet (12x12 frames, 792px square
natural, 396px CSS) on a layer of its own because it is moved by a stepped transform (will-change:transform) - the flare's loop
(.cosmic-rank-anim, screen-blended and filtered) and its <img> (the whole 12x15 sheet), and the flare's ::after forced up by overlap.
Chromium only rasters the clipped 33px of each sheet layer; WebKit allocates and paints a non-tiled layer's backing store whole, at the
screen's scale (a 396px sheet at 3x is ~1190px square, ~5.6MB) - ~30 of those per board visit would be the missing ~150-250ms, and it
is paid on every visit because each visit's rows are new layers. Also: WebKit does not hand a steps() animation to Core Animation
(GraphicsLayerCA falls back to software for steps timing), so every stepped loop in the app may be moved by the page every frame on
the phone. Neither can be confirmed here, so 378 measures it on the phone:

- "Test Leaderboard speed" (Report a bug, under Send tab timings) - runBoardTest(). ~70s. Taps Leaderboard then Profile; three rounds of
  seven looks taken in turn (so drift spreads evenly): [b:base] as is; [b:paint] html.lb-paint; [b:hold] html.lb-hold; [b:noloops] no
  loops; [b:nofx] loops without the round mask / screen blend / filter; [b:noglass] no backdrop blur on the screen; [b:norows] no rows
  (floor). Per look: Leaderboard p median and the three values, then in the 1.5s after it the worst frame w, slow frames s (>34ms),
  frames drawn n and f (MessageChannel round trips per 10ms - how free the page was), and Profile's p. Sent as a bug doc "Leaderboard
  speed test" (id ...-brd...), no code, like the others; read with `firestore-admin.py bugs`.
- html.lb-paint (lbPaintKF / lbPaintAll / lbPaintWatch): each board loop img keeps its sheet but is moved by stepped left/top keyframes
  (rk-pos-*, the same frames, the same clock - only animation-name is swapped, via --pk, so the delays and resync still apply) with
  will-change off: no layer per sheet, only the one frame in view is painted. Measured here: board layers 107-119 -> 25, pixels the same
  (32 antialiasing px of 880x1300 differ, max 44/255), loops still move.
- html.lb-hold: each loop keeps its layer but runs rk-hold-* keyframes - every frame held from its offset to 0.0002% before the next,
  linear timing - which looks identical to step-end (0 px off at three times) and which WebKit can give to the compositor.
- A board built or switched while a look is on comes up in it (a MutationObserver on the rows, installed only when a look is on).
- Both looks are OFF by default: nothing changes for the class in 378. The test's result picks what 379 does - [b:paint] much below
  [b:base] (and near [b:noloops]) = paint the board's loops; [b:hold] with the most free page (f) = hold-frame keyframes for every
  stepped loop in the app (board, Home's flares, the tab bar's character).

"Sliding now is broken, if you slide to another tab it won't actually open that screen. Even when sliding does work it's still not
smooth at all. Big big big bug, middle of my test the app just white screened, showed the loading splash screen, and sent me back to
home." Read frame by frame: five slides Home -> Profile in a row, the glass went over Profile each time and came back to Home, and the

iOS throttles hard there, so its smoothness numbers (bar updated ~20-40 times a second mid-slide) are not a fair read of the build.

  where canTaptic()) out of the page as a slide began. The switch a finger lands on IS the touch's target; on iOS a touch whose target
  leaves the page did not finish the slide (the release came back as a cancel: lensRelease(null), the glass home, no navigation). Even

  listens. The sandbox never saw any of it because the switches are not attached off an iPhone. Now tabSwitchesOut() does nothing; the
  switches stay. (Also: hsw's own MutationObserver re-attached a NEW switch to a host whose switch was removed, so 377's removal churned
  switches mid-slide besides.)

  And while a test is on the screen (.qpanel / .pausepanel) the ready loops let go of their decoded pictures (sp.pre, kept since 377 for
  the board's first frame), checked every 6s (testTrimSheets) and at load (charAnimSheetFromBlob); decoded again once the test is gone.
- NEXT TIME IT HAPPENS: the 6s in-use mark (class26e.session) now carries the same footprint as the hide (el/img/mp/cv/sh), plus
  "rec<n>" while a recording is running and "tt" while trimmed for a test, so an ENDED-visible line in the next report says what the page
  held and whether it was recording. (Before, an in-use mark had no footprint.)
- tools/check-bugreport.py clicked the FIRST .bugreport-send, which since build 349 is "Test tab speed" - it timed out on every build

### 379: a tap that ticked but did not pick the answer

His 11:07 recording (Drill, question 93): he presses C several times - it dips, the tick plays - and nothing is picked, until a later
press finally counts. Every answer choice carries a native switch (.nova-hsw, iPhone only) for its tick; the tick is the switch being
toggled, and iOS can toggle it - a press that rolls the finger is a drag of the switch's thumb - WITHOUT sending the click that the
choice's own handler (choose) waits for. (His UA reads iPhone OS 18_7, which iOS 26 also reports - the switch tick is the 26.5 path.)
The choice's handler itself had nothing that drops a tap (only paused/cleared guards).
Fix (in the hsw layer, next to the drag rule): a touch that began on a switch, did not move 10px (not a drag - those are still
swallowed, so a scroll that starts on a choice never picks it) and ended with NO click at all within 140ms is clicked on its control
(host.click()); a trusted click that arrives late on the same switch within 700ms of that is the same tap and is swallowed. Each rescue
is counted in class26e.hswrescue and shows in "Send tab timings" as "taps rescued N" - so the next report says how often the phone
dropped one. Gate: check-b379 (7) - real tap picks once, touch with no click still picks, slide picks nothing (fails against 378).

### 380, second pass: the tab bar checked top to bottom with the iPhone layer on

Madison's goal: "please get the bottom tab acting perfectly smooth, flawless, no lag jumps/spikes ... tapping ... sliding ... no
crashes ... Do an entire check on the bottom tab top to bottom". Every gate so far ran WITHOUT the iPhone-only layer: hswSync attaches
the native haptic switches only where canTaptic() (an iPhone UA, no vibrate), so the sandbox never had them. The audit now runs with an
iPhone user agent (init script: Navigator.prototype.userAgent, vibrate deleted) + CDP touch, at 4x CPU, CPU profile per tap/slide.
Found, only with that layer on (each also confirmed absent/failing on 379 by check-b380 7-9):
1. EVERY TAB TAP WAS TAKEN FOR TYPING. A tap leaves the tab's switch (an <input type=checkbox switch>) focused; the three keyboard fixes
   (pointerdown blur, focusin's lastTextFocusAt, the #stage MutationObserver's unwind) tested /^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/ - so the next press
   blurred it and every screen mount blurred it again and ran the unwind's passes. ~285ms of blur self-time over 8 taps at 4x. Now
   isTextEntry(): a TEXTAREA or an INPUT that is not checkbox/radio/button/submit/reset/range/color/file/image/hidden.
2. THE SWITCHES WENT IN DURING THE GLASS'S LANDING. Safari has no requestIdleCallback, so hswSchedule was a plain 90ms timer - on 379,
   36 of 43 switches went in inside the settle window. Now it waits out settleUntil and a slide (first switch ~600ms after the tap, none
   inside). And hswFlush judges every queued node's hosts first (size reads) and only then attaches (writes): judging and attaching one
   node at a time laid the screen out again per node (a board's rows each arrive as a node).
3. THE BOARD'S FLARES WERE RE-SYNCED OVER AND OVER: startRankMarks synced every mark on every art-queue step, and the row observer's
   first report re-synced every row on screen - 62 syncLoopClock (getAnimations: a style pass each) for 18 flares. Now a mark is synced
   when it is new to its row (a._syncRow) and the observer only syncs a row coming back from off screen (wasOff): 29 for 18.
Measured with the iPhone layer, sum of per-tab medians over 12 taps at 4x: style 1058 -> 777ms, script 3004 -> 2245ms, worst frames
700 -> 550ms (379 -> 380; layout/paint up a little - the loops now step on the page). Slides: median and p95 frame 17ms on Board,
Home and Profile; the only long frames are the first 1-5 of a slide (the lift), mostly rendering (layerize/commit/paint), not script.
Not changed (checked): the sound room's impulse is already made in quiet time (quietIdle); syncBackToTop and the segment slider's place()
read layout inside rAF (the layout the frame does anyway).

  Customize alone makes ~30 ready (his 377 report: 37 sheets held at a hide). The 14 used most lately keep theirs (lbFlipKnown touches
  a sheet as it puts it on); the return from the background and the end of a test decode only those again. check-b380 (10).

- Memory soak with the iPhone layer: 60 tab taps, the JS heap 6.4 -> 7.2MB, elements and images flat - no leak.

### 380, third pass: his four asks (results taps, tap-through, slide from the lit tab, board characters)

Madison: "at the end of a test, when I finish the retake and I click the screen, the tests goes away and takes me to the main menu ...
(I thought we fixed this already because I've mentioned it before)"; "if you tap it while it loads it would finish instantly and then go to
the xp box and do it normally, if you tap it again that would finish and so on" (pop-ups for unlocks and the hundo stay unskippable);
"if I use the swipe way instead of the tap, it lets me swipe even if I don't initiate the swipe from the current tab, that shouldn't ever
happen"; and "Should we make it so that the leaderboard characters don't animate when looking at the entire leaderboard? Would that fix
the lag?"
- THE MAIN MENU BUG (reproduced: a retake's results, a tap every 440ms where "Main menu" rises - home on the 8th): build 328's guard
  (rsTapGuardUntil: 700ms after a tap on the results, 600ms after the buttons rise) had a hole - a tap ON a risen button that the guard
  refused did not restart it (only the panel's own click handler did, and it returns early for a button), so the next tap was past it.
  Now a refused button tap restarts the guard: while taps keep coming the buttons stay quiet; a tap after a 700ms pause is a press.
- TAP-THROUGH, BOX BY BOX: build 305's tap ran ONE step of the timeline (the grade box is four: head, card, a beat, the count), so a tap
  often seemed to do nothing. makeRevealSequence steps now carry their box (`group`: "grade", "xp"); seq.nextBox() runs the rest of the
  box that is coming in at once (each step told instant: the count lands on its number, the bar on its fill) and brings the next box in
  after a 260ms beat, playing normally. Between boxes a tap brings the next one now. A `wait` step (an unlock's pop-up, a scene, the badge
  case) is never run early; the hundo effect is its own step and plays. Sandbox: 6-7s with a tap every 0.7s (20s+ untouched).
- THE SLIDE STARTS ON THE LIT TAB: pointerdown notes the tab under the finger (tabDragStartTab) and whether it is lit; a press on another
  tab never becomes a slide (pointermove ignores it) - let go on it and its own click opens it, let go off it and the glass goes back to
  the lit tab (lensRelease(null)), nothing opens.
- THE BOARD'S CHARACTERS: not taken out. His 378 test put their cost at ~230ms of the board's first draw (448 -> 218 without loops) -
  that was the whole-sheet layers; 380 makes each a window-sized layer (sheet layers 36 -> 0). If the phone still shows the board slow
  after 380, a still board (the 379 lb-still look, kept) is the next step, not a guess before the numbers.

### 380, badges: the unlock coin, the lift out of the case, the put back; the results guard counts a held-back tap

Madison: "The badge unlock cutscene is good but when the badge comes up it lags like it not shiny for a second or something and then is?
... When at the badge case and you select a badge to view, it does the same thing, as it pulls up (zooms in to get bigger) it lags and it
doesn't have a consistent look the entire way through ... When you click close to get off the badge, when it goes back to the case it lags
as it gets put in the case".
- THE UNLOCK COIN: buildBadgeCoin is ~22 <img>s on data: URLs (face, silhouette mask, the edge layers, the back). warmBadgeCoinFaces made
  the URLs ahead but nothing decoded them, so the coin came up with its pictures arriving over the first frames (the shine and edges a beat
  behind the face). bcPredecode(url) keeps a decoded Image per URL (BC_DECODED, at most BC_DECODE_MAX 64, oldest dropped) and the warm-up
  decodes every picture the coin will use. Sandbox: 22 of 22 complete the moment the coin is built (379: 0 at once, 2 by the first frame).
- THE LIFT: the big face (ensureFace) was rendered when the tap landed - a few hundred ms on a phone - so the badge lifted out on its small
  slot picture and the big face took its place part way up. binspectWarmSoon(), called at the end of buildBadgesTab, renders each found
  badge's big face, back and edges at the size .binspect-float shows (binspectW) in the quiet once the tab is up - one job per 150ms, never
  under a settle, a touch (recUserAt 900ms), an open badge or a hidden page, and only while #stage .ncase is up. A finger coming down on a
  found tile decodes those pictures (binspectPredecode). Sandbox at 4x CPU: pointerdown 345ms -> 26ms, one face through the whole lift.
- THE PUT BACK: putBack built the badge for the slot at the DEFAULT size (152px) as a draft, then badgeStrikeWatch measured the slot (88px
  at 2x) and rendered again, then the finish replaced it - three pictures and two renders in the frames it landed. The slot is now drawn at
  the slot's own measured size (slotOpts { px: slotRect.width }), and cleanOne renders that picture for the new stage 700ms after a stage
  comes off, so the put back finds it finished. (The empty slot a lifted badge leaves is a vector hole - no picture - and was never part of
  it.)
- THE RESULTS GUARD, AGAIN: one gate run of the 30-tap test pressed "Main menu". The taps were 450ms apart in the gate's own clock and one
  gap reached ~700ms - a tap reaching the page late is the same thing a phone does when the page is busy (the save at a test's end). The
  button now judges a tap by when it happened: rsTapAt(e) takes the event's own time (when given) and, while a results screen is up, a
  frame beat (rsBeatStart from rsRise; no frame for 120ms = the page was busy and the tap came in during it, counted from the last frame).
  The 30-tap test now taps from inside the page.
Gate: check-b380 (16) a found badge: finger cost and one face, (17) the coin complete when built, (18) the put back one finished picture,
(19) a tap held 900ms behind a busy page 120ms after a tap does not press Main menu - all four fail on 379 (19 also fails on 380 before this
pass). All 19 parts fail on 379 (run against origin/main: the local `main` ref in this sandbox is stale at 327t - use origin/main).

Phonetic Alphabet badge (8.8px) on 379 too - older than this build, not touched. check-behaviour's badge sections fail the same 10 checks on
