## 384 r16 - the class cards are one size and the coin is a clean disc (branch r16-classcards, from 1c91137; not on main)

Madison on the sign-up "Select your classes" step: "Both of the boxes should still be the same size on the SE (smaller devices)" and "the bottom of their circles look bad ... maybe the top too".
- EQUAL HEIGHT. The stacked short-phone layout (r13) left each card its own height (Police Academy 83px, Fire Code 133px on the SE 2nd/3rd gen). The cards' grid now has `grid-template-rows:repeat(var(--cc-n,2), 1fr)` and `grid-auto-rows:auto` in that tier: the two class rows share the taller one's height and the "More classes" row keeps its slim own (a bare `grid-auto-rows:1fr` would have made that row as tall too - see r11). `--cc-n` is set by showClassSelection() from NOVA_CLASSES.length, so a third class gets its row without anyone editing the CSS. Card is `align-content:start`, so the spare height lands at the bottom of the shorter card (the other layouts already stretched: two across and three across are one grid row). The Classes screen (showClassCatalog, Settings / the class button's Add a class) already had equal rows and still does; check-b384-classcards asserts it with none, one and both enrolled.
- WHAT THE SE PAID. Equalising on its own cost the step +50px (Continue 546 against the 522 line). Fire Code's card was 133px because its kicker ("2021 IFC + HC AMENDMENTS", ~195px) wrapped to two lines beside a 100px chip column. In the stacked tier now: the kicker spans the full width beside the mark (one line); the chip sits on the NAME's row (the chip column no longer takes the kicker's width); mark centred on those two rows (the picked check follows, +28px instead of +24); kicker line-height 1.2 (12.7px, same size); card padding 8px top and bottom (was 10.4 / 11.2); line under the title .15rem and the Needs line .1rem under it (was .3 / .15); "More classes" row padding .3rem (was .45); the line under the sub .3rem (was .45rem). Both cards are 112.9px; Continue stays at 521.6 with ~7px of slack (it had ~10); no type is smaller anywhere (the .76rem line, the 18.4px name, 10.56px kicker, 12.16px Needs are unchanged). Given up: ~3px of air round each card's text, 5px under the sub, the Fire Code kicker is now the width of the card instead of two short lines, and the picked mark has a 4px lower centre.
- THE COIN. Four things at once, found by zooming a dpr 3 render 8x and then by sampling the rim in 36 sectors: (1) the fill was `radial-gradient(...)` + a colour on a 1px-bordered circle with the default `background-repeat`/origin, so the gradient tiled under the border: the border's top strip showed the tile's dark bottom row and its bottom strip the bright top row - the flat cut along the top and the bright seam along the bottom (the `.class-bubble` has carried `no-repeat` + `border-box` for this since 342); (2) `inset 0 1px 1px white` at the top and `inset 0 -3px 6px black` at the bottom, a lit hairline and a dark crescent; (3) a 16px halo that the card's overflow cut off on a short phone (8px of padding); (4) `.cc-glow`, a -30% / -25% ellipse at opacity .5 whose gradient was still coloured at the end of its rounded box: a hard-edged lit disc behind the coin. Now: the fill is clipped to the padding box and does not repeat, centred and symmetric (nothing about the coin has a top or a bottom); the rim is the same white at every angle over the card; the only shadow is an 8px halo (the card's smallest padding); the glow is a box at the card's corner (min(100%, 13rem) x min(100%, 9rem)) whose gradient radii end on that box's own right and bottom edges, so nothing is cut inside the card. Same CSS for every `.cc-emblem` - the sign-up and the Classes screen share it. The Home class button and the class list it opens (`.class-bubble`, `.csi-bubble`) are a different object (frosted glass, set on purpose in 342) and already had `no-repeat`; they were not changed. No SVG filter anywhere.
- GATE: tools/check-b384-classcards.py. A: the two cards one height (1px) on 11 sign-up viewports in every pick state, neither card changes with a pick, and the Classes screen on 4 widths with none/one/both enrolled. B: the coin at dpr 3 with the card's background and glow flattened, 36 sectors, the rim's peak minus the mean of a band outside / inside it. Tolerance read off the fixed render: spread at most 1.4 (inner) / 4.3 (outer), top-90 and bottom-90 sector means within 1.7 of the mean; set at 3 / 6 / 3 (the unfixed build: inner spread 40-92, outer 28-32). Sampling uses pixel CENTRES (-.5) - without it a half-pixel shift reads as an uneven rim at a 1px border; and the peak along the radius rather than one band, for the same reason. C: the coin plus the halo's own computed reach, and the glow box, inside the card and every clipping ancestor. FAILS on 1c91137 (24 checks: A on the three short phones, C on every coin and glow, B on every coin); passes on this build.
- Chromium cannot show how iOS draws the 1px rim or the halo's blur on a real screen; the rim and the shadow have been measured here, not on a phone.

## Build 384 round 19 - the bottom tab with a mouse (Windows computer)

- REPORT: Madison, on a Windows computer: "clicking through the bottom tab is very laggy and doesn't work ... IT IS ALMOST UNUSABLE". Read with a real mouse (page.mouse down/up, never a script's click()), Windows' user agent, no touch, 1366x768 / 1536x864 / 1920x1080 at DPR 1-1.25, 4x and 6x CPU throttle, `--disable-gpu`. Chromium here is not a Windows GPU: nothing below is a frame time.
- NOT FOUND, MEASURED: no click was ever lost on the four tabs (Home, Profile, Leaderboard, Calendar; academy) or the Fire Code four (Home, Profile, Stats, Settings) - 20 paced clicks and 12 quick ones per class and size, none lost, at 4x and 6x CPU, GPU on and off. `document.elementFromPoint` at every visible tab's centre is the tab (or a child of it) at all three viewports in both classes. Stats and Settings are `display:none` in the academy by design (the laptop bar there is Home / Profile / Leaderboard / Calendar / Start), so "Stats and Settings do nothing" on the academy's bar is a click at (0,0).
- FOUND AND FIXED (index.html, `setupBottomTabs`):
  1. A MOUSE PRESS RAISED A FINGER'S LENS. `lensDown()` ran for every press: a spring simulated in script (~25ms of the press at 1x), the whole glass bar scaled up and back over ~500ms with its backdrop blur re-drawn each step, the landing planned on the release on the thread that is also building the new screen. Now `lensDown(clientX, mouse)` returns at once for `pointerType === "mouse"` - the path reduced motion already takes (`lensG = null`): the grey platter steps to the tab (a transform), the screen follows. Touch and pen keep the lens. A mouse slide still drags the platter tab to tab.
  2. A PRESS LET GO OFF THE BAR NEVER ENDED. A finger's touch is the bar's until it lifts; a mouse is not, so press on a tab, move 200px up, release: `pointerup` went to the page, not `navrow` - `tab-held` stayed on `<html>`, the lens stayed up (bar swollen, `lens-up`), `tabDragActive` stayed true, the page's warm-ups (`#bottomtabs-lens.is-up` waits) held, until the next press on the bar. A capture listener on `window` ends the press (as a cancel) when its release is not on the bar. (Pointer capture on press is NOT the fix: a captured press's click lands on the row, not the tab - the comment above the slop says so.)
  3. ENTER ON A FOCUSED TAB STARTED STUDYING. The run's "Enter for the next question" is a document keydown that clicks `#nextbtn` (on Home, the Start pill's float button) and preventDefaults - so Tab to Profile + Enter opened the modes instead. The handler now leaves Enter to a focused control of `.bottomtabs, .back-link, .navsegment, .chatdock`.
  4. THE KEYBOARD HAD NO PLACE AND NO FOCUS. `.bottomtab:focus{outline:none}` left a keyboard with no ring, and `navigateTab` blurred the tab after every open (a key's click included), sending Tab back to the top of the page. `.bottomtab:focus-visible` has a 2px white ring now; the blur is skipped for a trusted click with `detail === 0` (a key).
  5. Escape closes a unit's details (the held press on a unit card) as it closes every other card.
- WHERE THE TIME GOES (not changed; for the next round): a tab switch at 1x is ~100-230ms of main thread on this machine (Home the largest: ~8k elements restyled over ~70 style recalcs, `syncStartAction` ~30ms on the Start pill joining or leaving the bar, `place()` of the class button, a build ~50-60ms), no task over ~60ms. With animations switched off (`*{animation:none}`) the total did not move (1218 -> 1031, inside the noise), so it is build + style + layout, not the SVG loops. The ember-dot / flare / eye animations show as ~300 style invalidations per switch each but are a few elements a frame. Idle with the mouse still: Home ~12-16% of the main thread, the Leaderboard ~26% (rows' art, Paint x545 in 4s), the Calendar <1% - the first-launch flip-book recorders (`orbitAnimYield`, cached afterwards) are most of Home's. The `:has()` rules rooted at `body`/`.wrap`/`html` (`body:has(.screen-home-actual){--home-bar}`, `.wrap:has(> #stage > .screen-home-actual){overflow:clip}`) make a Home mount a whole-subtree restyle; that is the lever if a computer is still slow.
- GATE: tools/check-b384-mouse.py (1366x768 and 1920x1080, academy and Fire Code, a mouse only, Windows UA): every click lands, a quick run ends on the last tab, no lens under a mouse, a press let go off the bar ends, a mouse slide, Tab + Enter + focus ring, and the controls walk (Start, modes, units, Select all, held press, Escape, Begin, answer, Enter, number key, Space, leaderboard boards, chat, daily question). The median click-to-screen (button up to the screen painted, read in the page) at 4x CPU is held to 900ms, not 600: the sandbox is shared and a median of 500-620ms was seen with the same code under load.
- ONLY A REAL WINDOWS MACHINE CAN CONFIRM: the felt lag (a GPU re-drawing a blur(7px) backdrop under a scaled bar, DWM compositing, 125%/150% display scaling with CSS `zoom:.9` on the bar), a touchscreen laptop (touch presses keep the lens), a precision touchpad's click and tap-to-click timing, Edge vs Chrome, high-refresh displays, and the real cost of the first-launch recorders on a weak CPU.
### Build 384 (round 18) - Safari in a tab: no hard line at the top or bottom of the page (NOT on main)

## Build 384, round 19: the page viewer on a computer (branch r19-viewer, cut from af5725d = 384.1; no build bump here)

Madison, on a Windows computer: "when opening the view page of code it was absolutely massive and it didn't look like a normal page on a computer? ... We need this app to be functioning perfectly on the computer." The Fire Code "Show the whole page" / "Show the whole book page" viewer (`ifcOpenViewer`, ifc/ifc-viewer.js's `paintPages`) and Enlarge.
- WHAT WAS WRONG. `.ifc-vz-card` was `width:100%` of the window (inset 12px) and `.ifc-vz-pages canvas{width:100% !important}` fitted every page to the card's WIDTH. A letter page is 1.29 times taller than wide, so at 1920x1080 it was 1878px wide and 2430px tall: a third of one page on the screen, the highlight (at 60% down the page) below the fold, the bar 1896px wide with its title at one end and the buttons at the other. At 1366x768 the page was 1324x1713, at 2560x1440 2518x3258. Enlarge (a cut picture, fitted to the width) was the same, 1878px wide. The wheel panned, but there was no keyboard at all, Ctrl + wheel was a jump (a mouse notch is deltaY 100, so exp(-1) = 0.37x), and while it was up the keys 1-4 and Enter still answered / advanced the question behind it (the drill's document keydown handler). The card picture in the answer card was never the problem: on a desktop the drill is a ~850px column and the picture is the card's width.
- NOW. The card is `flex:0 1 64rem` centred (on a phone it still shrinks to the window less 12px each side, so a phone is as it was: page 398px at 440 wide, the same as af5725d). `layout()` in `ifcOpenViewer` sets the width of `.ifc-vz-pages`: the page fitted to the window's HEIGHT (so one whole page is on the screen), never wider than 60rem, never wider than the room, never narrower than 22rem (a phone on its side, a letterbox window) - at 1920x1080 a page is 747x967, at 1366x768 506x655, at 2560x1440 960x1243. `z` is the zoom from that fitted page (1 = whole page; limit 5x; the buttons step 1.25 with a mouse and 1.5 on touch); "Fit width" / "Fit page" go between it and the room's width (hidden where the two are the same: a phone). The padding zooms with the page, so the width fit is `(room - 2 pad) / (page - 2 pad)`, not room / page (that came out 4px short). Enlarge (`fit:"width"`) is capped at 2.6 CSS px to a point on a window 900px or wider (`opts.ppt` carries the renderer's pixels to a point), so a book column's cut is not 3.6px to a point. A computer's mouse paints the pictures at up to 4.4 device pixels to a point (`ifcDeskScale`: 2.2 -> 3.08 at DPR 1) so a zoomed page stays sharp; touch and anything under 900px keep the old scales.
- KEYS (all of them are the viewer's while it is up: `stopPropagation` on every key but those with Ctrl/Meta/Alt that are not zoom): Esc closes; + / = / - / _ zoom (also with Ctrl, and Ctrl + 0, so the browser's own zoom is not what answers) and 0 resets; arrows scroll 64px (left / right switch page where the view holds one whole page and there are two); Page Up / Page Down / Space move a page at a time (to the next page at the fitted zoom, a screenful when zoomed); Home / End; Tab cycles inside the viewer and Esc gives focus back to the button that opened it. Enter / Space on a focused button press it. The wheel scrolls (deltaMode 1 and 2 handled); Ctrl + wheel and a trackpad pinch zoom the PAGE about the pointer, a step of at most exp(0.4) per event; the wheel over the dimmed app around the card moves nothing; a mouse drag pans a zoomed page (grab cursor). A slim marker at the right edge shows where the view is on a tall column of pages (the page moves by a transform, so there is no scrollbar).
- GATE: tools/check-b384-viewerdesk.py. Windows desktop tab, 1366x768 / 1536x864 / 1920x1080 / 2560x1440 at DPR 1 and 1.5: page width <= min(60rem, window - 24), centred (2px), whole in the window's height, bar and Done at its top right inside the window, no sideways scroll; the soft tint inside the page, from the cited lines' top to their bottom (pt, read off the booklet's own lines), on the screen, the deeper gold on the cited words (HC 5609.4.1), the same place on the page at 1.5x; + / - / 0 / 40 presses stop at 1x and 5x; Ctrl + wheel zooms the page (defaultPrevented) by a step; the wheel scrolls a zoomed page, a drag pans, Page Down moves on; Fit width reaches the room and back; 1, 2, Enter do nothing behind it; Esc closes and the app is as it was; Enlarge whole in the window. Phone (440x956, touch, installed) page 398px (as af5725d), card inset 12px, no Fit button, double tap zooms, Done closes; iPad 834x1194 and 1194x834 inside the window with the page whole in the height. With IFC_BOOK (the owner's PDF, only read): IFC 1004.5 and IFC 1013 at 1920x1080 and 1366x768 the same geometry and highlight legs. Run against af5725d it FAILS (32 checks in --quick: page 1878px / 1324px wide and 2430 / 1713 tall, highlight below the screen, the keys + - 0 do nothing, Ctrl + wheel jumps 5x, 1 / 2 / Enter answer and advance the question behind it, iPad landscape 1152px wide and 1491 tall). Zoom stress at 5x (12 presses) occasionally crashes this sandbox's Chromium under load (software raster of a 3700x4800px layer); a real browser tiles it. check-b384-codeopen (2) fails the same way on af5725d and on this build when the machine's load average is 20 (long tasks), so it is load, not this change.
- WHAT ONLY A REAL WINDOWS MACHINE CAN CONFIRM: Chromium here has no Windows font rendering, no real precision touchpad (the pinch arrives as ctrl + wheel in Chrome and Edge on Windows; the gate sends that event itself), no 125% / 150% display scaling with its fractional layout rounding (DPR 1.25 and 1.5 were run, but not as the OS does it), and no Edge / Firefox (Firefox sends wheel in lines, deltaMode 1: handled, not run). Safari on a Mac pinches with gesture events, not ctrl + wheel: not handled (the buttons and keys work).
### Round 18 (on 384.1) - the splash scaled off-centre as it faded; two tour gates that raced the owed-unlock sequence

- **THE SPLASH'S WORD AND BAR SLID 4% UP AND LEFT WHILE IT FADED (a 384 regression, found by check-fixes' "splash off-centre by -5,-3 in an oversized box" on iPad mini 6th gen 1133x670 browser and iPad mini home-button 1024x768 installed, on a loaded machine only).** 384 added `#splashscreen.splash-hide #splash-group{ scale:1.04 }`. The group is centred by `left/top` (in pixels, from the script under the markup) plus `transform:translate(-50%,-50%)`, and the `scale` PROPERTY is applied after the transform, about the default origin - the middle of the group's LAYOUT box, half a group-size down and right of the screen's middle. So the scale also moved the painted middle by 4% of that offset: -4.5,-2.4 on a phone (a 233x120 group), -6,-3.6 on an iPad Pro 11". Nearly invisible (it is fading), but a real jump from centred to drifting on every launch, and the gate read it whenever the splash's own timer reached the fade during its measurement; alone on a quiet machine both devices passed. Absent from 383 (no scale rule there). Fix: `transform-origin:0 0` in that one rule - the group's top-left is where left/top put it, the screen's middle, so the scale is about the visual centre; the origin changes while the scale is still 1 and only `scale` transitions, so nothing jumps. GATE: tools/check-b384-splashhide.py (puts the hidden class on by hand, waits the transition out, measures the group's painted middle against the viewport's on 440x956 and 834x1194, and that the scale really is in effect): FAILS on af5725d (-4.4,-2.4 and -6.5,-3.6), passes on this build.
- **KNOWN, OLDER THAN 384, MEASURED AND LEFT AGAIN: check-fixes' GREY BAR on an SE 1st gen in a Safari tab held sideways (568x260), 7 levels at (284,221), limit 6.** Identical figure on live 383 (run against 383 with its APP_BUILD matched to version.json, or the gate reloads for the update), and in this file since 279 (10 levels then, 7 since 334). Cause as in the 11% note on body::before: Home is taller than the 260px viewport, so the page scrolls and the html fallback (pinned to one viewport at the document's top) sits that far off the fixed layer at the bottom edge. It shows only where the fixed layer fails to paint, on a phone sideways in Safari; no cheap change makes a fixed layer and a scrolling one agree at every offset without dimming the bottom glow for everyone.
- **check-tours' classtip and studytip read "0 of 1 steps rendered" on the phone, 3 of 3 runs alone - a fixture race, not a tip that never shows.** Both tips wait for a calm Home. The seed is a high-level account, so an unlock sequence is owed and boot starts it on its own timer (`homeUnlockPlaying`, ~5-7s, state rather than a node); `weekRecapBlocked()` (reached through `a2hsBusy()`) holds the tips for all of it, and the gate's fixed 8-9s wait ended just before the tip's third calm beat (tip up at 10-12s in a debug run, 2s in another, depending on when the timer fired). The app is right to wait. The fixture now marks the owed unlocks shown and clears any spotlight (`CALM_HOME`), and a scenario with a `min` polls up to 25s more for `#tour-tooltip` instead of reading it at a fixed second; a tip whose target matches nothing still reads 0 of 1 (checked with `.class-bubble` renamed). 6 of 6 clean runs after.
- Machine note: siblings were running gates at load 29 while this was done; check-b384-classcards (rim evenness, iPad/Pro Max signup) and getstarted (frame gaps of 600-1200ms on the laptop) each failed once and passed on re-run, classfloor hit TargetClosedError once. Chromium cannot show how iOS draws the splash's fade; the centring was measured here, not on a phone.
### 384 r20 (r20-signin, cut from 844c314 = 384.3, live) - signing in to Fire Code no longer unlocks what the academy held
Madison: "people signing into the fire code class, they unlocked the character of the placeholder of that one that they have selected from the academy class". Reproduced on 844c314 (tools/check-b384-signinchars.py fails there): an account wearing a CLOWN or an ASTRONAUT in the academy came into Fire Code wearing it, unlocked, with the Customize tile unlocked.
- THE LEAK. `store.legacyChars` ("kept from before", the pre-243 rules) makes `isLockedCharacter()` false. A Fire Code store's first load seeds itself from the academy's copy (the avatar among it) and `applyLoadedData()` then has no list, so it computed one: `legacyCharsFromRanks()` adds whoever WEARS a clown or astronaut, so the academy's selected character became "kept" in Fire Code. Same for `migrateHive384()` (wearing the Hive, or `busiestDay() >= HIVE_DAY`) whenever the copy's `hiveMoved384` was not yet written (an academy copy that has not saved since 384). Both then travel: the list is written to Fire Code's own cloud document (progress/<code>__ifc), unioned back by `mergeSameAccount`, and `ensureUnlocksShown()` seeds "shown" with what is held, so no card announced it. `ifcLookCheck()` could not help: the list says it is not locked.
- THE FIX, at the root. (1) `legacyHeld(id)`: false in Fire Code, used by `isLockedCharacter()` and `hiveKept()`: the list is the academy's history and Fire Code (built at 328) has none, so a Fire Code character is unlocked by this class's own challenge or rank and nothing else (the Sprinkler Head: host three Virtual Room matches). (2) Fire Code no longer creates the list: `legacyCharsFromRanks()` returns [], `migrateSheriff324()` / `migrateHive384()` only set their flags there. (3) The first-visit seed no longer copies `seenUnlocks` (the dots behind new things are the class's own; the academy's marks named characters Fire Code had not unlocked). (4) `ifcLookCheck()` also acts at launch on the leak's own mark (the worn character is on the kept list), not only when it equals the academy's. (5) `ifcCharsRepair384()`, in Fire Code: an unlock queued for a locked character is dropped; once (`ifcCharsFixed384`) the kept list goes off the copy and a character it had marked shown/seen comes off those marks while still locked (earning it for real then announces it). It runs at `markCloudConfirmed()` (after `ifcLookCheck(true)`), after every later merge in `syncSameAccount()` once the launch has heard the server (a copy arriving from an older device wearing a locked character), and at launch for a copy with no sync.
- THE MIGRATION. Touches only a Fire Code copy with something on its kept list or a locked character worn (people who wore a Clown, Astronaut or Hive in the academy when they first opened Fire Code, and any copy another device wrote that way). A locked character worn goes to the first starter, quietly; the kept list is emptied; counts, points, anything earned, the academy's copy and the cloud account are untouched (checked: points 4321 unchanged, an earned Marksman and a Clown earned by five Virtual Room wins both stay). The flag `ifcCharsFixed384` is a persisted field (default in `applyLoadedData`: done in the academy, not done in a Fire Code copy that lacks it; reset sets it; OR-merged in `mergeSameAccount` and `mergeLeavingAccount`), and the academy's flag is never seeded into Fire Code. The Hive keep (migrateHive384) is unchanged in the academy: whoever unlocked it under the 500-a-day rule keeps it there (check-b384-hivekept).
- WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. A Fire Code copy whose old build already wrote `legacyChars` and that another device pushes back is simply never read there. A first visit on a device that signs in where Fire Code's cloud document already exists still takes the academy's name and starter from the seed (the seed is stamped newer than the cloud copy, so the merge keeps its scalar fields): a person's Fire Code character picked on another device can come back as the starter after a sign-in. Not changed here: it is not an unlock, and lowering `lastModified` of the seed touches every first visit.
- GATE: tools/check-b384-signinchars.py: A (fresh device, academy wearing 12 characters), A2 (academy copy without its Hive flag), B (Fire Code's document carries the leak; on a fresh device, and the migration on a device that has it: repaired once, the earned kept, left alone after, no-sync repaired at launch), C (the first class switch, really switched), D (sign-up for both: the starter comes across), E (the real Sign in screen, Fire Code alone), F (the academy afterwards: its own kept characters kept, Fire Code's nothing in it). Asserts shape: nobody wears a character the class has not earned, nothing unlocked that its own challenge or rank has not earned (read with the kept list emptied), Customize tiles, no queued unlock or Home card, the academy's saved copy byte for byte. Fails on 844c314 (clown, astronaut and, where the academy copy lacks its Hive flag or Fire Code's document carries it, hive; 22 of 44 checks fail there, 44 of 44 pass after). The other gates were run too: check-sync, check-b383-ifcsync, check-b384-lbclasses, check-unlocks, check-b384-hivekept, check-b384-hivechallenge, check-b384-fcchars2 pass; check-b383-classes (5), check-b384-r9-chars (H) and check-b384-classes-open (7b, 9-12, 14) fail identically on 844c314 (sandbox-related, not this change); check-sync 4c is a known race (fails ~1 in 3 on 844c314 alone).
- Under load a page sometimes crashes (TargetClosedError / "Page crashed"): the gate re-runs the walk from a fresh context.

### Build 384 (round 18), second commit - the tab bar's lag and the swipe in a Safari tab (NOT on main)

Madison: "The bottom tab is a little laggy", "The bottom tab STILL lags when swiping", then "The bottom tab is nearly perfect, could be a
slight smoother. THE SWIPING AND SLIDING FUNCTION IS TERRIBLE". All of it in a Safari tab (the installed app's slide he called "100x
better" in 383). What differs in a tab is the toolbar, so that is where this looked:

  one the page has at rest (~47pt at 383's measurement), so Welcome, Home and the boards were that much scrollable (his Welcome frames
  show the scroll indicator on a screen with nothing to scroll). Any touch that drifted vertically - a slide, a swipe - scrolled the
  document, Safari shrank its toolbar, the layout viewport changed height under the fixed tab bar. Now html.is-browser{min-height:100dvh}
  on touch devices: the root's box is the page's own viewport (the paper layer still reaches the bottom; the layers sized in lvh are
  no-repeat on the canvas beyond it). Chromium's lvh equals its dvh, so the gate models Safari's by substituting calc(100dvh + 47px)
  for 100lvh in the served page: Welcome and Home document 844px in a 797px viewport on the old build, 797 now (and the same on a 16, an SE).

  slideBubbleToActiveTab, which measures then writes; the splash's place(), still running for a splash long gone; syncChatDock;
  syncTestPin; alignNavChat; syncBottomInsetClass; syncFieldFloor; backToTopRoom's 40 measures...). Wrapped with a listener timer
  (init script) on Home at 4x CPU, a viewport growing then shrinking 47px in 94 frames: the resize listeners alone cost ~2.6s of script
  (onBarResize 1416ms = 15ms a frame, place 468, syncChatDock 233, syncTestPin 126, alignNavChat 95...). A new script right after the
  status-bar one (touch devices only) governs window "resize" listeners: (1) one that has answered a size is not called again for it,

  before. After, the same burst: the wrapper's own cost 335ms and getBoundingClientRect reads in the burst Home 692 -> ~350, Profile 2546 ->
  ~1400 (the rest are the visual viewport's and the page's own listeners, not governed). The tab bar itself sits by CSS
  (--tabs-bottom) and was never the thing moving.
- NOT CHANGED: the bar's drag (touch-action:none already), the slide's code (383/384's lens, FLIP and holds - their gates pass), the
  visual viewport's listeners. What the swipe feels like on his phone cannot be read in Chromium; if it is still bad after this, a
  bug report's tab timings (class26e.tabperf) and `edges` are what to read.
- GATE tools/check-b384-safaribottom.py: noscroll (Welcome, Home, three iPhones, lvh modelled 47px taller) and govern (the governor's

  from the viewport's bottom when the toolbar collapses). All fail on af5725d.

## 384 r13 - friend codes find people with no academy board row (build 384.10)

Madison: "Friends codes aren't working, they are saying it says no one in the class has that code." All 41 live board rows carry an `fcode` and Cap's / Madison's row, academy copy and Fire Code copy agree, so the data is whole; the LOOKUP was the gap. sendFriendRequest only read the academy leaderboard rows this device already held: a person in Fire Code alone has no board row (the new Fire Code class), and a board read before somebody joined never had them.
Now: (1) the presence beat (`c[pub]`, already written every few minutes) carries `f`, the friend code - already public on every board row, never a sync code - and the lookup falls back to it; a person found that way has no row for a request to sit on, so it goes to their mailbox. (2) A code in neither is asked of the cloud once as a one-document query (`leaderboard where fcode == code, limit 1`), on a miss only, then retried. (3) The refusal reads "No one in your classes has that code yet. They may need to update and open the app once." (a friend still on an older build has no `f` until they update and open the app).
Gate `tools/check-b384-friendcode.py` (fails on 384.9); check-friends and check-b384-friends pass.
## 385 - Fire Code's own leaderboard, and Stats moves into Profile (NOT on main, waiting for Madison)

Madison: "fire code is gonna get the leaderboard. So move stats to profile as a top tab option. The leaderboard for fire code. It will be an entirely different leaderboard than the academy one. They will look the same but ifc one will only be for the people in the class. In other words, every class will have their own leaderboard. Different about the fire code one, there won't be a weekly one or whatever. Just hundos and overall."

WHAT IS SHARED AND WHAT IS NOT
- Shared: the Leaderboard screen (showRankings, renderRankingRows, the pill switcher, search, Find me, the person card, the rank/level/badge columns), boardNumbersOf, rankOfEntry, fixBoardLevel. Not shared: the rows, the listener, the opt-in. The academy's board is the `leaderboard` collection, one document a person, exactly as before; its code paths are unchanged (every new branch is `window.NOVA_CLASS === "ifc"`). Fire Code's board is ONE document, `vrooms/lb-ifc-v1` = { kind:"board", cls:"ifc", rows:{ <public id>: row } }, read only by the Fire Code copy (classBoardRows, never leaderboardRows, which Fire Code's friends use). `CLASS_BOARD_DOC` maps class -> document, so a third class is one more line.
- Fire Code's two boards: Overall (rankingBoardsFor() drops `week` in Fire Code) and Hundos. No weekly board, no last week's podium, no weekly rank observation (observeWeeklyRank skipped), no week recap on opening (scheduleWeekRecap skipped), no weekly fields in the row. The empty state says "Nobody has joined the Fire Code leaderboard yet." Its tour and the Settings hint name Fire Code and its two boards.
- Row = firstName, avatarChar, accent, correct, level, badges, hundos, rankFloor, xp, tests, banner, lastModified. Not in it: week, weekPoints, prevWeek*, wk, pwk, fcode, freq, facc, inv, cinv, seenAt, mystery. The field name is the academy account's public id (publicIdOf: Fire Code's friends identity), so a tap on a row opens the same person card and its friend button works. NO SYNC CODE anywhere (Fire Code's syncCode is "<code>__ifc"; neither it nor the academy's appears as a key or a value; gate scans `vrooms` and `leaderboard`).

WHY `vrooms` AND NOT `leaderboard` (the old-client invisibility proof)
- Every phone on 383/384.x lists the whole `leaderboard` collection and draws any document in it as an academy classmate (only ids shaped XXXX-XXXX and rows with no firstName are skipped). A Fire Code row there would be a stranger on every old phone for days. Nothing before this build reads `vrooms/lb-ifc-v1`: they read presence-v1, inbox-<id>, chat and room documents by their own ids; the only two listings of `vrooms` (seedVroomHistory/seedVroomTop3, once per account, and the open-rooms search, `where open == true`) look for `participants` / `open`, which the board document does not have.
- Proven in tools/check-b384-fcboard.py section 5: the previous build (git show ca5f8f0, as the academy) over the same stub holding the academy's rows in `leaderboard` AND Fire Code's rows in `vrooms/lb-ifc-v1` lists only academy people on its board and Friends, its scans read the board as nothing, it writes nothing to it, no page errors; and the CONTROL puts the same people into `leaderboard` and that build DOES draw them (so the check can see them). 3a6675d (the build before 384.8) reads the same collections the same way.
- Fire Code can write it with no rule change: its scoped handle (ifcSocialMay) already writes `vrooms` and only reads `leaderboard`; the invariant "Fire Code never writes `leaderboard`" still holds. ASSUMPTION I cannot test here: `vrooms` accepts a document with this id and shape (presence-v1, inbox-* and chat documents are written there today, so it should). If the live rules reject it, the board shows only the viewer and nothing breaks.

WRITES AND BUDGET (free tier: 20k writes / 50k reads a day, class ~40)
- No timer, no polling. The row goes where the academy's goes: after each account write (afterAccountWrite), the score fields waiting ROW_SCORE_PUSH_MS (5 min) between writes, the end of a run (flushLeaderboardRow from summarize), launch, putting the app away (publishNow/pagehide). Unlike the academy's flush, a row whose signature equals the last one written is NOT written again (a launch or hide that changed nothing costs nothing). The write is a transaction (1 read + 1 write) that refuses to write numbers behind the row (rowBehind), as the academy's. A person who opts out or resets removes only their own field (update with FieldValue.delete); the switch acts at once in Fire Code (the academy's waits for the account write).
- Estimate, ~40 people on a study day: ~10 row writes each = ~400 writes and ~400 transaction reads. Reads for watching: one document read per open board on opening plus one per row write on each phone that has the board open (say 5 open at a time: ~2,000). Under 3% of the writes and ~5% of the reads. The academy's reads do not grow at all (they never see this document). One hot document: ~0.5 writes/s at the busiest minute, below Firestore's ~1/s per document; a collision is a transaction retry.
- leaving Fire Code (finishLeaveClass("ifc") in the academy) and the academy abandoning a public id (setSyncCode) delete that id's Fire Code field too; Fire Code's reset and remote reset delete their own.

OPT-IN (decision for Madison)
- leaderboardOptIn on Fire Code's own store, Settings > Leaderboard & Privacy is now a real switch there (copy names Fire Code and its two boards; each class is listed Shown/Hidden, the academy's Fire Code entry read from the saved Fire Code copy). The default is ON, as the academy's is: a first Fire Code visit seeds from the academy's choice (hidden there stays hidden); every existing Fire Code copy (which was "off" only because the first-visit seed wrote it, nobody could choose) is moved on ONCE per device (localStorage class26e.boardseed.385) unless the person hid themselves in the academy. To make it opt-in only instead: the seed line (`seed.leaderboardOptIn = a.leaderboardOptIn !== false`) and the one-shot block under "FIRE CODE HAS A LEADERBOARD NOW". No new store field.

BARS AND TABS
- Fire Code's bar: Home, Profile, Leaderboard, Settings (Settings stays: no Calendar). #bottomtab-stats stays in the markup, hidden for good. Laptop: the same four, Start in the bar on Home as before. Profile's top tabs in Fire Code: Profile, Stats (Settings is its bar tab, built alone on request); the academy's stay Profile, Stats, Settings. PROFILE_TABS order = the buttons' (profileTabOrder is derived from the defs). Test history lights Profile and says "Back to Profile" (returns to Stats). showStatsScreen() = showProfile("stats"), so old links work. Tips: the main-menu tour has the Leaderboard step in Fire Code (no Stats step), Profile's tour points at the Stats tab. Nova's leaderboard/calendar answers updated.
- Gates: tools/check-b384-fcboard.py (new; fails on ca5f8f0: 20 checks), check-b384-lbclasses.py (new rule; fails on the previous build), and brought up to the new structure: check-b383-ifcsync (board document allowed among Fire Code's writes), check-b384-mouse (Fire Code bar), check-b384-toptabs (Profile and board switchers in Fire Code), check-b384-walk, check-b382-ifc, check-b332, check-b342, check-b328-classes, check-b384-friends, check-centering (Fire Code's leaderboard screens). Failures that are the same on the previous build: check-b382-board CLS 0.0571, check-b328-classes "academy's saved copy byte-for-byte". check-b384-toptabs' two-segment "it lands" frame counts flake under load.
- RULE CHANGE NEEDED: none. (If `vrooms` ever gets a per-document id/shape rule, `lb-<class>-v1` with a `rows` map must be allowed.)
## Build 384 r21: the class switch is one smooth motion (Madison: "There's a bad transition when switching between classes.")

He did not say what was bad, so it was measured: the real switch driven (class button, its list, the class) with a CDP screencast for what a person sees and an rAF log kept across the reload for what the page was doing (tools/b384_switchfx_lib.py; tools/record-b384-switch.py lays any switch out as a frame-by-frame contact sheet, `--device phone|se|laptop --cpu 4 --reduce --against OLD`). A switch is still a reload into the other class's stores (nothing about STORE_KEY, class26e.activeclass or the stores changed); what changed is everything a person sees between the tap and the settled Home.

WHAT WAS WRONG ON 3a6675d (iPhone 17 Pro Max, installed, 1x CPU, academy -> Fire Code; ms from the tap):
- The cover held on a clock: 2.5s from the tap (`arrive.dur`), whatever Home was doing. Home (planet, button, 4 tabs) was built at ~0.85-1.0s and sat behind it for 1.6-1.8s; then the splash faded for .75s. Tap to Home 3.4-3.5s; the same Home was ready 2.5s earlier.
- The cover's word, line and bar came in at full opacity the instant the cover started to fade, over a Home that was only dimmed to .22 - Home's own NOVA and the cover's NOVA were both on show (frames 250-300ms); and going out, the splash's NOVA faded over Home's NOVA again (cover's word .5 against Home's .5 at the same frame), the group drifting back 4% (`scale:1.04`) as it went.
- The class list stayed open under the cover until the page was gone (never closed into the button).
- The splash's line changed under the planet ("opening Fire Code..." -> "syncing chapter progress..." -> "booting core runtime..." -> "ready.") for a screen that was only waiting for a reload.
- Home was not eased in: it was simply there, under a thinning splash (the planet and flares visible at full strength in the first frames of the fade).
- In a browser tab the status bar / Safari's bars kept the class left's colour under the cover until the reload (they were told the splash's colour only by the NEW page's head script).
- From a sign-in or a sign-up (`enterAccountClass`) the stage was emptied FIRST and the cover faded in over an empty stage.
- Reduced motion: every transition is off (`[data-reduce-motion] *{transition:none}`), so the cover was a hard cut both ways.
- After a given-up switch (a reload that never came, 60s) the old screen came back with its list still open and Home still dimmed (#stage.class-list-open stays until closeStack).
NOT faults (measured, written down so nobody chases them): no white or black frame in Chromium (the cover is #0A0A0A + the glow the splash has, 19-22 light the whole hold); no seam across the reload (the head script's `class-arrive-pre` picture is the loader's last frame to 0.3 levels); the tab bar never shows the old class's items after the cover is up (it has 4 items in each class on a phone, 5 on a laptop in the academy).

THE NEW SEQUENCE (phone, 1x CPU: tap to Home settled ~1.6s; 4x CPU ~3.4-3.6s; all of it the page loading in the middle):
1. Tap: the class list folds into the class button (`classListRetract`: `.is-open` off, Home stays stepped back by `#stage.class-list-open` so it does not brighten under the cover; `classListClose` gives it all back if the switch is given up). The cover (`#class-switch-loader`, #0A0A0A, the splash's own colour) fades in over .24s, opacity only; its mark (word, line, bar) comes in AFTER it (`#csl-group`: .14s delay, .16s fade), so Home's word and the cover's are never both on show. Reload at +270ms (+170 reduced motion).
2. In a browser tab the status bar / theme-color and html's background take the splash colour at the same moment, under the cover (`splashOwnsFrame()` is true while `html.class-switching`; the app's colour is handed back as the lift starts, as every splash does). Installed apps: iOS reads theme-color once, nothing to change.
3. The reload happens under the cover. The new page paints the loader's last frame from its first frame (`class-arrive-pre`, unchanged), then its splash with the bar still creeping (`csw-creep`, negative delay = time since the tap), ONE line of text.
4. The cover is held at least `CSW_HOLD_MS` (900ms) from the tap (a floor, so a fast reload is not a flicker) and then only until Home is BUILT (`arriveReady()` in the splash script: `[data-screen=home]` with the planet and `#nextbtn`, the tab bar not hidden, a screen that is not Home - a sign-in or sign-up carrying on - after 1.5s up, at the latest SPLASH_STAGE_WAIT_MS 6s as every launch). It lifts after the boot script's own tail has run (the poll is a timer, so it is behind the synchronous script), so the lift is not under a busy main thread.
5. The lift: the bar runs to full (120ms, WAAPI) while the mark goes first (.12s opacity) and the cover after it (.3s opacity, no scale: `splash.class-lift`); the same frame adds `body.class-rise`: planet (`scale .96 -> 1` + opacity), then greeting + Start button + class button, then the tab bar (`translate 10px -> 0` + opacity, .4-.42s, 0 / .06 / .12s delays: three steps; `translate`/`scale` not `transform`, so a phone's own planet transform and the bar's centring stand). The status bar colour is handed back in that frame. The splash element goes 450ms later (800 on a launch).
6. Reduced motion (the app's setting or the system's): the cover and the lift are plain linear cross-fades (.14s, set inline with `!important` because `[data-reduce-motion] *` turns every transition off), no rise, no bar animation; `class26e.classswitch.calm` carries the choice across the reload.
7. `enterAccountClass` no longer empties the stage first: `switchClass(..., { clear: true })` empties it under the cover, at the reload. Anything else that calls `switchClass` (Settings' join/leave, the catalog, the book's Enroll, a sign-up) gets the same cover and lift. The "Welcome back to ..." banner (`maybeSwitchWelcome`) is unchanged and still waits for the splash to be gone and the page calm.
8. A switch whose reload never comes still gives the screen back after `CSW_GIVEUP_MS` (60s): cover off, html background and bars handed back, list shut, Home not dimmed. A new page whose Home never builds lifts after 6s.
The `sessionStorage` handoff (`class26e.classswitch`) now carries `min` and `calm` instead of `dur`; nothing else read `dur`.

BUDGETS in the gate are what the switch itself controls, measured on this machine (loaded; they have room): tap to the cover gone 2.8s at 1x / 6.5s at 4x (measured ~1.6 / ~3.5), Home built to the lift 1.0s / 2.0s (measured ~0.4), the lift .36s (.2 reduced) / .6s (measured ~.2). The old build: 3.4s, 1.8s, .57s. A phone reloading a 10MB page is slower than this machine at its first paint; what is fixed is that nothing waits on a clock any more.

GATE: tools/check-b384-switchfx.py (phone, se, laptop both ways; cpu4; reduce; settings and sign-in paths; giveup; the source). Fails on 3a6675d for the faults above (budgets, the word twice, the scale, the open list, the missing rise, the one line; with reduced motion the hard cut; from sign-in the empty stage; after a given-up switch the list and the dim). Re-run on TargetClosedError. Only a phone can confirm: the real iOS compositing of the opacity/translate/scale animations on a loaded device (Chromium's compositor is not WebKit's), whether Safari's own bars follow theme-color in the same frame, the reload's first paint on a cold or evicted cache (the loader's last frame is held by the browser only as long as the old page is), the safe-area insets under the cover and the haptic/sound on the tap.
## 384 r11 - faces per class (branch worktree-agent-afd328b9f47331311, cut from build 384.8; no build bump here)

Madison: "In the friends chat, if I look at them while in one class, I'll see what they have selected as the placeholder in the class I'm in. I guess it would be whatever class they are currently in and whatever character that is, so it may change constantly."
THE CAUSE: one account is two classes and each class has its own character, but everything social carried only the ACADEMY's id (socialMe -> the presence beat's `v`, chatSelfEntry, the mailbox, a vroom entry, the board row). A page draws ONE class's art: under IFC_ART_ON an academy id is re-skinned as a Fire Code look (IFC_CHAR_LOOK), so a friend in the academy's Marksman showed in Fire Code as a Hazmat nobody had picked or unlocked there.
THE RULE NOW: in a class, every other person is drawn wearing THEIR OWN character OF THAT CLASS. Academy page: `avatarChar` as always. Fire Code page: their Fire Code character; unknown (an older build, never opened Fire Code, not enrolled) = `classDefaultCharacter()` (the class's first free starter), never the academy id re-skinned. Your own face in your own class is `store.avatarChar` (faceCharFor says so for your public id).
WRITERS (no new write or read anywhere; the field rides what already writes, and every old field is untouched so older builds keep working):
- `socialMe()` / `socialCard()` gain `avatarCharIfc` (`ifcCharOfMe()`: in Fire Code it is store.avatarChar; in the academy page it is read from localStorage "class26e.ifc.drill.v1" - the academy page has no key mapping - only when accountClassesOf says the account is in Fire Code, validated against AVATAR_CHARACTERS, try/catch; nothing but the character id is taken from it).
- The presence beat (`presenceClassesValue`): `fv` beside `v`. Chat entries (`chatSelfEntry`, `chatPresencePatch`) and the vroom beat patch: `avatarCharIfc`. A vroom entry (`vroomMeEntry`) `avatarCharIfc`; a room doc `hostAvatarIfc` beside `hostAvatar`. The mailbox (`sendToInbox`, `sendToInboxSlot`): `avatarCharIfc`. A direct chat's other-person entry (`them`) too.
- The board row (buildLeaderboardRow) was NOT touched (leaderboard code is r21-fcboard's). Its Fire Code board can set `avatarCharIfc` on a row and faceCharFor will draw it.
READER (one function): `faceCharFor(card, pub)` (+ `faceSpanFor(card, pub)` which draws it). `card` is any board row / friend card / chat or room entry. Order in Fire Code: nova as is; your own id -> store.avatarChar; `card.avatarCharIfc`; the person's presence beat `fv` (`presenceIfcChar(pub)`); classDefaultCharacter(). The academy page returns `card.avatarChar || "ghost"` exactly as before. `friendCardFromPresence` now returns `avatarCharIfc` (their `fv`); `friendCardOf`'s chat fallback and `chatPersonOf` carry it (chatPersonOf: row, then beat, then the room entry's own); `chatPeopleOf`, the chat-list cache and `seedChatRosterFromList` keep BOTH ids and the class is chosen where it is DRAWN (the cache sits in localStorage, which both class pages share, so it must never store a resolved face).
SURFACES that now call it: chat roster chips, Members list, a friend's chat header, the chat's Friends tab rows, group-chat face clusters (list + invite peek), notification rows (invites, friend requests), the chat invite sheet, the Virtual Room invite sheet, Manage friends (personRow), the person card (and its glow colour), the friend-moment pair, paintFriendFallbacks, the name-check clash card, the Virtual Room rooms browser (host), the lobby (and its change signature, so a changed face redraws), the race markers, podiums (race and team), the battle/tug figures and winner reveal, the results chart rows. Left alone on purpose: the Leaderboard boards and the weekly recap (board data, r21-fcboard); every site that draws YOURSELF (store.avatarChar).
GATE: `tools/check-b384-faces.py` (fails against 384.8). Real boots of the academy page and the Fire Code page against the in-memory Firestore (check-vroom's), five people (both characters in a row+beat; academy only; an old-format person with a row and nothing else; one known only from the chat entry; a friend in Fire Code alone with a beat), `data-char` read off the spans in the roster, Members list, Friends tab, Manage friends, a friend's chat header, a person's card and the Virtual Room lobby, in both classes; your own entry/beat/card carry both ids and the academy page says nothing when the account is not in Fire Code.
NOT VERIFIED HERE: nothing on a real phone (this is drawing-by-id, no layout change); the race markers/podium/results rows were changed the same way as the lobby but are not driven by the gate (a full race needs several tabs: check-vroom/check-b384-vr* gates were run instead); the academy board row does not yet carry `avatarCharIfc`, so in Fire Code a classmate who is NOT a friend and is not beating (no presence entry) falls to the class starter until they join a chat or beat on a build with this change.
## Build 384 (r22) - swiping and sliding: the next-question slide, the top-tab swipe

Madison: "THE SWIPING AND SLIDING FUNCTION IS TERRIBLE" / "there is still so much lag when swiping between stuff ... I noticed on Windows computers too, that
swiping to the NEXT QUESTION had a lot of lag". Measured in Chromium at 4x CPU with real touches (CDP) and a real mouse; a phone's WebKit and a Windows GPU are not here.
- NOT DONE ON PURPOSE: swiping the page between BOTTOM tabs. It was removed by explicit request (the comment above the keydown listener near the end of
  index.html; "a swipe on Rewards while reading it could silently change tabs") and is not back. "The tab sliding/swiping function" in the notes since 383 is the bar's
  own finger slide (the glass lens); it was measured again (check-b383-tabslide, -b382-slide, -b384-mouse all pass) and not changed.
- THE NEXT QUESTION (commit b328405, in 384.8): a Next (click, Enter, tap, committed swipe) ran the bar/dock sync (syncVisibility -> syncChatDock ->
  placeDockBesidePause: offsetLeft + getComputedStyle of Pause, a style pass and layout of the whole page) 2-4 times inside the tap - for the stage swap, for the slide's
  own copy going onto <body>, and (phone) for the swipe's stand-in going on where a finger lands and off where it lifts - and read the outgoing box after putting a
  class on <html>. Now syncVisibility ignores the slide's copies (.q-slide-clone, .q-blurpair) on <body>; while a slide is under way a stage swap only marks the sync owed
  (qSyncHold / qSyncOwed) and qSlideDone runs it once in idle time (qSyncRelease; the last question's advance is not held: summarize() changes the bar); the box is read
  before the class goes on. 4x CPU (thread time, medians of 8): laptop click task 64 -> 41-51ms, forced style/layout 32 -> 13-15; Enter 56 -> 33 / 35 -> 12; phone tap
  76-85 -> 42-49 / 30 -> 12; swipe release's build 60 -> 44; dock measures inside the move 2-4 -> 0. The rest of a Next is the new question's own build
  (replaceChildren: style + layout of its panel, 13-43ms at 4x), left. Gate tools/check-b384-qslide.py.
- THE TOP-TAB SWIPE (Profile's tabs, the Leaderboard's boards; attachTabSwipe): a swipe did nothing until the finger lifted, then swapped the tab in one step; on the
  Leaderboard the next board's build (180-280ms at 4x) sat between the lift and anything on screen (first frame with the new tab 230-330ms after the release).
  Now: axis chosen once at ~10px (a finger that went down first never becomes a swipe), the content (opts.content: the visible tab's node; the board's rows) follows the
  finger by transform only (one rAF write, no reads; passive but the one touchmove that cancels the scroll; data-tabdrag marks the moving elements), a third as far where no
  tab lies that way; released past a third of the width or thrown (>0.35px/ms over the last ~100ms of moves, the last two when it rested first) it is carried off on the
  compositor (WAAPI) and the next tab's content comes in from the other side; short of that it eases back (260ms). The Leaderboard's old rows are lifted into a copy that
  stays where the finger left it while the next board is built under it (a first version carried it off first and left a bare screen for the build), then the two cross.
  Nothing starts within 20px of the left edge (the system's swipe back), inside anything that scrolls sideways (hScrolls) or [data-noswipe], or with a second finger.
  Reduce motion, or no opts.content: the plain swap as before. An opacity under 1 on the dragged list was tried and dropped: it made the whole long list a blended
  surface every frame. Gate tools/check-b384-swipe.py (every adjacent pair, both ways, 1x and 4x; academy Profile and Leaderboard read off the page, Fire Code's single-tab Profile
  moves nothing); fails on 3a6675d at (1) follow, (3) ease-back, (5) down-first / left edge / sideways strip.
- LOOKED AT, NOT CHANGED: a bottom-tab click with a mouse at 4x CPU is 417-579ms to the screen (check-b384-mouse info, held to 900). Profiled: Home 270-340ms, Leaderboard 190,
  Calendar 200 are the new screen's first style pass and layout, which slideBubbleToActiveTab / syncLoopClock's getAnimations force inside the click task - the same work the first frame
  would do, moved earlier, so deferring them buys nothing; the first-use sound synthesis (prewarm: sndImpulseData / sndNoiseSamples, 28-55ms a step at 4x) runs in idle slots 4s
  after the first touch. A real saving needs a lighter screen, not a reorder.
- PHONE ONLY: how the follow, the carry-off and the ease-back feel on his 17 Pro Max (Chromium's compositor is not WebKit's; the harness cannot send a thumb's 60-120 touches
  a second at 4x), whether Safari's page zoom (html.page-zoomed: CSS zoom on cards inside the tabs) leaves the dragged element's px 1:1 with the finger, and the system's back
  swipe against the 20px edge.

What can be done at once is: from the academy, Fire Code's row comes off its board immediately (retireOtherClassBoardRow; the academy's handle writes `vrooms`); from Fire Code the academy's row cannot be reached (its handle never writes `leaderboard`) and comes off when the academy next opens, as an opt-out there always has. ## 384 r15 - next question on big screens (branch worktree-agent-a7c0620b9d4dd61ba, cut from 384.12, merged with origin/main 384.15; no build bump here)

Madison: "I saw something taking a test on a LARGE SCREEN and going to the next question was not smooth at all. Get this fixed. Ensure the smoothness is the same for all devices and all screen sizes." / "ensure the transition from selecting units is good".
Measured in Chromium (CDP traces: thread CPU time; rAF stamps; the slide's animations frozen at their first and last frame and read) on phone 440x956@3, iPad 834x1194@2 and 1024x1366@2, laptops 1366x768@1 and 1512x982@2, desktops 1920x1080, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 @1; main thread at 4x. The sandbox is a software compositor on a machine that ran at load 25-50 while this was done, so wall-clock frame times swing 40-100ms run to run and are NOT a measure; CPU time and the page's own numbers are.
- WHAT WAS NOT THE CAUSE (measured, left alone). The question's own cost does not grow with the window: the column is capped (.wrap 56rem), the panel is 848x475 on every window from 1366 up (400x574 on the phone, 786x507 on the iPad), the page has the same ~775-805 elements, the input task of a Next is 39-94ms at 4x on every size (the JS is ~12ms real: replaceChildren, a few reads), no per-question write lands in the slide (saveRunSession 1.4ms), the 88-dot meter is cached (drawMeter), the layers the slide makes are the copy and the incoming panel (panel-sized, not window-sized: a LayerTree dump at 3840x2160 shows the four window-sized layers - root, body::before, the page, the stage - painted once and not again), and will-change on the choices makes no measurable difference (A/B at 1366x768 x7, noise). The frame gaps at 4K and at 1366x768 are the same in this sandbox.
- THE CAUSE OF "NOT SMOOTH ON A LARGE SCREEN": THE MOVE ENDED ON SCREEN. The push crosses the panel's width plus the gap (876px on every window from 1366 up). On a phone or a portrait iPad that takes the old question clean off the screen. On a window wider than the panel it ends mid-screen: the outgoing copy ended at 55% opacity (qOutFrame) and was removed in one frame (qSlideDone), and the incoming one began at 85% where it was not (it appeared whole, in the middle of the window, at the first frame). Read off the page by freezing the slide's animations at 0 and 1 (opacity x share of the panel inside the window): main 384.15, out at the end / in at the start: phone 0/0, iPad 834 0/0, iPad 1024x1366 .041/.060, laptop 1366x768 .156/.232, 1512x982 .205/.305, 1920x1080 .343/.509, 2560x1440 .55/.83, 3840x2160 .55/.85. A pop, not a dropped frame - which is why every frame-time measure said the move was fine. FIX (qSetFade, qInAlpha, qFadeOutLoss): where the end of the move is on screen the outgoing question fades out over the same trip and the incoming one fades in from nothing: the share of the panel inside the window at the end (start) decides, 1 where none of it is (the signed-off .55 / .85, so every phone and every portrait iPad is byte-identical) and 0 from a twelfth of it on; the drag's blurred stand-in follows the same number (qSoftAlpha), so a touch window wider than the panel (a landscape iPad) does not pop either. After: 0/0 on 1366 and up, .006/.009 on the 1024 iPad (a 60px sliver), 0/0 elsewhere. Same push, same curves, same 280-392ms.
- THE COPY OF A QUESTION WAS BLANK WHERE ITS PICTURES WERE (every size). cloneNode copies a <canvas> as an empty one: a Fire Code question with its code box open (the remembered preference, so every answered county question) or the hint's picture open slid off with a blank paper-coloured frame - the print gone in the first frame of the move. qCopyCanvases draws the bitmaps across in makeClone (a blit). Gate: a canvas painted red is put in the question; at the move's first frame 240 of the copy's samples are painted (main: 0, on every size including the phone).
- THE START SHEET'S BLUR (the unit pickers). The sheet after Start is as wide as the window (a bottom sheet reaches both edges) and its glass rule gave it backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(2) with will-change:backdrop-filter - sampled again every frame of its 250ms slide, 80vh x the window = 6.6M px at 3840x2160 - while its fill is the solid #0F1115 (.is-setup), so the blur showed nowhere. `[data-layout="modern"] .unitoptions-modal-sheet.is-setup{ backdrop-filter:none; will-change:transform }`: the same picture. NOT PROVEN BY A NUMBER: one early single run at 3840x2160, 4x read the compositor's draw of the slide's frames at 106ms -> 37ms (phone 15), but the repeat (5 opens x 2, main's page with and without the blur injected, machine at load 50-70) read medians 95 / 89 as built and 113 / 45 without: inside the noise, and Chromium's software renderer may not draw a backdrop blur at all. What is certain is the structure (the computed backdrop-filter of the opened sheet is now none, a window-wide sample of the page behind it per frame less on a GPU); the gate asserts that, not a time.
- LOOKED AT, NOT CHANGED (needs a real GPU to say anything): (a) Home -> Choose your mode: the sky's fade (body::after: a window-sized layer with mask-image and an opacity transition over .6s, so an offscreen pass per frame) draws 46-80ms a frame at 3840x2160 in this software compositor against 7-13 on a phone; (b) LOADING TEST -> first question: the frame that shows the first question at 3840x2160 waits 460-800ms (4x) for the compositor (the window-sized glow repaints when the dim goes on: body.has-active-question) where a phone's is 7-23ms; pre-applying the class under the loading overlay was considered and not done (the chat dock, the status bar and the sky all read that class); (c) the units screen's first build is 130-250ms CPU at 4x once the badges are warm (a cold first visit also draws every badge strike: 870ms at 4x; the app's own warm-up does that 5s after launch, the gate does it before measuring).
- GATE tools/check-b384-bigslide.py ([--quick] [--full] [--against REV|file] [--only fc|academy|units]; PDFJS_DIR adds Fire Code): per viewport, academy short and long questions and Fire Code with the code box open / shut / the hint's picture open: (1) pops <= 2% at the move's two ends, (1b) the copy keeps a probe canvas, (2) input task <= 120ms at 4x, (4) no stall (p95 <= 140ms, <= 45 dropped; printed per size), (5) ends right; the unit pickers walked by real taps (Start Studying -> mode -> units -> a unit -> Start -> the sheet -> Begin -> LOADING -> the first question): (6) every step arrives, the sheet's backdrop-filter is none. Against main 384.15 it fails (1) on every window from 1024 up, (1b) on every size, (6) on the sheet.
- ONLY A REAL DEVICE CAN SAY: whether a Windows GPU at 4K was ever short of fill for the sheet's blur (this removes it either way); the sky fade and the first-question frame (a) (b) above on a real 4K monitor; a landscape iPad's finger drag with the new fade (the harness has no thumb); Safari's page zoom with the fade (a zoomed panel's rect is what qSetFade reads).
