## 384 r22 - friends show the class they last used (branch worktree-agent-aea30e25653093d05, from 384.17; no build bump here)

Madison, his Friends list in Fire Code: ten friends, EIGHT the grey ghost (only Nova and Logang showed a real character). "I don't want to add friends again for each class ... I'm thinking: on my friends list, maybe it will just be the character of the class they are in currently or the class they were in last? Same for the banner? ... in the friends list you also see their levels, and if you click their profile you also see their rank and stats and everything. ... some of the accounts I'm looking at have banners set from academy but have the corresponding IFC one on somehow? That should not be possible."

THE RULE. A person is shown as ONE class on every screen that draws them: the class their most recent presence beat was written from (`lc`, "academy" or "ifc"). That class's character, in that class's ART, its banner (in its art), its level and its rank. A name, a face, a banner and a number can never be from two different classes: `friendCardOf()` hands every friends screen a card already resolved by `faceFor()` / `shownCardOf()` (faceChar, faceCls, shownCls, and the shown class's level / badges / banner; `levelUnknown` when no source holds a level).

THE FIELDS (the presence beat, `vrooms/presence-v1` `c[pub]`, merged field by field, written by the heartbeat as before - ONE write, no listener and no read added):
- `lc` the class this beat was written from; `b` the ACADEMY banner id and `fb` the FIRE CODE banner id (ids only, "" = the default theme; each page writes only its own class's, validated by wornBanner(), so an id is never one the person does not hold in that class); `lv`+`bg` the academy's level and badges, `flv`+`fbg` Fire Code's (so a friend with no board row still has a number). `k`, `n`, `v`, `fv`, `f` are r11 / r13's, unchanged. The set merges deep, so the other class's fields stay as that class last wrote them. ~135 bytes a person. No sync code anywhere.

THE LADDER. lc (when it is a class the person is still in, friendClassesOf, and their character in it is known) -> this page's class when their character in it is known -> the other class when it is -> the class's starter (classDefaultCharacter). The academy character is always known from a board row or a beat, so nobody whose academy character is known is the placeholder (`none:true` only when nothing is known; friendCardFromPresence no longer invents "ghost"). A Virtual Room asks for this page's class first (ROOM_FACE: they are in this room's class right now), a board row says boardCls (a board is one class), vroomPersonEntry says pref.
LEVEL / RANK / STATS: the shown class's board row first (the academy's rows are what both pages hold; Fire Code's lb-ifc-v1 only once the Leaderboard screen has read it, classBoardRows), else the beat's number, else left out - Manage friends then says the class's name, the card too, and Hundos shows a dash rather than 0. Nothing is carried over from the other class. A quiet class mark (the class icon, solid fills, no words, .class-mark) follows the level for a person who is in BOTH classes.

ART IN EITHER PAGE. `buildAvatarCharSVG(id, art)` / `buildBannerArt(id, cls)` take "academy" | "ifc" (default: this page's, unchanged: one template per id, no new hash for the flip-book - data-art is left out of the sheet hash). The other class's art is lent for the length of one synchronous draw (`withCharArt`: the id's kind, glow, head / art scale, centring and special; Zeus is put back in the table for the draw) from `ART_ACADEMY_SNAP` (Fire Code's page: taken just before IFC_CHAR_LOOK overwrites the table) or `artOtherSnap` (the academy's page: read off IFC_CHAR_LOOK) and restored in a `finally`. Templates are keyed `id~art-<class>`; the svg's data-char carries the same suffix, which is how the flip-book (charAnimDrawing) records the right drawing. Every svg has `data-art`; a span has dataset.art. Banners: `BANNER_ART_ACADEMY` (kept before IFC_BANNER_ART overwrites) / `IFC_BANNER_ART`, templates keyed the same way, `bannerTintOf(id, cls)`. An id drawn the same in both classes is the page's own drawing either way. The other class's ULTIMATE banner (Astral in the academy / Zenith in Fire Code) is not in this page's BANNERS and falls to the theme. THE REPORTED BUG: an academy banner id read from the academy row was drawn through Fire Code's BANNER_ART, i.e. as its Fire Code twin. A banner is now drawn in the art of the class it was read for.
NOT CHANGED: the cutscenes and the hundo effects (own character only; the Virtual Room winner cutscene is handed an id and draws the page's art), the leaderboard's own rows (a board is one class: its rows stay that class's character in that page's art - a tap on a board row opens the card as that class: boardCls), reactions (rxCharOf: an academy-only move is not put on a Fire Code drawing - ifcRedrawn).

OLD BUILDS. A device from before this build writes no `lc` / `b` / `fb` / `lv`: its friends read as "no lc" - this page's class when their character there is known, else the academy's (never the ghost while a row or beat has an academy character), and their level is the academy row's. They turn into the real thing as soon as that friend updates and opens the app once (the first heartbeat of a session writes it). Only a phone and the real cloud can confirm that, and the Fire Code leaderboard's rows (a board read) the first time it is opened.
GATE: `tools/check-b384-lastclass.py` (fails on 384.17).
### 384 r23 - a Fire Code account only counts its own challenges
Madison, on his phone in Fire Code (Customize > Challenges): the Smoke Diver (CHARACTER `masked`, challenge `retake100`: `store.retakenQuestions >= 100 || hardcoreUnitsBeaten() >= 10`) read Unlocked with a full bar on an account days old (level ~4, 0 of 58 badges): "There's no chance I completed this, why do I have this unlocked already". He was wearing it (the Profile tab's icon is the Smoke Diver). The other eight visible tiles were correctly locked; the first row (Inspector, Smoke Diver, Chief, Strobe) was under the card.
- WHAT WAS PROVED (Chromium, check-b384-fcchallenges.py against main = build 384.17). A fresh Fire Code store seeded from a heavy academy copy (640 retakes, 12 Hardcore units, 60 study days, every flare, weekly/VR wins, a 300-run, a passed 450 test, 5,400 answers) holds NOTHING after boot, after the first drill start (beginRun runs every seed), after a pull of its own near-empty document and after the academy's copy changed underneath: the first-visit seed copies none of the counters (name, character, look, seen tips, and the seed flags only), `seedVroomHistory` cannot run there (`fbDb` is null in Fire Code), `foldSocialFrom` takes the friends block only, `mergeSameAccount` takes counters as a max and is never fed the academy's document, `mergeLeavingAccount` (the one that SUMS retakenQuestions) is only reached by a merge note for the account's own code. The table has 20 challenges and 21 banners; none reads done on that fresh account (that is gate A, and it passes on main as well: there was no inheritance path to find on main for a FRESH store).
- THE PATH THAT DOES PRODUCE IT, with numbers. `seedChallenges289()` backfills `retakenQuestions = round(misses x drillPlays / (drillPlays + examPlays))` from the store's own `stats` whenever `store.challengeSeed289` is false, once, at the next `beginRun` / Customize / results. It was written for accounts that played before build 289 kept the count; in Fire Code (counted live from its first answer) it turns every miss into a retake it never made. Fire Code store, 150 misses on record, 400 answers, drillPlays 20, examPlays 0, flag false: first drill start -> retakenQuestions = 150 -> Smoke Diver unlocked (E on main: 150, featsDone [retake100]; the new build: 0, flag set). The flag reads false whenever a copy is loaded from a document without it (`applyLoadedData`: `got.challengeSeed289 === true`; a cloud document or an academy copy from a build that predates it) - and a few days of use is easily 100+ misses. I could not read his phone, so this is the one mechanism shown to unlock the Smoke Diver on a Fire Code store that never retook anything; whether it is what happened to him only a look at his numbers can say.
- THE FIX, three layers (all Fire Code only; the academy is byte for byte what it was, gate D).
  1. No backfill in Fire Code: `seedChallenges289`, `seedLateHundos312`, `seedBannerCounters` only mark themselves seeded there; `applyLoadedData` reads the three seed flags as true in Fire Code; the first-visit seed sets them true and never copies the academy's.
  2. THE REPAIR IS A RULE, NOT AN EDIT (precedent: `applyWeekWinVoids`; the counters merge as a max / union, so a lowered copy would be put straight back by the cloud document, the `__floor` backup or another device - revokePenalKoi295 / sheriffMoved324 / hiveMoved384 / ifcCharsFixed384 are flags or one-shots and would not hold). `ifcChallengeClamp(d)` works on any store-shaped object: `retakenQuestions` is held to `min(misses on record (sum of stats m), lifetime.answered)`, and `unitGameBeat` (Game mode: retired, academy units, nothing in Fire Code can write it) is emptied. `ifcChallengesRepair384()` runs it on the store and, for a character whose challenge is `retake100` and that is now locked: drops it from `pendingCharUnlocks`, from `unlocksShown.chars` and `seenUnlocks.chars` (so a real earn is announced as it should be) and, if it is worn, puts the class's first starter on (`classDefaultCharacter`, quietly, no toast). It runs where `ifcLookCheck(true)` / `ifcCharsRepair384` already do - `markCloudConfirmed` (the server's copy is in), after each `syncSameAccount` once confirmed, and at launch for a copy with no sync - and BEFORE them, so the look is judged on the corrected count. `writeAccount`'s `build()` clamps the document it is about to write, and the account document and its `__floor` are written from that same copy, so both come down (a deliberate lowering, said here because CLAUDE.md asks that lowering on purpose lowers the floor too).
  3. What is NOT clamped: anything a Fire Code store can honestly hold. The bound is an invariant of play: every counted retake (a Drill question missed then answered again, or a question of a Retake run) follows a miss on that question recorded in `stats` (`m`) and is an answer given, so honest `retakenQuestions <= sum(m)` and `<= answered` (a retake of a retake counts again only because it was missed again, which adds a miss). A Fire Code account that really retook 120 with 160 misses on record keeps the Smoke Diver, wears it, and a live Drill retake counts one more (gate C).
- WHAT IT DOES TO AN AFFECTED ACCOUNT, and to his Smoke Diver. If his count is over what his own record supports (the inherited-640 shape: gate B), the next launch that hears the server (or the first merge) puts it at that cap, empties the Hardcore record, locks the Smoke Diver, takes it off his avatar (he is put on Ghost, the first starter, with no toast) and drops its queued unlock and its announced / seen marks; the account document and floor follow on the next push. If his count is within his record - which is what the seed path above produces, since its sum is bounded by his own misses - the rule cannot tell it from a real earn and leaves it: that case is the one a clamp cannot undo, and it needs his own numbers (retakenQuestions against the misses and answers on his Stats). What is not touched: points, XP, hundos, anything else, the academy copy, the cloud account's other fields.
- CHOSEN AND WHY: clamp to the record (the lead's rule) instead of zeroing, so no real earn is ever taken; Fire Code's Hardcore record is cleared outright because the class has no Game mode (every entry there is another class's); no new persisted field (the rule is idempotent and needs no flag); weekly counters (`weeklyWins`, `weeklyTop3`) are not repaired: Fire Code has no weekly board and no challenge reads them there.
- AUDIT of every challenge on a fresh Fire Code account seeded from the heavy academy (inputs): daily10 (dailyCorrectTotal, dailyCorrectStreak/Best), bigtest400 (bigTest450Passed / bigTest500Passed), retake100 (retakenQuestions, unitGameBeat hardcore), weektop (weeklyWins), weektop3x3 (weeklyTop3), novabeat (novaBeaten), flares (mysteryColorsFound red/orange/yellow), vrwins5 (vrWins), streak100 (ifcRunBest), hundo7day (hundoDay / hundoDayBest), study20h (studyLog hours), days30 (studyLog days), busyday300 (vrHosted, legacyChars - never read in Fire Code), studyrun7 (studyLog run), flare4/5/6 (mysteryColorsFound), allchars / allbanners / everything (collections of the others). None is true there; none of those counters is in the first-visit seed. The 21 banners read the same counters (tests, hundos, units, streaks, friends, fullTests, lateHundos, VR matches) and none is earned there.
- GATE tools/check-b384-fcchallenges.py (A fresh store x {no cloud document, its own near-empty one} x {boot, first drill start, another boot, the academy's copy changed underneath}; A2 seed flags not copied; B the repair - cloud document and floor carrying 640 / 12 Hardcore, worn / queued / marked -, once, after another boot, after a newer and an older merge, the document written clamped; B2 no document yet; C a real earn kept, worn, a live retake counted and not undone by a merge; D the academy unaffected; E the backfill). FAILS against main (build 384.17): B (all nine), B2, E.
- ONLY A PHONE CAN SAY whether the repair finds anything on his account (the numbers are his), and how the Customize tile and the Profile tab icon look the first time the Smoke Diver goes back to locked while the page is open (checked here only by reading the page).
## 384 r16 - leaving a class (branch worktree-agent-a051485695d4c7974, cut from 384.13 and merged with 384.16; NOT on main; no build bump here)

Madison, five things about LEAVING A CLASS (Settings > Classes): (1) "When I hit the red leave button, it should ask again for confirmation." (2) "When it happens, the splash screen loaded but it massively lagged and the screen jumped around." (3) "The fire code class was still in the class drop down. I didn't leave it." (4) "When looking at it in settings, it says Your classes, and the one I'm in says Open now, I click it and it asks if I wanna leave. Should the title of that section be Manage classes instead?" (5) "I hit the Join another class button, I hit the back button, and that took me to the main menu for some reason."

ROOT CAUSE OF (3), AND ONE OF (2): A LEAVE ASKED FOR IN FIRE CODE NEVER HAPPENED. `leaveClass()` in Fire Code wrote its hand-off note as `localStorage.setItem("class26e.leaveclass", ...)`. Fire Code remaps every `class26e.` key that is not on the head script's SHARED list to `class26e.ifc.<rest>`, and `leaveclass` / `leftnote` were not on it - so the note landed at `class26e.ifc.leaveclass` and the academy's page read `class26e.leaveclass`, found nothing, built its Home and did nothing. Leaving Fire Code from Fire Code: the academy opened with Fire Code still in the class list and the class button ("The fire code class was still in the class drop down. I didn't leave it"). Leaving the academy from Fire Code: it opened the academy and nothing else. (Leaving from the academy always worked: no mapping.) The check-b384-r4 gate only ever drove a leave from the academy. Both keys are SHARED now (head script, `var SHARED`). Reproduced first on main (build 384.13) with the real two-page flow, a persisted account in both classes and an in-memory cloud: after "leave Fire Code" from Fire Code the page is the academy, `enrolled` = ["academy","ifc"], cloud unchanged; after "leave the academy" from Fire Code the same.

OTHER THINGS FOUND IN (2) (measured with tools/b384_leave_lib.py: page loads, layout shifts, long tasks, covers, Home mounts, toasts kept across the reloads in sessionStorage):
- Leaving the class you are in sat on the Settings page for `setTimeout 300ms + the account's write polled` before the cover came up: cover at 362ms from the final tap on main at 1x CPU (about 1.2s at 4x on a loaded machine), nothing on screen saying anything happened. The cover now comes up at the tap (26-64ms at 1x) and the write is done UNDER it: `switchClass(..., { until(go, giveBack) })` runs the work when the cover has covered the page, and the page reloads when the account has it (`waitLeaveWritten`, 8s at most).
- The write was also waiting out the push deferral: a page that has just opened must read the account before it may write (the hard rule), and the push that was waiting then went on the usual few-second timer (`cloudPushTimer`). `waitLeaveWritten` pushes at once when the account has been read and a push is only waiting on the timer (measured: the hop page's wait went from 2.7s to 0.1s).
- The academy page that finished a leave built its whole Home FIRST (the cover lifts over a built Home) and only then left (`runPendingClassLeave()` was the last line of showHome). It is the first line now: a leave of Fire Code is done before anything is built and Home is built once, with the right list; a leave of the academy asked for in Fire Code is written and the page goes straight on to Fire Code with no Home built at all (`NOVA_CLASS_HOP`: finishSplash waits, the splash is the cover all the way). One cover: the cover Fire Code puts up is Fire Code's own picture and colours from the first frame to the last (`switchClass(..., { final: "ifc" })`, so it never turns to the academy's colours in between), and the hop re-writes the arrival record (`class26e.classswitch`, same `at`) so the final page's splash carries the bar on from the same moment. Two page loads are the minimum for that one case (the academy's copy is written only by the academy's page); it was never a third.
- Leaving the other class from the Classes page remounted the whole Settings page (entrance, scroll to top, tab-bar work) and then called `mountClassBubble()`, which appended the Home screen's class button to the Settings stage. The list is rebuilt where it stands now (`refreshClassesPage()`), and nothing from Home is mounted.
- A leave that cannot finish changes nothing: `leaveCanReach()` (offline, or Firebase not loaded for a syncing account) says so before anything is touched; a write that does not land in 8s is undone (`undoLeaveClass`: the class is joined again, dated after the leave) and the cover is given back (`giveBack`), which now also puts `class26e.activeclass` back (a given-up switch used to leave it pointing at the class it never reached). "Couldn't leave X ... Nothing was changed" is the sheet (`sayCannotLeave`).
- NOT faults, measured: no layout shift under 0.02 once the cover lifts in any direction on this build (main's leave-from-Fire-Code page shifted 0.10 over 155 IMG shifts on the wrong page); the leave's own main-thread work (list, board row, account push, page refresh) is 10ms at 4x; the ordinary class switch has the same page-load time (a loaded machine measured both: cover 589ms, reload 2180ms for the switch from the class button, 26/812 for the leave).

(1) TWO QUESTIONS: `askLeaveClass()` is the first sheet as before ("Leave X?", red "Leave X", Cancel); its red button now opens `confirmLeaveClassFinal()`, "Are you sure you want to leave X?", whose body says what goes (the class and its leaderboard) and what is kept (rank, level, badges, progress, returning if you join again) and, for the class you are in, which class Nova opens; red "Yes, leave X" and Cancel. Only the second red button calls `leaveClass()`. Both are `showClassEnrollConfirm()` (the second is shown at once in the first's place: the dim stays). Cancel at either stage changes nothing (gate: lists, dates, cloud, no cover, no hand-off key).
(4) The section is headed "Manage classes". The class you are in reads "Current" (not "Open now"); every row's aria-label is "Manage X"; the footnote says "Tap a class to manage it. You can leave a class from here: your progress in it is kept, and comes back if you join again." The Settings menu's Classes row value is unchanged (the count, or the one class's name).
(5) `showClassCatalog(from)` takes where it was opened from: "settings" (Settings > Manage classes > Join another class, and the only-class sheet's Join another class) returns to that page; "home" (the class button's +, the new-class banner) returns to Home. Fire Code's enrol screen's own Back returns to the list, which returns to where it was opened from. Welcome/sign-up has its own class screen (showClassSelection) and never opens this list.

EXACT LISTS (3, checked both ways): the Fire Code side reads the academy's copy through `pickAcademyCopy()`, which kept only `classes` - it now keeps `classJoinedAt` / `classLeftAt` too, so `accountClassesOf` reads the list there as the academy does (the owner rule that puts Fire Code back on his list respects a leave). Gate: after each of the four leaves (academy from the academy, academy from Fire Code, Fire Code from the academy, Fire Code from Fire Code) the page is the right class, `enrolledClasses()` is the other class only, only the left class is dated as left (in the store and in the cloud copy), the class button lists no other class, the Manage classes page and the class list's Enrolled marks agree, the leaderboard row is off for the academy, no hand-off key or note is left behind; then the rejoin (the real catalog flow for the academy; the Enroll button's own calls for Fire Code, whose book is a PDF only a person can choose) brings both back with each class's progress as it was and the join dated after the leave.

REMAP TRAP, FOR ANY HAND-OFF KEY (the lead asked to verify it; it is real and is the root cause of (3) above): a page in Fire Code that writes a `class26e.*` key for the academy's page writes `class26e.ifc.*` unless the key is on the head script's SHARED list. Anything a hand-off writes from Fire Code must be on that list or be written by property access (`localStorage[k] = v` bypasses the patched setItem/getItem). `leaveclass` and `leftnote` are on it now; check-b384-classleave 'keys' asserts it from a real Fire Code page, and the lists/hop sections drive both directions end to end (they fail on 384.16 main).

GATES: tools/check-b384-classleave.py (sections texts, confirm, back, lists, hop, undo, timing; `--against` old index.html must FAIL: on 384.16 main it fails 1 (single confirm), 3 (leave-from-Fire-Code never happens: both directions), 4 (heading, "Open now", footnote), 5 (Back goes Home) and the timing check (cover at 354ms against the 250ms budget at 1x; the hop's second page load never happens). tools/b384_leave_lib.py is the harness (it rides on b384_switchfx_lib: the page served as Pages serves it, in-memory Firestore in the tab's sessionStorage, owner's account in both classes, a witness that survives reloads: loads, layout shifts with how much cover was over them, long tasks, covers, Home mounts, toasts). check-b384-r4 (U) drives both sheets now. A gate run in a BACKGROUND shell with its output redirected hung before its first line twice in this session (Chromium never started under a loaded machine); run them in the foreground.

Only a phone can confirm: whether Safari reads the cover as continuous across the two page loads of the academy-left-from-Fire-Code case (Chromium keeps the last frame; iOS may paint a frame of the page's own background between two reloads), the real Firestore round trip time under the cover (the fake answers in 15ms; the 8s limit is a guess at a bad connection), `navigator.onLine` on iOS (it can say true while offline - the write then fails, and the 8s undo is what catches it), and the toast "You left X." over a settling Home.
## 384 r15 - a tab tap always lands on its tab (branch worktree-agent-a8034a9c557c7bc75, merged with 384.17; no build bump here)

Madison: "if I'm selecting a unit, go to settings, and then hit home it goes back to units?? Fix that and ensure none of it does that."
THE CAUSE: a flag, `returnToSetupAfterTabs`. `captureSetupReturn()` set it at the top of `showProfile()`, `showCalendarTab()` and `showRanksScreen()` whenever `.screen-setup` (the unit screen) was the screen being left, and the next tap on the Home tab (`confirmMainMenu()`, the first line) saw it, cleared it and built `showSetup()` instead of Home. Fire Code's Settings tab and the academy's Settings (a top tab of Profile) are `showProfile()`, so both classes and every bar (phone, laptop) did it. It was a deliberate feature from a much older report ("tapping Profile/Rewards/Settings while choosing units used to just abandon that screen for good"); it is the opposite of what he wants now, so it is gone, not patched: the variable, `captureSetupReturn()`, its three calls, the line in `confirmMainMenu()` and the reset in `showHome()` are removed. Nothing is held now; a tab leaves the unit screen for good and Home is Home. Start Studying is how the units are reached again, and it is unchanged: `showModeSelect()` drops the picks on the way (`cfg.units = []`), so arriving at the units shows none ticked, as the 100 note ("LEAVING UNIT SELECTION DROPS THE PICKS") says. That note's reason for clearing in `showModeSelect()` rather than `showSetup()` ("a tab round trip would lose your picks") no longer applies and the comments say so; the clearing place is unchanged.
THE AUDIT of the class of bug (a tap on a tab landing on something other than that tab's root): read every other piece of state a tab tap or `showHome()` can consult. `friendsBack` (a back target only, cleared when Friends is not the screen), `testInProgress` (Home tap on a running test asks "Leave to main menu?" - by design), `runLabel === "Daily question"` (straight Home - by design), the saved-test slot (only Start Studying offers it; a Home tap never does), `LAST_TAB_KEY` (read at boot only), the rank-up / badge cutscene interception at the top of Home, Profile and Rankings (owed moments, by design). No other flag brings a screen back. (`vroomCode` left set by a Virtual Room lobby makes `runSessionSavable()` false - this is the lobby's own Leave room that clears it, the lobby hides the bar, so a tab cannot leave it; noted, not changed.)
THE GATE: `tools/check-b384-tabroots.py`. Starting screens (22 academy / 21 Fire Code): Home, the modes, the units in Drill and in Review with a unit ticked, Customize, Friends, the badge case, the rank ladder, two Settings pages, Test history, Review's list, flash cards, the Virtual Room's choice, setup and lobby, the chat open, Profile, Profile's Stats, Profile's Settings tab (academy), the Leaderboard, the Calendar (academy), Settings (Fire Code's tab) x every tab of the class's bar (academy: Home, Profile, Leaderboard, Calendar; Fire Code: Home, Profile, Leaderboard, Settings), tapped for real (a touch tap on the phone; a real mouse - move, down, a beat, up - on the laptop), each followed by a Home tap: the tab's own root up (read off the page by class, not a label), no other tab's root up, exactly that tab lit, nothing of the screen it came from (unit screen, modes, Customize, Friends, Review, flash cards, a sheet, a resume card, a pause panel), Profile on its first top tab. Then a chain of every tab in turn and back to Home from each start. Where the bar is hidden or covered by design (the Virtual Room's lobby, the chat's dock on a phone, a question, Pause, the daily question, results) there is no tab to tap: the gate reads that the tab is not reachable (an element-at-point test, so a covered bar counts) and then leaves by the screen's own exit and checks Home and Profile-then-Home. And the test in progress: the Home path on a running drill asks "Leave to main menu?" with Keep going and Leave; Keep going puts the running question back; Leave goes Home; the daily question goes straight Home; Save and exit keeps the test (a saved slot), lands on Home, Profile/Leaderboard/Calendar-or-Settings then Home is Home with no resume card, and Start Studying still offers "Resume test" / "Start a new test". Phone = iPhone 17 Pro Max installed 440x956, laptop = 1536x864 with a mouse. `--quick` (fewer starts), `academy|ifc`, `--only SUBSTR` (one starting screen), `--against REV|DIR|index.html`.
RESULT (this build): promax academy 126 taps and a 108-tap chain, promax Fire Code 115 taps (one start flaked once on a machine at load 50: "units, Review" could not be reached in 10s; the start alone was re-run and passed, and `reach_retry` now tries once more), laptop academy 133 taps, laptop Fire Code (full) - all pass. FAILS against the build before (384.17 on main, and 384.12): "the units, Drill, a unit ticked > Profile > Home", "> Calendar > Home", the chain's Home, and the ticked-units check, all with `.screen-setup` on the stage and no tab lit where Home should be. The other checks (test in progress, saved test, hidden-bar exits) pass on both - they guard what must not break. Run the others one at a time: the harness is heavy and a machine at load 50 makes a tap time out.
NOT VERIFIED HERE: a real thumb on a phone (Chromium taps); Safari's own tab/page behaviour; Fire Code's lobby (the Virtual Room lobby start is a faked room).
## 384 r16 - every pop-up is frosted

Madison, the Settings > Classes "Leave Police Academy?" confirm on his iPhone 17 Pro Max (installed, Safari page zoom ~85%): "These pop ups need the Frosted look, why does the font look weird here by the way??" The confirm family (`.savecode-card` > `.savecode-sheet`: class enroll / leave / only-class, new account, sign out, the save-code card) read as a flat dark navy slab, and its title was bold Georgia over a sans body.

WHY IT READ FLAT (three causes, all fixed for every pop-up at once). (1) THE DIM: `rgba(4,6,10,.66)` over a mostly empty dark page leaves nothing lit for the glass to blur; it is `--pop-scrim` (.4) now, a layer of its own (the overlay's `::before`), faded by opacity. (2) THE GLASS: the shared `--pop-bg-glass` was a dark `rgba(26,31,38,.5)` at `blur(9px)`; the new tokens `--sheet-bg` (lighter, bluer, top sheen over `rgba(40,48,62,.42)`), `--sheet-blur` (22px, saturate 1.8, brightness 1.05), `--sheet-border` (.17 white rim) and `--sheet-shadow` are one set used by one rule. `--pop-bg*` stay for the banners / toasts / tooltips ("the circled stuff is great") and for Profile's in-page card. (3) BACKDROP ROOTS: an element with opacity < 1, a filter, a mask or its own backdrop-filter is a backdrop root, and a sheet inside it blurs that element's own (empty) content instead of the page. `.savecode-card` faded by opacity AND scrolled (`overflow-y:auto`); `.chatdock-confirm`, `.resume-offer` and `.unitver` carried a `backdrop-filter:blur(6px)` of their own. Chromium shows the settled state fine; iOS WebKit is the one that composites a sheet inside such a layer as flat (the person card's 327z10 note found the same trap for that card alone). Now every overlay is a plain fixed box (opacity 1, no filter, no scroll, `overflow:visible`), the dim and the sheet each fade by themselves (`.show` / `.invite-overlay-show` drive both; the two overlays with no show state use a one-shot keyframe), and a tall sheet scrolls inside itself (`max-height:100%`, `overflow-y:auto`): `.savecode-sheet`, `.intro-card`.

ONE RULE: the block ".POP-UP GLASS" at the END of the stylesheet. Hosts (overlays): `.savecode-card, .chatdock-confirm (not .chat-leavesheet), .resume-offer, .friend-moment, .installguide-overlay, .unitver, .invite-overlay, .intro-pop, .pop-glass-host`. Sheets: `.savecode-sheet, .chatdock-confirm-card, .resume-card, .friend-moment-card, .unitver-card, .installguide-card, .intro-card, .a2hs-sheet, .invite-sheet (person / unlock / rank / level-coming / members / poll / invite / room chat), .chat-leavesheet-group/-cancel, .pop-glass`. A new pop-up puts `.pop-glass-host` on its overlay and `.pop-glass` on its card and inherits everything; the selectors carry `html[data-theme][data-layout] body` so they out-rank the older `[data-theme="dark"][data-layout="modern"] .installguide-card`-style rules (those were left in place, inert). The old r8 rule giving `.intro-card / .unlock-card / .person-card` the pop glass was folded into this one.

DELIBERATELY NOT CONVERTED (and why): the unit card `.unitdetail` (it grows out of its row by animating left/top/width/height; a blur re-sampled every frame of that is a cost this app does not pay; its scrim keeps its blur), the Start / options sheet `.unitoptions-modal-sheet` (dragged by a finger, opaque on purpose, see its own note), the document viewer window `.ifc-vz-card`, the arrowed popovers `.under-note` and `.hundo-why` (an arrow that shares the body's fill must be one opaque colour, 384 r5), the Home stats popover, and full-screen takeovers (cutscenes, rs-spot, the loading / analyzing / update screens, Pause and "Quit this test?", which are panels in #stage, not pop-ups). The tour tooltip and the daily-question lock tip were already clear glass.

THE FONT. `.savecode-title` was forced to `Georgia, "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", serif` at 1.5rem by the 384 r9 rule ("The sync code card circled: This should match the what's new frost look" - What's new's own title, `.intro-title`, is `var(--serif)`), which was fine on the one card it was asked for and wrong on the confirm family that shares the class: a bold Georgia headline over a system-sans body. It is `var(--sans)` (system-ui: San Francisco on his phone, not a bundled Inter) 700 at 1.35rem, -.01em, line-height 1.25 for the whole family. What's new's own title stays serif. check-b384-savefrost (2) used to assert "the title is What's new's typeface"; it now asserts the title is NOT a serif (the decision it encoded was reversed on request).

GATE: tools/check-b384-popglass.py, over `tools/b384_pop_lib.py` INVENTORY (22 pop-ups opened by the app's own functions over Settings / Leaderboard / Profile), iPhone 17 Pro Max in both classes (Fire Code via `class26e.activeclass=ifc` and a two-class account) and iPad Pro 11" in the academy: translucent fill (< .75) + blur >= 16px with saturate, one glass for all sheets, no backdrop-root ancestor (opacity / filter / backdrop-filter / mask / clip-path / scroll) in the settled state, the confirm's dim <= .5, confirm titles not a serif, a short window scrolls the card and not its overlay. 143 FAIL against 384.13 (origin/main). `--shots DIR` writes the frames for the contact sheets. UNVERIFIED on a phone: Chromium does not reproduce iOS compositing, so the backdrop-root removal is the robustness change, not a measured before/after; and the 22px blur / .42 tint are tuned on dark pages (a very bright page behind a card could want the tint nudged up: `--sheet-bg` is the one place).
## 384 r19 - the Home Screen reminder (branch r19-a2hs-bar, cut from 384.16 and merged with 384.17; not on main)

Madison, after the Add to Home Screen walkthrough: "if you can improve the guide at all.. maybe you can put out reminders for people who are on Safari without it as a home app? And it won't go away on the screen till they hit the X button or something?" A page cannot add itself to the Home Screen (the person has to do Share > Add to Home Screen), so the app does what it can.

THE BAR (`syncA2hsBar`, `showA2hsBar`, in the a2hs block above `showHomeScreenSheet`). A slim glass notice at the top of Home for anybody in a browser tab on a phone or tablet (`a2hsDeviceGuess()` apple or android, `isStandaloneApp()` false): "Add Nova to your Home Screen to open it as an app." with an Add pill and an X. The whole bar but the X is one button that opens the walkthrough (`showHomeScreenSheet({ from: "bar" })`, headed Home Screen). It is `.update-banner.is-glass.is-a2hs` - the update notice's glass, z-index, safari-bars margin and cutscene hiding come with the class - with its own id `#a2hsbar`.
- STAYS until ended: `class26e.a2hs.bar` (localStorage only, never on `store`) holds `x<time>` after the X and `d<time>` after "I've added it", after the browser's own install (`appinstalled`), or when the app is seen open from the Home Screen (`isStandaloneApp()`; on Android that shares the browser's storage, on an iPhone the icon's jar is separate and never shows it anyway). Once there it never comes back: not on a reload, not a day later, not on a new build. A private-mode localStorage that throws still ends it for the session (`a2hsBarGone`). "Not now" in the walkthrough only closes it; the bar stays.
- WHO: finished sign-up, has a sync code and sync on (without one the new icon would start a second, empty account), and the one-time walkthrough has already shown (`class26e.a2hs` is a time): a sign-up under way (`owed`) is left to its own sheet, and an existing account gets its "Quick tip" first and the bar after it is closed (no bar before or under the tip). Never on a computer.
- WHERE: Home only (`dataset.screen === "home"`), as the update notices are. Held (and hidden if up) during a tour, the tour's quiet time, a cutscene (`noticeAllowedHere`), the splash, a loader, the walkthrough's own showing and anything Home is busy with (`a2hsBusy`); on screen changes away from Home it goes at once (never over another screen's title), on the others it fades. First arrival of a launch waits ~0.9s of quiet; back on Home later it is simply there.
- PRECEDENCE: the update and re-add notices (`#updatebanner`) win: while one is up (even fading) the bar is not, and `hideBanner` re-syncs it when that goes. `syncNoticeVisibility` is now a wrapper (`syncNoticeVisibilityMain` + `syncA2hsBar`) so every existing caller keeps it right. Banners that arrive after it (`positionDailyAlert`) park below it; banners already up are re-parked when it arrives (`resettleTopBanners`); the bar itself ignores them in `settleTopBanner` (it is the permanent resident, the alerts are the visitors) - without that, bar and an alert swapped places mid-arrival and the bar sat 278px down on an iPad.
- NO SHIFT: `position:fixed`, placed (top measured) with transitions off, then `.show` in the same tick (not on `requestAnimationFrame`: an invisible bar would still take taps in a background tab). The planet system clears it through `pushHomeHeroForNotice` - a `translate`, so nothing re-flows. THAT FUNCTION HAD A LATENT BUG THE BAR EXPOSED: it measured the hero's top and subtracted the push it was HEADING for, but the hero's translate transitions for .45s and the bar's sync runs on every Home mutation, so each call mid-slide pushed it further (168px on a 17 Pro Max, 482px on an iPad, for a 52px bar). It subtracts the translate the hero is at NOW (`getComputedStyle(hero).translate`) and only writes the property when the number changes. It also now clears whichever of the update notice and the reminder is up (`.is-leaving` marks a bar on its way out; `hideBanner` sets it).
- PLACEMENT: `topNoticeOffset` for the bar counts only obstructions it overlaps horizontally. On a phone the chat button is in the bar's span so it goes under it (centred, as every banner is); on a tablet and a phone on its side the corner is clear and the bar takes the top (its inline margin-top is zeroed once anything was measured, because the measured rects already carry a Safari bar's margin). An open chat panel hides it (`body.chatdock-open`), as it does the other banners.
- HOME HAS NO ROOM FOR IT BEHIND A SHORT PLANET: `pushHomeHeroForNotice` also compresses the planet system (the `scale` property, `--notice-scale`, never below .72) where sliding it down clear of the bar would put its lowest flare over the greeting - measured on the baseline, the gap between the lowest flare and the greeting is 50px on an SE and 65 on a 17 Pro Max, and the bar costs 66-92px, so without it a flare sat over "Good morning" on every phone. The natural (un-pushed, un-scaled) edges are worked back from the transform in effect (scale is about the hero's centre), the greeting's top is the floor. Only while the reminder is up; the update notice is unchanged.
- A PHONE ON ITS SIDE gets none (`a2hsBarCramped()`: wider than tall and under 480px high): Home's planet system is a few dozen pixels there and the class button sits where the bar would, so it waits for the phone to be turned upright (`repositionTopNotices` re-syncs on rotation). A tablet on its side has it.

## 384 r18 - top tabs like Delta's

Madison, his Profile > Stats page beside Delta's Change App Icon screen (its Light / Dark control circled), with a screen recording of ours: "I'm not sure what's up with our top tabs. It should be designed like the Delta one, look like it. Function like it. Fix that, make it smooth."

WHAT WAS WRONG (read off his recording, 5s HEVC, decoded at 10 fps, and the two screenshots). Round 8 had read Delta's control as a DARK track with a LIGHTER thumb, and had made a touch lift the bottom bar's glass lens (1.26x the track's height, 1.15x the thumb's width) while the whole control swelled 9% and the thumb travelled as a stretched capsule that stood proud of the track above and below. On the recording that is a big bulging lens crossing the control, wider than the control at the ends of its travel. Delta does none of it.

WHAT DELTA DRAWS (pixel-sampled on the 1186x2576 screenshot; 2.693 px per pt on a 440pt screen; the page behind it is #1C1B1C):
- the TRACK is a LIGHTER capsule, #3A3A3C (58,58,60), 180 x 46pt, a rim about +8 levels over the fill and a point wide, a black hairline round its outside, a faint lift at its top edge;
- the THUMB is a DARKER capsule, #202123 (32,33,35), inset 4pt in the picked segment (40pt tall), a soft inner edge, nothing glassy;
- the labels are white at one weight - BOTH labels, the picked and the unpicked - so it is the thumb that says which is picked;
- equal segments. (The track height read off it is 46pt, not the 34-36pt a native control usually is; ours is 44pt on his zoomed phone, so the heights already agree and were left.)

WHAT IT IS NOW (index.html: segThumb + attachSegSlider, and the last CSS block, "THE TOP SWITCHERS, AS DELTA'S iOS 26 CONTROL DRAWS ONE"):
- every pill switcher (Profile / Stats / Settings, the Leaderboard's boards, the units screen's levels, the Virtual Room review's Missed / Entire test, the chat sheet's Friends / Groups / Inbox) is `.has-seg-thumb`: track #3A3A3C with rim, hairline and a still soft shadow; thumb #202123 with an inset shadow; labels #fff at weight 500, the unpicked at .86 opacity (the cross-fade is opacity, so it is on the compositor), 1 on hover. Equal segments: the chat sheet's tabs used to be content-sized pills with no track; they are now `.chatdock-seg` (a track round the three tabs, the close button beside it in the row) so the thumb is the segment's size throughout. The old `.has-seg-glass` class and the whole attachSegGlass (about 330 lines) are gone; `.has-seg-thumb` takes its place in attachTabSwipe's "a finger on a top switcher is its own". The glassLens* helpers stay for the bottom bar, untouched.
- a TAP slides the thumb on a critically damped spring (w = 21: 90% in 0.19s, 98% in 0.28s, settled in ~0.45s). A critically damped spring never crosses its target, so there is NO overshoot by construction, and the thumb is the segment's size throughout (no scale, no resize). The track is precomputed from the closed form (s = T + (a + (v + w a) t) e^(-w t)) at 120 samples a second and handed to Web Animations as a `transform` track, so it runs on the compositor through a busy main thread. A move that arrives while a spring is running carries that spring's position AND speed into the next.
- PRESS the thumb and it lifts up to 5% (scale about its middle, capped to what the track's own edge leaves room for: 3.5% on a 2-segment phone control, 5% on three), on its own faster spring (w = 28); let go and it settles back. A press on any other segment lifts nothing.
- DRAG follows the finger 1:1 from where the finger went DOWN (anchoring to where the drag was recognised left it 5-8px behind), clamped between the first and last segment, requestAnimationFrame only while a finger is down; let go and the thumb springs to the NEAREST segment carrying its release speed (clamped to what cannot overshoot) and that segment is picked then (`t.el.click()`, as a tap would), not live; a press elsewhere on the track and a drag runs the thumb to the finger (the offset decays with a 80ms constant). Native iOS 26 changes the value on release; if Madison wants the live tick as the thumb passes the half-way point it is one line (click at the crossing) and a haptic where iOS has one (none on the web).
- a tap on the PICKED segment does nothing (Profile's and the boards' handlers had re-run selectProfileTab / selectBoard - toTop, repaint - on a same-segment tap; they check now; the levels already did).
- two things in the app were fighting the thumb and were found by the gate, not by looking: (1) `setupBubbleButtons` (the global press dip) scaled a pressed `.iconbtn` to 97% with an inline transform and sprang it back past full size over .4s - under the thumb, and it made place() read a scaled box (a 3% wrong thumb size after a drag, the layout properties changing 23 times in a tap); segments are excluded from it, and the stylesheet's `.iconbtn:active{transform:scale(.96)}` is off for them. (2) the old CSS gave every iconbtn a `transition:transform .1s` that the press used; the segments' own transition is opacity alone.
- reduce motion: the thumb is placed, never animated, never lifts (pointerdown returns early). Keys: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move focus and pick (a tab list's), Enter / Space pick, focus-visible draws the white ring inside the segment. RTL-agnostic (the thumb is `left:0` + a translate in the control's own px; rects are divided by the control's own on-screen scale, so a scaled-in sheet and Safari's page zoom both read right).
- no filter, no backdrop-filter, nothing animates width / height / left / top / box-shadow: the thumb's box is sized once to its segment, its shadow is a still one, and the only animated properties are `transform` (the thumb) and `opacity` (the labels, and the thumb's own first fade-in).

## 384 r15 - bottom tab like butter (branch worktree-agent-a7d920c90d1aa8c8d, cut from build 384.12; no build bump here)

- REPORT: Madison, after his 384.11 recording of the bar on his iPhone 17 Pro Max (HEVC HDR, 20s, Home / Profile / Leaderboard / Settings hopped about twice a second): "Bottom tab is starting to feel really really good. I need this to be a smidge smoother. Like butter. It's nearly perfect but I'm wanting perfection. Ensure this smoothness is the same for ALL devices and all screen sizes, because I've seen how laggy it is on computers."
- WHAT THE RECORDING SAYS (ffmpeg: every frame's timestamp and a per-region diff; the file is variable-rate - a frame is written when the screen changed: 1,142 frames, 1,007 of them 16.7ms apart, 103 of them 25ms):
  - the screen change is ONE frame, a hard cut with no fade and no travel, 150-200ms after the press, under the glass (build 302's decision: "a screen simply appears where it belongs"; the .panel-enter animation is switched off for #stage's children). No half-drawn frame, no late frame at the cut. Not touched.
  - the glass is at 60 wherever Home is not involved: Profile, Leaderboard and Settings glides, and every hop from 13s to 18s (none through Home), drop 0-1 of ~20 frames.
  - EVERY stretch of dropped frames has Home in it. Home at rest (81 frames read mid-stay): 31% late (25ms gaps: the page draws at ~40, not 60), mean 19.2ms; Profile, Leaderboard and Settings at rest: 0%. Glides: Home -> Settings 4 of 20 frames late, Settings -> Home 2 / 4 / 7 of 18-22, Leaderboard -> Home 4 of 22, against 0-1 for the other three.
  - Home's hero is ~30 loops on the compositor (orbit rings, three masked smoke layers, the plasma, the glow's breath, the flares' sheens and cores - all transform or opacity), ~5.7x the viewport's area in drawing layers, ~10 backdrop-filter surfaces, and the bar's own blur over all of it. The glass gliding over it is drawn at that price. Nothing else in a tab change shows in the recording: no pop, no double step, no icon or label flicker.
- NOT FOUND, MEASURED (Chromium; its software compositor stands in for a GPU): nothing in a tab change scales with the SCREEN'S AREA. Home's hero is capped (554px at 1366x768, 768px from 1920x1080 up: the same hero on 1080p, 1440p and 4K); with the hero hidden the whole page draws in 1.9ms a frame at 3840x2160 (3.4ms with the page hidden too); and a tab change costs the main thread 0.6x as much on a 3840x2160 (62ms 1x-equivalent) or a 1920x1080 at 2x (59ms) as on a 1366x768 (102ms). What a computer pays for is Home's hero (~28ms of software draw a frame at every size, 1-2ms without it), not pixels. (The software renderer draws a backdrop filter's whole surface, so it overstates this on a GPU; it is printed as INFO, not asserted.)
- FOUND AND FIXED (index.html):
  1. A TAP HOLDS THE HEAVY ART STILL UNDER THE GLASS, as a slide has since 382. lensDown looks once a frame after the press, navRun once more a frame after the new screen is built (so Home arriving is held too), lensFinish gives it back; the same set as a slide (SLIDE_HOLD_SEL: Home's hero, Profile's card and goals, the board's rows) plus whatever loop is under the bar's band. Measured: before, 26-65 of those loops ran through the whole glide of every tap (29 on Home arriving); now none from the third frame under the glass, and Home's ~29 run again once it has landed (check-b384-tabbutter (1), 12 pairs, phone and iPad). Software compositor draw per frame in a tap's hop on the phone: 12.2ms on 384.12, 3.1-5.7ms now (median of 4-12 hops on a shared machine: the direction, not a number to quote).
  2. NO STYLE PASS PER LOOP. `syncLoopClock` read each loop's timing (getTiming, which updates the style the animation came from) straight after writing the previous loop's currentTime: one style pass per loop, 26-75 a Home tab change (traced: UpdateLayoutTree attributed to that callback by its stack; ~8ms at 1x, ~30ms at 4x). The Leaderboard's rows did the same per row coming into view (the IntersectionObserver callback read a row's padding after the last row's class change, then synced each flare on its own), and the hold's own look (`barUnderPause`: 66 passes in one look, a pause() then the next playState read) and its give-back (`play()` between two reads) did too - and a slide takes the same look. All are reads first, writes after: one pass, the same times, the same animations held.
  3. THE IDLE STAND-IN WAITS FOR A FINGER ON THE BAR AND THE GLASS IT LANDS WITH. Safari has no requestIdleCallback; the page's own runs one warm-up job at a time (badge art, sound synthesis, character sheets: 15-70ms each at 1x here), never within 700ms of the last touch - and "the last touch" was only a pointerdown / touchstart / key / wheel / scroll, never a move, so a finger that stays down on the bar (a slide, a long press) was 700ms old in the middle of the slide and a job ran under the lens (measured: a job asked for under a finger ran 533-1002ms later with the bar held). A job now waits, 250ms at a time, while html.tab-held is on (the press until the glass has landed). FIRST VERSION, REVERTED: it also waited for the settle window (settleUntil) - check-b384-swipe (2) then failed on 384.17 + this (Profile and Leaderboard top-tab swipes: "the next tab is lit within 450ms", 4 of 18 against 0 of 18 on 384.17 in the same hour, and 0 of 17 with the settle wait taken out): the settle window stretched the wait for the sound warm-up, so the first sound of a swipe found its noise and impulse samples not yet made and made them inside the swipe. A change to when warm-ups run needs that gate.
  4. A LENS TRACK NEVER GOES BACKWARDS (`lensOffsets`, four call sites: the bar's fades and swell, the top switchers' fades and swell). check-b384-swipe (7) threw "Failed to execute 'animate' on 'Element': Offsets must be monotonically non-decreasing" under load: a landing planned with its grey-over point before its clearing point (a glass that never shrank, a release long after the lift: greyAt 0 against a clearing at 1ms) made keyframe offsets 0, .02, 0, 1, inside lensRelease, before the timer that puts the glass away - a lens left up and a bar left swollen until the next press. Each offset is now at least the one before it. (Reproduced as a track, not as the load; 384.17 throws on the same track, it just takes a slow machine to plan one.)
- LOOKED AT, NOT CHANGED, ON PURPOSE: the cut (302), the lens, the glass, the 40ms wait for a finger's tap, page swiping between bottom tabs (removed on purpose; not back). A mouse click's build one frame later (rAF, then the timer), so that the click's answer is never behind the build: in Chromium the click already answers within a frame (median 9ms before and after - rAF runs ahead of a 0ms timer there) and the screen came 150ms+ later under load; reverted. hswFits shows ~20-30 style/layout "passes" per tab change in a trace: they are markers with no dirty work (0ms, 0 elements), not thrash. Not tried (a design or a risk): content-visibility on the below-the-fold cards of Profile and Settings (cuts the first style pass; changes layout containment), taking the flares' backdrop-filters off (a signed-off look), the 190 :has() rules (a Home mount invalidates html, body and #chatdock through them ~40 times; ~12ms at 1x), the class bubble's four place() reads (~11ms at 1x).
- MEASURED, 1x-equivalent main-thread CPU per tab change (median of the 12 ordered pairs of Home / Profile / Leaderboard / Calendar; worst task; the page's own frame clock and the software compositor's draw per frame are the shared sandbox's at load 25-60 and are INFO only): phone 440x956@3 69-129ms, worst 48-54; phone at 4x CPU 101ms, worst 109; iPad 834x1194@2 92ms, worst 58; 1366x768 102ms, worst 69; 1366x768 at 4x 104ms, worst 97; 1512x982@2 102ms, worst 101; 1920x1080 116ms, worst 76; 2560x1440 85ms, worst 83; 3840x2160 62ms, worst 68; 1920x1080@2 59ms, worst 66. Input handlers (pointerdown / up / click): 5-11ms on a finger, 5-6ms with a mouse, 13.5ms at 4x on the phone.
- GATE: tools/check-b384-tabbutter.py ([--quick] [--only DEVICES] [--checks 1,6] [--against REV|path]). (1) the hold (finger: phone, iPad; every pair; read off the page, in frames, on the glass seen), (2) no script function forces more than 8 style recalcs that restyled something, or 8 layouts of 50us+, in a tab change, (3) budgets in 1x-equivalent main-thread CPU (a finger: worst task 140ms, input handler 20ms, a tab change 600ms; a mouse: 140 / 14 / 600), (4) a tab change costs a 4K no more than 1.6x a 1366x768, (5) frames and no errors, (6) a warm-up job asked for under a finger waits for the lift and the landing, (7) a lens track planned out of order still animates.
