## 384 r24 - every Fire Code banner moves

Madison: "Some ifc banners issues: why barely any of them animate, and why do some of them not animate as you scroll through them?" (Customize > Banner in Fire Code: the 17 Fire Code banners and the three rank banners it shares.)

WHAT WAS TRUE (measured in Chromium, 440x956, every banner forced earned, 384.17). Every banner that is in view runs (never `.rk-idle` while visible, and the on-screen observers wake a tile before it arrives), so "some do not animate as you scroll through them" reduced to two things:
- THREE Fire Code banners were held completely still: Certified (tests100), Squared Away (hundos100), Mutual Aid (vr50). They were absent from `BANNER_ANIMATED`, which is the academy's "first rung of each ladder is still" rule (build 243), and `buildBannerArt` gave them `.is-still` (`animation:none !important` on the whole banner). Fire Code inherited a rule written for a different set of banners.
- The others ran a slow breathing glow or two and a sheet of dust sliding up over 18-24 seconds: Code Book 3 running animations, On Call 3, After Hours 3, Plan Review 3, Inspection Team 4, Clean Sweep 4 (against 9-19 on the busiest). Measured as pixels that change over 0.7s of a phone-width strip: On Call 0.04%, Inspection Team 0.3-0.4%, After Hours 0.4-1.0%, Plan Review 0.5-0.8%, Clean Sweep 0.5-0.6%; the three still ones 0.00%. A scale of a few percent and an opacity from .8 to 1 over five seconds is below what the eye picks up at tile size, which is what "barely any of them animate" and "some of them do not animate" both look like.

WHAT WAS DONE.
1. `IFC_BANNER_ANIMATED = ["tests100", "hundos100", "vr50"]`, read by `buildBannerArt` only when `IFC_ART_ON`. The academy keeps its still first rungs (check-b384-fcbanner-motion section 4 holds that: every academy banner outside `BANNER_ANIMATED` is `.is-still` with nothing running, and Certified, Squared Away and Mutual Aid among them).
2. EVERY Fire Code banner now has one continuous loop and one event or more IN ITS OWN SCENE, at least 8 running animations each (12-14 on most), all transform or opacity on a box (the compositor's; `getKeyframes()` is asserted). Helpers above `IFC_BANNER_ART`: `fcmGlow` (a flickering/popping light), `fcmSpark` (a four-point glint), `fcmPing` (a ring that goes out), `fcmLed` (an indicator lamp), `fcmGlint` (a band of light across a box, clipped to it), and new `bl-*` keyframes: `bl-led`, `bl-ping`, `bl-spark`, `bl-glintx`, `bl-flick`, `bl-swing` (a beam turning about its lens), `bl-flash` (lightning), `bl-pop`, `bl-away` (a light running to the vanishing point), `bl-sec` (a ticking second hand), `bl-fly`, and `bl-run0..4` (Mutual Aid's five units, each along its own route; the corners are the routes' vertices as shares of an 8-unit box, so if vr50's `routes` move, regenerate them).
   Certified: the banker's lamp flickers, a glint crosses the big certificate and the coin stand, seal/badge/coins/small seal sparkle in turn, the badge on its stand rings out. Squared Away: the lamp swings on its cord, the radio's lamp blinks and rings, steel glints run along the duty belt, the vest/wallet badges, flashlight lenses and cuffs sparkle. Mutual Aid: five units run from their stations to the incident, the incident rings out twice, the dispatchers' screens scan and their headset lamps blink. Code Book: a second faster rain with brighter drops, lightning over the city (one is already on its way as the banner appears), the lamp flickers, a second wisp off the mug, the moon glints. On Call: the display scans and flickers, a glare crosses the panel's glass, the AC POWER lamp rings out, the ceiling light flickers, dust drifts up, the pull station/box lock/key switch glint. After Hours: the beam sweeps and its lens flares, the gauges and handwheels catch it, the clock's second hand ticks, a light runs along the red main and the hazard tape. Plan Review: a glint across the plan, the reviewer's red lights tick by tick, rings from the revision cloud, a thump on REVIEWED, the lamp bulb flickers, the radio blinks and rings. Inspection Team: both torches sweep, both lenses flare and ring, the EXIT blinks and rings, a light crosses the floor. Clean Sweep: the ten tags light in a wave from the nearest door pair to the far one, the EXIT pulses and rings, two bands of light run down the floor to the exit. Top Floor: aviation lamps ring out, a light sweeps the glass, the crowns and the moon glint, the plane crosses in 22s (it was 46s) and a second one crosses lower. Fire Investigator: the beam sweeps, red and blue truck lights go round on the window behind him, a glint runs along the tape, the lens and the three evidence markers glint. Nebula: the gas flickers in waves and a shooting star crosses (one shooting star is already crossing as the banner appears). Comet: the nucleus flares and its existing fragment is now already on its way as the banner appears (its delay was -2s of 7.5s, so the first streak came 2.4s in). The four secret flares and the rangers stay under the sets check's 14 layers (check-b384-sets item 7: "3+ moving and at most 14 layers"): Nebula is 14 (12 + the gas and the shooting star), Comet 14 (13 + the nucleus's spark); a first draft with a layer for every spark and ring (21 and 16) failed it, and the budget was kept rather than raised - the pins in that gate are the layer budget the sets were built to.
3. NOTHING AT REST MOVED. Every added layer carries `opacity:0` inline (the keyframes set the opacity), so with motion off a banner is the picture it was and `bannerStaticSVG` (which the older banner checks hash) skips it: check-b384-fcbanners, -banners, -sets and -r9-banners pass unchanged. A layer that animates only a transform (`bl-cross`) cannot be hidden that way, so `bl-fly` and `bl-sec` carry `opacity:1` in their own keyframes.
4. EVERY NEW LAYER IS ALREADY MID-FLIGHT THE FRAME THE BANNER APPEARS: its clock is a negative `animation-delay` (`fcmT(dur, at)`, `at` seconds into its cycle), picked so something is in motion in each 0.7s window. A banner built `.rk-idle` and woken (`animation:none` off) restarts every animation at its start, so a layer that begins at zero, or waits out a positive delay, or whose event is the seventh second, is a banner that looks still for as long as that takes; the Fire Code banners before had no positive delays (their loops were small, not late), the academy's event layers use `ev` with a negative delay for the same reason.

THE SCROLL SYMPTOM (what could be measured; the rest is phone-only).
- NOT reproduced as such: through five scroll stops at 440x956, every drawn tile that is at least half in view had running animations, was not `.rk-idle` and not `.is-offscreen`, and every tile more than half a screen out ran nothing (`.rk-idle` beyond a screen and a tenth). The tiles are not rebuilt by a store save, a tap or a sync (the same DOM nodes were there afterwards).
- THE MECHANISM FOUND: a Customize banner tile has TWO observers. `.rk-idle` (`_rkIO`, margin a whole screen) stops a banner and a wake restarts it from its first frame; `.is-offscreen` (the tile's own observer in showCustomize, margin 120px) PAUSES it, and every tile is BORN paused until that observer's first callback. 120px is 60ms of runway at 2,000px a second, and an observer callback waits for the main thread, so one 65ms frame (the Leaderboard's, at 4x CPU, build 360) in a fling is a tile that arrives in view still. Its margin is a third of the screen now ("34% 0px": ~320px on a phone, ~400 on an iPad, ~160ms). A paused tile keeps the layers it has, so this does not touch the build 252 budget, which is `.rk-idle`'s and stays a screen out. Chromium cannot prove it: a headless frame here is ~1 second in a software renderer, so a callback is always inside one frame; check-b384-fcbanner-motion section 3 asserts the settled state (every in-view tile running and moving, far tiles idle) and cannot see a stall that only a phone's main thread has.
- WORTH KNOWING: every layered banner's motion sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference)`, so a phone with iOS Reduce Motion on shows NO banner moving at all, whatever this build does (and the app's own Reduce motion switch does the same). If he still sees stills on his phone, that setting is the first thing to look at.

RUNNING ANIMATIONS, BEFORE -> AFTER (a banner built in a 440-wide strip), and the share of the strip's pixels that change in the worst of three 0.7s windows (BEFORE -> AFTER): Certified 0 -> 12 (0.00% -> 1.55%), Plan Review 3 -> 12 (0.48% -> 3.2%), Inspection Team 4 -> 12 (0.34% -> 1.55%), Squared Away 0 -> 13 (0.00% -> 1.38%), Mutual Aid 0 -> 14 (0.00% -> 3.3%), Code Book 3 -> 8 (1.8% -> 3.4%), On Call 3 -> 15 (0.04% -> 1.8%), After Hours 3 -> 13 (0.38% -> 2.4%), Clean Sweep 4 -> 13 (0.50% -> 7.4%), Fire Investigator 6 -> 14 (0.69% -> 14%), Top Floor 7 -> 19 (1.35% -> 2.9%), Nebula 9 -> 11 (0.91% -> 2.1%), Comet 11 -> 12 (0.88% -> 1.33%). Not touched: Grand Finale 9, Downpour 9, Quasar 11, Whiteout 10, the three rank banners and the rangers. The layers per banner (the `.bnl` boxes) went 3-8 -> 12-21 on the changed ones, the flares staying at 14.
A TIME NOTE for whoever reads those numbers later: the machine this was built on ran at a load average of 40-60 (other sessions' browsers), so a headless frame took ~1s; every number above that depends on timing is therefore taken by SETTING the animations' time, not by waiting; the only waited-for numbers are the scroll section's, and those are "is it moving at all" (>= 1% of a tile's pixels over three frames 0.6s apart), not "how fast".
GATE: tools/check-b384-fcbanner-motion.py (see its docstring). Strips at phone (440) and tablet (834) width for every id in IFC_BANNER_ART: not `.is-still`, at least 6 running, only transform/opacity; and a pixel diff over three 0.7s windows (0.0-0.7s, 1.1-1.8s, 2.4-3.1s), taken by pausing every animation and SETTING its time rather than waiting for it (a screenshot is slow here, and what it should compare is the same picture on any machine), at least 1% of the strip's pixels changing in every window. Customize > Banner scrolled through; the academy unchanged. Fails on 9b0ee77 (tests100/hundos100/vr50 `.is-still`; nine banners under 6 running animations; eleven under 1% in some window: Certified, Plan Review, Inspection Team, Squared Away, Mutual Aid, On Call, Fire Investigator, After Hours, Clean Sweep, Nebula, Comet; and in the scroll section the still tiles neither run nor move). It also takes `--vp 518x1126` (the page-zoom case), `--vp 834x1194`, `--vp 1440x900`, `--cpu 4` and `--skip-strips` for the Customize section alone.
- A harness lesson: calling `pause()` or `play()` on a CSS animation makes the browser IGNORE the CSS's own `animation-play-state` for it from then on. The first version of the scroll section paused everything to take a deterministic picture, and every later stop then reported tiles "running" that the page had stopped (and tiles "paused" that it had started). The scroll section photographs the tiles as they run; the strip section seeks, on a page it throws away.
- NOT in the gate, on purpose: the compositor layer budget. The Leaderboard and the Virtual Room lobby draw these banners too (a row's banner is `.rk-idle` off screen and `content-visibility:hidden` with its row); a Fire Code banner is 8-19 `.bnl` layers now against 3-11, so a screen of rows is on the order of 150 animations, not 100. Tiny layers (sparks, pings, LEDs) are boxes a few dozen units across; the wide ones were cut to the region they cross (a wall-wide glint on Squared Away was dropped, Clean Sweep's corridor-wide tag glows are a box round each door pair, Inspection Team's floor glint is 280 units not 480). Still wide: the red main and the hazard tape on After Hours (480 by 9 and 6, thin), and Nebula's gas (one soft 380 x 136 glow, a layer the sets check allowed). If a phone drops paint on the Leaderboard again (build 252's symptom), this is the first suspect.

FILES: index.html (CSS classes and keyframes beside `.bl-slide` and `bl-shimmer`, `IFC_BANNER_ANIMATED`, helpers above `IFC_BANNER_ART`, the layers at the end of each scene's array, the Customize observer margin), tools/check-b384-fcbanner-motion.py, tools/shoot-fc-banners.py (`--frames 0.2,1.2,2.4` writes the banner at those seconds one under the other, paused and set to the time).
## 384 r17 - the launch handover (the splash's first frame, its word, and what the page can and cannot do about the frames before it)

Madison, a screen recording of opening the installed app from the Home Screen on his iPhone 17 Pro Max after an iOS update: "When opening the app, the splash screen glitches sometimes and it's not smooth. This is vital." Read off the recording (HEVC, 1320x2868, decoded at 20fps; the flat #0A0A0A startup image decodes to 24, so levels are compared, not read as sRGB):

- Frames 4-11 are the startup image (24). Then ONE whole-screen NEUTRAL grey ramp, 24 -> 36 -> 81 -> back to 25, two frames, the status-bar rows included. That is before the page's first frame (the next frame is the splash). Neutral (R=G=B at every pixel) and lighter than anything the page paints, so it is not ours: it is what the web view shows until the page has painted something. Nothing in the document can reach it; what the page can do is paint sooner (below).
- The splash's FIRST frame: its box ends 186px (62pt) above the bottom of the screen (rows 2682-2868 are another colour, 36 against the splash's 25) and what shows in that strip is the app's own glow and starfield (`body::before/::after`, fixed, which are not the splash's size). NOVA, the status line and the bar sit at the middle of that SHORT box (447pt of 956).
- One frame later the box is whole and the word is exactly 186px (62pt) higher, then does not move again. But it rests at 390pt, 88pt ABOVE the screen's middle (478pt). An earlier recording of the same splash (the 19:09 one) has the group at 433-533pt, the middle. So something the old code read as "the viewport" changed with the iOS update.
- The handover to Home at ~2.3s (the splash holds "ready." with a full bar, then cross-fades into Home) is clean in the recording: no flash, no jump. Left alone.

THE CAUSE OF THE GEOMETRY. `#splashscreen` was `position:fixed; inset:0; width:100vw; height:100lvh` and the group (its own fixed element) was set by JS to the middle of "the smallest size any viewport API reports" (innerHeight, documentElement.clientHeight, visualViewport.height; smallestCredible, from the first attempts at the iOS oversized-box launch). On this iOS one of those reports a height that is short of the screen by a different amount at each moment of a launch (62pt at the first frame, 176pt at rest), and a box 100lvh tall comes up 62pt short at the first frame. The old gates modelled the opposite lie (a visualViewport 1.6x too big for 250ms), which is why they were green.

WHAT WAS CHANGED
1. `#splashscreen` is OVERSIZED: left/top -300px, width calc(100vw + 600px), height calc(100lvh + 600px) (100vh first as the fallback), z-index 9999, #0A0A0A, overflow hidden. Whatever the first frame's box is, nothing but the splash shows round it. Its glow (`::before`) is inset:300px so the glow keeps the viewport's size and centre. A fixed box does not add to a document's scrollable overflow, so the oversize cannot make a page scroll or shrink-to-fit.
2. THE WORD IS SET BY THE SCREEN, NOT THE VIEWPORT. In an installed app (navigator.standalone / display-mode: standalone) a head script writes --splash-cx/--splash-cy on <html>: x = innerWidth/2, y = (screen height in CSS px)/2, where a CSS px is `innerWidth / screen width` points (the page's own scale: 1 at 100%, 518/440 at his 85%). screen.height is the device's own and does not move while a launch settles. It is used only when it is plausible (scale .6-1.8, innerHeight within .85-1.03 of the screen's height at that scale: a whole screen, short by at most a launch's transient - never an iPad window that is some of it). Anywhere else (a browser tab, a window) the old smallest-credible reading is used. `#splash-group` reads `left:var(--splash-cx,50%); top:var(--splash-cy,50%)`, in the first style block AND in the stylesheet, so the very first paint already has them.
3. NOTHING MOVES AFTER IT IS SHOWN. The group is opacity 0 until the readings (innerWidth/Height, clientWidth/Height, visualViewport, screen) have been the same for three frames and 100ms (or 30 frames, so a viewport that never settles still shows a splash); then `.splash-ready`; after that only a change of WIDTH (a turn, a page-zoom change) re-places it. The old `centred()` check (the group against the same number it was placed by) could only ever agree with itself and is gone.
4. THE SPLASH IS THE FIRST THING IN <body>, BEFORE THE 2.9MB STYLESHEET. The stylesheet (bytes 125,608-3,025,000 of a 10.3MB file) was in <head>, so nothing could be painted until it had all been read: that is the window in which the web view shows its own colour. The head is now the small scripts, metas and links (to ~126KB), then `</head><body>`, the splash's markup and its placement script, THEN the stylesheet (a <style> in <body>), then the splash's clock script. The launch's own first-frame rules (the oversized box, the group at opacity 0, the position variables) are in the document's FIRST <style> and are declared once (removed from the big sheet, which would have won the cascade). `data-theme/layout/accent` moved to the head with them so the first style pass of the stylesheet already wears the saved colour. In Chromium first-paint came at 0.2-0.5s against 0.5-1.2s (4x CPU throttle and without, on a machine at load 40-50, which is why these are ranges).
   - Anything that adds a <style> at run time now appends to <body> (`(document.body || document.head).appendChild`), after the stylesheet: later in the document wins a tie, and head styles would now come BEFORE it. 8 sites (the display test's, csw-tint-keys, rk-sheet-keyframes x2, lagtest-variant, board-test-look, drag-look). A gate or tool that appends a non-!important rule to <head> to override the app now loses ties.
5. Nothing rewrites the page under the splash: `resetStuckZoom()` (which rewrites the viewport meta) does nothing while the splash is up; an installed app's theme-color is not rewritten under the splash (finishSplash writes it as the fade starts); in a browser tab `refreshEdgeTints` no longer clears <html>'s inline #0A0A0A on the first applyTheme (it did, so the root was the app's colour for the whole splash, which is what Safari's bands show); 384.17's `#top-guard` (z-index 2147483000, a lighter band across the top) is made as the splash fades, not under it (and by a MutationObserver if the splash is taken out of the page without the fade).
6. apple-touch-startup-image: added the iPhone Air (420x912 @3x -> launch/1260x2736.png and 2736x1260.png); it had no exact entry and fell to the media-less catch-all. Now 22 devices, 45 link tags; 16e (390x844), 17 Pro (402x874) and 17 Pro Max (440x956) were already there; `--check` is clean. (Install-time: a device that installed before keeps what it had.)

GATE tools/check-b384-launchframe.py (written against main's index.html first; `--against` it FAILS on the short-viewport cases)
- the page runs in an <iframe> that the host grows from a short height to the final one at the moment the splash's group is inserted (a real viewport resize, in the first frame the splash has); screen.width/height fixed; an installed app (navigator.standalone + display-mode) and a browser tab; 100% and his 85% page zoom (518 css px on a 440pt screen); iPhone 17 Pro Max, SE, 16e, iPad Pro 11in portrait and landscape; the initial height short by the bottom inset, the top inset, both, and not at all; the growth immediately or 110ms later.
- every sample (animation frame and a 10ms timer: a launch blocks the main thread for seconds) is recorded from inside the page, and a screencast of the painted frames is read pixel by pixel.
- asserts: the splash's box covers the whole FINAL viewport in every sample (first sample at the short size); once the word is visible it is at the same x/y in every sample and at the middle of the screen (installed) or the viewport (tab); <html>'s computed AND inline background is #0A0A0A while the splash is up; no painted frame before the fade has more than 10% of its pixels lighter than luma 60 (the word is ~1%; a light flash is 100%); nothing writes the viewport meta; nothing rewrites theme-color before the fade (installed); the splash's markup precedes the stylesheet; no page errors.
- NOT reproducible in Chromium and not claimed: the grey ramp before the first frame (it is outside the page), iOS's real safe areas and timing, the real HEVC of a launch.

ONLY HIS PHONE CAN CONFIRM: (1) that the first frame is now flat dark edge to edge with nothing across the bottom and the word absent until it fades in already at its place; (2) whether the grey ramp before it shrinks or goes (it should, if the page paints before the 2.9MB stylesheet is read, but if WebKit waits for more than the document's first style and some content it will not - the next recording says); (3) that the word now rests at the middle of the screen on his phone (it was 88pt above it) - the number to look for is the group centred on row ~1434 of 2868; (4) that no band appears across the top while the splash is up (384.17's strip). If the word is wrong by a fixed number again, the readings to add to the head script are screen.width/height, innerWidth/innerHeight, visualViewport.width/height/offsetTop and documentElement.clientHeight at the page's first and last frame (a build that logs them to a toast or the display test would show them on the phone).

RESULTS (machine at load 40-65 on 4 cores the whole time, so every timing budget is load-bound; read as shape): check-b384-launchframe `--quick` (Pro Max 100% and 85% installed, iPad Pro 11in landscape installed, Pro Max tab) ALL PASS on this build; `--against` main's index.html FAILS the short-first-frame cases on COVER (the box is [0,0,440,922] in a 922-tall first frame: the strip), on STILL (the word moves 461 -> 478 and 430 -> 478 when the viewport grows), on theme-color rewritten under the splash, on the splash markup being AFTER the stylesheet, and in a tab on <html>'s background cleared mid-splash (rgb(28,28,31) in place of #0A0A0A). check-js, gen-startup-images --check (22 devices, 45 tags), check-b384-topguard, `sweep-layout --quick` (20/20 clean), check-b384-switchfx `ONLY=phone` (every picture check passes: 6b, 8, 8b, 8c; the timing budgets (1), (1c) fail on main as well at this load), check-behaviour `ONLY_FN=check_launch` ("never paints off-centre" passes; "settles centred and visible" reads 999px on main and here alike - at this load the splash is gone before the gate measures), check-b384-splashhide (the splash is gone before it measures, on main too), check-fixes (one fail per device, "tapping a done daily question showed no banner", on main too).
- check-b384-splashstage (5) "an ordinary launch: off at its own time (< 3.3s)" reads 3.85s here and 0.85s on main under load: on main the splash was not in the page until after the stylesheet, so the gate's sampler counted "no splash yet" as "off" and passed spuriously; with the splash in the page from the first bytes it measures the real clock (the stylesheet's parse + 2.5s), which is over its budget only on a loaded machine.


## 384.19 merge fixes (branch claude/b384-int-fix)

Five gates failed on the merged 384.19 (claude/b384-int) and passed on their own helper branches. Each was traced to its cause; three were the app, two were the gates. APP_BUILD and version.json are unchanged (still 384.19).

1. tabbutter check (2), "no script function forces more than 8 style recalcs or layouts in a tab change": the app. Three causes, found in order, each hiding the next.
   - `attachSegSlider()`'s `place()` called `seg.classList.add("has-seg-slider")` on every measure (the top-tabs rewrite, r18, dropped main's `styled` flag). `classList.add` of a class already present still rewrites the attribute, which the slider's own MutationObserver (attributeFilter: class) reads as the switcher changing, so every `place()` asked for the next one a frame later and went on for as long as the page was open: a style pass and a layout per switcher per frame (about 60-90 `place` passes per tab change on a phone with the chat dock's switcher and Profile's). It is now added only when absent. Counted with a copy of the page that logged each MutationObserver record (the old value equalled the new one).
   - `hswFlush()`'s last read (`hswFits`, the check that a switch or label fits its control) and `backToTopRoom()` (the last 40 tappables' rects) both read sizes INSIDE rankings rows the page has skipped (`.screen-rankings .rank-row.is-offscreen`, content-visibility:hidden). Chromium opens the row's display lock for the read and shuts it again ("DisplayLock" in the invalidation trace), so each row costs a style pass and a layout: 31 and 16 on the Leaderboard's first hop. Neither is new in this merge (origin/main and the tabbutter helper's tip both have `hswFits` at 31 on a phone; the gate only fails on whichever is largest, which was `place`). Both now leave a skipped row alone: the fit check does not ask it (a row on screen is read and fits), and the back-to-top measure reads the row itself (its own box is free) and not the controls inside it.
   - Where things land is unchanged: no read that fed a position changed its answer, and the back-to-top room is the same because a row is at least as low and wide as anything in it.
2. segdelta and toptabs, "<device>|ifc|boards: the switcher is on screen with 2+ segments -> None": the gate was stale. Since 384.12 (dbf516a) Fire Code's Leaderboard is Overall alone ("Remove the hundo leaderboard in fire code"), `rankingBoardsFor()` gives one board, and `showRankings()` draws no switcher for one board (`boards.length > 1`). That is by design and in origin/main. `tools/b384_seg_lib.py` listed the boards switcher for both classes; it is the academy's alone now.
3. classleave:
   - "lists rejoin the academy: the cloud lists both": the gate raced the app. Joining the academy from Fire Code is recorded by the academy's page as it opens (`setEnrolled`), and the account's write follows that page's first read of the cloud's copy: about 0.6s after Home is up, which is exactly where the gate's 600ms settle ended (3.6s vs 3.64s measured; the helper's own tip is as close, 3.8 vs 3.82). The gate now reads the cloud until it has both classes (up to 10s). The app's write was never missing: 2s later the cloud has ['academy','ifc'] and the join dated after the leave.
   - "no layout shift is seen once the cover lifts" (and a2hsbar (8), below): all the shifts are IMGs inside `.rk-frame`, a recorded loop's sprite sheet. Since build 380 a loop is a sheet stepped by left/top inside an overflow:hidden window (html.loops-paint); Chromium 1243 reports each step as a shift of that IMG while an ancestor is moving on the compositor (the flares' float, the hero's ease). Not width/height: nothing is unreserved or late. Proof: origin/main's Home alone, 2.5s after boot, 124 IMG shifts, 0.043; the same page with `.rk-frame img{animation:none}` 0; the leave helper's own tip reads 0.036 over 97 shifts under its own gate. No CSS containment or will-change variant tried (contain:paint, contain:strict, overflow:clip, position:absolute, will-change:left/top, translateZ) removed them, and the loops' paint mode is a deliberate memory decision (158MB of layers on a Leaderboard), so the app is untouched. `b384_leave_lib.py`'s witness names those sources `LOOP` and `summarise()` counts them on their own (`shift_loops`) and not in `shift_seen`; every other shift still counts.
4. a2hsbar (8), "no layout shift from the moment the bar shows": the same loops (the hero eases by translate and scale for .45s as the bar arrives, and the loop IMGs step under it); the gate's PERF observer names them `LOOP` and the check leaves them out. The planet's own box still must not shift. This gate fails on the a2hs helper's own tip (3a5f360) in this sandbox too.
5. qslide, (1) "the input's task is short": not changed and not a regression. origin/main's index.html fails the same checks in the same band when run here: laptop click 72.1 and 54.2, phone tap 59.0 and 69.8, phone swipe 64.5 and 74.8 (limits 56 / 66 / 52); this build 60.6 and 79.0, 66.3 and 80.2, 61.8 and 62.0, with eight-sample medians that swing 54-80 run to run (single tasks 33-150ms). A load-bound budget; a quiet phone-sized machine is needed to read it.

Not fixed: tabbutter check (2) on the 2560x1440 and 3840x2160 desktops of the FULL run (not `--quick`, which is a phone, 1366x768 and 1920x1080 at 2x) fails on `charFlipAttach` (10 and 12 forced passes on the Leaderboard's first hop; one per character tile, each tile's own timer reading its size after the last one wrote its sheet in). It is not this merge: the tabbutter helper's own tip and origin/main read 12 there too. Batching those reads is a change to the recorded-sheet attach path (builds 308-375) and was left alone.

Gate results (this machine, load about 1.5): tabbutter `--quick` ALL PASS (was: `place` 33-66 per tab change, then `hswFits` 31, then `backToTopRoom` 16, in that order); the full run passes every device except the two desktops above; segdelta `--quick` and `--quick --class ifc` 0 failed; toptabs `--quick` 0 failed; classleave ALL PASS; a2hsbar ALL PASS; qslide fails as on main. check-b384-haptics: the same two Calendar failures as before these changes, plus a Safari-tab Home one that comes and goes between runs.

## 384.18.1 - no weekly Nova pop-up in Fire Code

Madison: "Why did nova pop up for a weekly thing in the fire code class? Remove that."

What it was: Nova's Tuesday-to-Sunday "weekly recap" (`maybeShowWeekRecap`). Fire Code has no weekly board, so since build 383 it was given a
stripped-down personal version (`buildWeekRecapOptedOut`: your own points, tests and hundos for last week) and still stopped a person once a
week on Home or the Leaderboard. A second weekly thing was also allowed there: Nova's weekly challenge message (`novaPending(...).weekly`).

Now, in the Fire Code class (`window.NOVA_CLASS === "ifc"`):
- `maybeShowWeekRecap` returns first thing, marks nothing seen, so the account's `@recap` record is untouched;
- `novaRecapOwedToday` is false, so a recap that will never play no longer holds Nova's other messages back on a Tuesday;
- `novaPending` leaves `weekly` null: no challenge message.
The academy is untouched (its recap and weekly challenge still run). Nothing stored changes, so an account in both classes is unaffected.

Gate: `tools/check-b384-ifcweekly.py` (a Wednesday, both classes; Fire Code: no `.nova-talk`, no seen mark, no recap owed on a Tuesday, no
challenge in any of twelve weeks; academy: both still there). It fails on 384.19 (the recap plays, 3 checks). `check-b383-classes` (5) used to
assert the Fire Code recap plays; it now asserts it does not, and still asserts the academy's.

## 384.19.1 - the pearl, and a stray merge marker

Madison, shown the three unlit secret flares (ember A, socket B, pearl C): "For the secret flares, I like the pearl look." The unlit flare is now the pearl (option C of "384 r15 - unlit secret flares"): frosted pale glass over a dark core, a bright thin rim, a glint high on the left, a veiled light drifting inside it (`cof-ul-drift`, opacity + transform only), the existing slow sheen, NO ring (`.cof-ring` is `display:none`; the part stays in the DOM so the four-part markup is unchanged). Same one look in every place (Home's orbit, Welcome's planet, recap dots, hint card, locked secret character's mark). Colourless, no filter, reduced motion leaves the core as a still dim light. `check-b384-unlitflares.py` follows: "a pearl has no ring" (display none, nothing running) replaces "a ring opens and goes", and the pixel check asks for a frosted body clearly lighter than the panel inside a brighter thin edge (it fails on 384.19: the ring check, the dark body).
- A STRAY `=======` LINE in index.html's stylesheet (left by the 384.19 merge, between the unlit-flare block and the Settings "Account name" block). In CSS a stray line before a rule becomes part of that rule's selector, so the browser dropped that one rule: the Account row lost its `min-height:54px; padding-right:12px` (51px high instead). Nothing else was affected, and no gate saw it. `tools/check-js.py` now fails on any line that is only `<<<<<<<`, `=======` or `>>>>>>>` (it fails on 384.19's index.html, line 39471, and passes on this build).
- Gates: check-js, check-b384-unlitflares (ALL PASS; fails on 384.19), sweep-layout --quick, check-centering --quick (the sign-up "Coming soon" offset is on main too).

### 384 r20 - the mode screens fill their screens
Madison, on Choose your mode (Fire Code's three) and the Virtual Room's Host / Join, from his iPhone 17 Pro Max at ~85% page zoom (518x1126 CSS px on a 440x956 screen): "There's so much open space on these screens, it doesn't look like that. In the academy there's a 4th mode in mode selection so it looks better, however, on the phone not so much.. should we do them as a different looking boxes? Almost like the boxes you see when signing up for a class? Idk? Fix it though.. each device size may need a different layout and that's okay." (Branch worktree-agent-a0cbcdbc42a392ec0, cut from main 4bb08b1; NOT on main.)
- WHAT WAS WRONG. The cards were the same flat 160px rows at every size, centred (build 384) in a screen three times their height: ~300pt dead above and below on his phone (Fire Code three), and two rows parked at the top of Host / Join with the lower 60% empty (r9 had moved them up from the centre). Centring and parking both leave the room; the fix is to use it.
- THE DESIGN. The title bar and the question stay at the top (the 18px under the question stays). The cards are TILES that take the room under it down to the tab bar (18px above the bar, the same as under the question): the app's own solid card (the units card's - one colour for every card, no rim, no gradient, no shadow: check-b383-look (2) holds that, and a first version with a 12% tint wash and a tinted rim failed it, so the mode's colour lives only in the MEDALLION - a gradient disc and an inset rim in its colour, no filter, no blur - and the chevron disc: `--mc`, Drill red, Mock orange, Review green, Virtual Room blue, Host violet, Join green), a medallion top-left, a chevron disc top-right, the name and the line at the foot. A hover (pointer devices) raises the rim to the mode's colour, `:focus-visible` is a 2px outline in it. No radial gradient anywhere on the panel (check-b384-modes (7): "a glow that moves with the scroll" was reported once). The markup is the card it always was: `.modecardtitlerow` is `display:contents`, so the mark, the name and the line are the tile's own grid items; every class, `data-mode`, `.vrc-card-host/-browse` and tour target is unchanged and `check-tours` passes untouched.
- THE LAYOUT IS DECIDED BY `fillModeGroup(panel)` (one function for both screens; it replaces `centerModeGroup`). It measures, in GLASS px (CSS px divided by `--zc`, so the owner's page zoom gets the layout and sizes a 440pt screen has): the room between the question and the tab bar (the bar's own `getBoundingClientRect().top` - its `offsetTop` is wrong on a wide screen - against the cards' layout position minus scroll, since the screen comes in on a transform), the width, the count. Then: ONE column below 640 glass px; TWO columns from 640 (an odd tile spans both: Fire Code's Virtual Room is a wide tile on a tablet held upright); ONE ROW (3 or 4 across, 2 for Host / Join) where the screen is wide and not tall (>= 900 and wider than 1.1 x its height: a landscape tablet, a laptop, a desktop). It sets `--ms-cols/--ms-tile/--ms-room/--ms-gap/--ms-w` and `data-build/data-cols/data-tall` on `.modecards`; the CSS grid (`grid-auto-rows:minmax(var(--ms-tile), auto)`, `align-content:center`) does the rest, so a group that is capped or short is centred in its room and one that cannot fit simply scrolls.
  - Tile heights: they share the room equally on a phone (capped at 17rem, 17rem + 40px for the two of Host / Join), 28rem on a tablet's two rows, 40rem for one row of two, 30rem in a wide row (a desktop's tile is not a poster; the group is then centred, ~57% of a 1080px desktop's room).
  - `data-build="stack"` (the medallion above the words, the words at the foot) or `"snug"` (a phone with three or four tiles: the medallion 38px beside the name, the line across the foot; chosen when a tile would be under 176 glass px). `data-tall` 1 / 2 (tile >= 250 / 380 glass px) steps the medallion to 64 / 88px; the type is 22px / 15px on every phone tile (so Choose your mode and Host / Join read as one family), 24 / 16px on a tile in a multi-column group, 28 / 17px on a tall one of those. The layout attribute is `data-build`, NOT `data-tile`: check-b384-rowtiles reads every `#stage [data-tile]` as a Settings row tile, and a container carrying it was measured as one. Side by side, every line is made as tall as the longest in the group (`--ms-dh`) so the names sit on one line along the foot of a row.
  - A wide row is wider than the 50rem panel it sits in: `--ms-w` is the row's own width (px) and the left margin `(100% - w) / 2` breaks it out, centred; `.panel.modeselect` is `overflow:visible` for it.
  - The wrap reserves 7.5rem under the screen for the tab bar; on a phone with no home indicator (SE) that is ~41px more than the bar takes, and a group that fits would still scroll by that. The panel takes the overshoot back with a negative `margin-bottom`, only when the group fits.
  - The floor follows the tab bar: it is re-measured on resize, on the bar's own ResizeObserver / MutationObserver, on its `transitionend` / `animationend`, and at 450ms and 1100ms (the first screen after a launch, and the screen after a cutscene, have the bar still sliding in; a slow phone has it unfinished at 450ms - seen as a flaky check-b384-modes on a loaded machine).
- Sizes are `calc(N * var(--u))` with `--u: calc(1px * var(--zc, 1))`, so at the owner's zoom (1.18) a tile is drawn on the glass at the size it has on a 440pt screen; check (7) of the new gate asserts the name is 18.9pt at 100% and at his zoom within 1pt (the old build draws 16.0pt there).
- The iPhone's switch under a mode card's head (`.modecard > .nova-hsw`, 62% x 64px) is `96 * --u` tall on a stack tile, so it still covers the medallion where a finger picks a mode; the label (`.nova-hlb`) covers the rest, as before. Neither is a grid item (both are absolute).
- Press / focus: `:active` keeps a 12% ink wash and the 0.98 scale (transform only); reduce-motion: nothing here animates (the screen's own slide is the stage's). The DOM order is the focus order.
- DECISIONS THIS REVERSES, ON REQUEST: build 384's centring of the group (gate 1 of check-b384-modes now reads "fills the room, 18px above and below"), 343's "still BIG" 160px floor and 154px academy tiles (check-b342 still holds 150px+ on a phone; the tablet's third Fire Code card may now span both columns), r9's "cards 18px under the line, side by side from 40rem" (still 18px under the line; the row is now side by side from 640 glass px AND stretches), r8's reverted "bigger boxes". The two options shown for the phone: A, tall tiles with the medallion on top (chosen), B, big rows with the medallion at the left (the words wrap to four lines in 60% of the width and the tile stays half empty); /tmp/.../r20-modes/contact-sheet-phone-options.png.
- Gate: `tools/check-b384-modelayout.py` (+ `tools/b384_modelayout_lib.py`, the shared page boot; `--dump` prints the numbers). Both classes x Choose your mode (3 / 4) and Host / Join (2) x seven screens (SE 375x667, Pro Max 440x956, Pro Max at 85% zoom 518x1126 on a 440x956 screen, iPad Pro 11" upright and on its side, 1366x768 laptop, 1920x1080 desktop) = 267 checks: fill (>= 85% of the free height on a phone / upright tablet, >= 55% for the two tall tablet tiles, >= 50% wide; never more than 100% - a small phone that cannot fit scrolls and the last tile then clears the bar), centred (above and below within 3px), tiles in a row share a top and height, one width, >= 44px, words inside, no fixed control over a tile, no sideways scroll, the build's edges (stack: mark / name / line share a left edge; snug: mark and name centred on one line), five hit points per tile hit that tile, a real tap on each Choose your mode tile sets its mode and leaves the screen, page-zoomed set only at 518, the zoom size, no page errors. Against main's index.html on SE / Pro Max / zoom it FAILs 18 checks: Fire Code three-mode (fill 73% and 58%, off-centre) and Host / Join (48% / 38% / 70%) and the zoomed name size.
- Gates re-read because they encoded the old decisions: check-b384-modes (below the cards measured to the bar, not 16px above it; iPad above >= 12), check-b342 (the tablet's third card centred, one column wide or across both). check-b384-vrcenter passes unchanged (cards still 18px under the line).
- AUDIT of the other screens reachable from Home / Start (Pro Max 440x956, both classes; tools in the build message's scratchpad, screenshots r20-modes/audit-*): Choose your mode and Host / Join are the only screens that are a stack of option cards, and both are fixed. Checked and left: the units pickers (Setup, Review's, Virtual Room's Match settings: long lists, excluded by the brief; Match settings is 2,300px+ tall), Open rooms (`showRoomBrowser`: a title, a line, "Looking for open rooms..." and Refresh with the lower 60% empty while there are no rooms - an EMPTY STATE, not a stack of choices, so not redesigned; worth a decision from Madison, since in a class of ~40 "no rooms" is the usual state), Test history (an empty-state note until a run is saved; a list after), the Leaderboard with one row (a list). The Review chooser (a list or flashcards) is a switch inside the Start sheet, not a screen. The sign-up class cards are the reference and were not touched.
- NOT confirmable in Chromium: how the tiles read next to the real Dynamic Island / home indicator (the safe areas are modelled), a real finger on the iPhone's head switch over the medallion (the invisible switch is where it was, taller), Safari's page zoom at the owner's exact setting (emulated by a 518 viewport on a 440 screen), a slow phone's tab bar settling (covered by four re-measures, not by a real device).
- GATES, one at a time, on this tree (merged with origin/main 384.17): check-js ALL PASS; check-b384-modelayout 268 PASS (--against main's index.html on SE / Pro Max / zoom: 18 FAIL); check-b384-modes, check-b342, check-b384-vroomlook, check-b384-vrcenter, check-b384-rowtiles, check-tours --only modeselect, check-b383-modeselect, check-b384-vrifc (one load-flaky banner check, then ALL PASS), -mouse, -popfrost, -navchat, -vroom-review, -glitches, -walk, sweep-layout --quick (20/20), check-positions, check-fixes --only "Pro Max" all pass. FAIL, identically on main (compared with --against): check-b383-look (3) x3 (back button / switch / chat button glass), check-b384-haptics Calendar x2, check-behaviour sections check_b245_modes / check_b283 / check_b323u_units (5 failures: the units' boxes and Penal Code row, and the 2-beat copy rule that the third sentence of 384 broke), check-positions' notes (an SE 1st gen and a Home gap on an iPad), check-centering --quick (a leaderboard row 1px in one run, clean on the next: 944 elements, 0 off centre). check-b384-vroomlook now asserts one family (material, face, type within 2px) instead of equal padding.
